## Notes

Context recorded with verified facts.

### npm

- `cooldown.configFiles`: Any npm config layer works: project .npmrc (read only at the project root and not for global installs), \~/.npmrc, the global npmrc, npm_config_min_release_age or the CLI. package.json cannot set it. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/configuring-npm/npmrc)
- `cooldown.unit`: Type is null or Number; 0 turns the delay off. Fractional days are not documented. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#min-release-age)
- `cooldown.default`: Unchanged in npm 12. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#min-release-age)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: npm audit fix keeps the vulnerable version, warns that the fix was blocked (since 11.18.0) and exits non-zero. Add the package to min-release-age-exclude or relax the delay. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#min-release-age)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: strict-allow-scripts (default false) turns a dependency script that allowScripts does not cover "from a warning into a hard error ... instead of running with a notice", so from 11.16.0 such scripts still run. npm 11.21.1 ran esbuild's postinstall on 2026-10-29 ("has install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts"); npm 12.2.1 blocked it ("had install scripts blocked"). The v11 install-scripts command page says scripts are blocked by default, which the config definition, the 11.16.0 pull request, the GitHub changelog and the test contradict. npm 12 also blocks implicit node-gyp builds and prepare scripts of git, file and link dependencies. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.16.0/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: Only the root package.json counts; allowScripts in dependencies is ignored. npx, npm exec and global installs use the allow-scripts config instead. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/commands/npm-install-scripts)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Default false. Overrides allowScripts and dangerously-allow-all-scripts. npm run/test/start still run the named script, but not its pre/post scripts. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#ignore-scripts)
- `sources.git.values`: root allows only git dependencies listed in the project package.json. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-git)
- `sources.remoteTarball.values`: Tarballs on the configured registry hostname are always allowed. The 2026-05-22 GitHub changelog mentions only all and none; the config reference also lists root. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-remote)
- `sources.file.values`: The 2026-05-22 GitHub changelog mentions only all and none; the config reference also lists root. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-file)
- `sources.file.default`: npm 12 did not change the default. [↗](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-09-upcoming-breaking-changes-for-npm-v12/)
- `sources.directory.values`: The 2026-05-22 GitHub changelog mentions only all and none; the config reference also lists root. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-directory)
- `sources.directory.default`: npm 12 did not change the default. [↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/config#allow-directory)
- `project.lockfiles`: npm 11 and earlier prefer npm-shrinkwrap.json over package-lock.json when both exist; npm 12 no longer reads or writes npm-shrinkwrap.json (same format, rename it). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-lock-json.md)
- `project.workspaces`: An array of folder paths or globs. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md#workspaces)
- `user.files`: userconfig defaults to \~/.npmrc ("The location of user-level configuration settings. This may be overridden by the npm_config_userconfig environment variable or the --userconfig command line option"); \~ is resolved against \`this.env.HOME || homedir()\`. Same in 11.21.1. The project .npmrc is loaded first and may set userconfig= itself. Only the keys above the first [section] header are settings (extra.npmrcFormat). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/index.js)
- `user.settings`: Every config definition is read from any config file; only prefix is refused in a project .npmrc. allowScripts in package.json is project-only: at user level the allow-list is the allow-scripts key (allow only, every name becomes true; resolve-allow-scripts.js), used where the root package.json has no allowScripts and for npx, npm exec and npm install -g. The source keys use the later of the disputed first versions. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definition.js)
- `user.unknownKeys`: Unknown .npmrc (file) configs warn by default, matching pre-npm-12 behavior, but error when strict-npmrc is set. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/base-cmd.js)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: A value of the wrong type is reported as invalid config and the default is used. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/index.js)
- `user.weakening`: A key in the project .npmrc replaces the user value, lists included (prototype chain, no merging); the CLI and npm_config\_\* variables beat both. dangerously-allow-all-scripts is on for every value but false, null and undefined: npm reads .npmrc values and npm_config\_\* variables with parseField (https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.21.1/workspaces/config/lib/parse-field.js), which trims them, turns an empty value of a Boolean setting into true and only "true", "false", "null" and "undefined" into their values, and leaves 0, 1, yes or no as strings; load() does not run the nopt type check (validate() runs only in npm config), and arborist tests the flat option for truth (!this.options.dangerouslyAllowAllScripts in workspaces/arborist/lib/arborist/rebuild.js at 11.21.1). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `user.variables`: Environment variables starting with npm_config\_ are interpreted as configuration parameters; config values are case-insensitive, so NPM_CONFIG_FOO=bar works the same. loadEnv in workspaces/config/lib/index.js (11.21.1 and 12.2.1) skips variables whose value is empty and reads them in the order of the environment, so of two spellings the later one wins. userconfig defaults to \~/.npmrc (definitions.js), and npm exports the resolved path as npm_config_userconfig to every command it runs (see extra.childEnvironment), so that value names the default file. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md)
- `extra.environmentNames`: loadEnv takes every variable whose name matches /^npm_config\_/i, cuts the prefix and lowercases the rest (with \_ as - but for a leading \_), so NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY and Npm_Config_Registry set registry as npm_config_registry does (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/index.js)
- `extra.localPrefix`: loadLocalPrefix: --prefix on the command line is the local prefix. Otherwise npm walks up from the current directory (walk-up-path yields the directory and each parent up to the root, with no other stop; "for (const p of walkUp(this.cwd))") and takes the first directory with a package.json file or a node_modules directory ("hasPackageJson || await dirExists(p, 'node_modules')"). Unless workspaces are set to false on the command line ("this.#get('workspaces', 'cli')", so --no-workspaces or --workspaces=false; .npmrc and npm_config_workspaces do not count) or npm runs in global mode, it walks on: each higher directory with a package.json is read with @npmcli/package-json normalize, and one that cannot be read or normalized (".catch(() => ({ content: {} }))") or has no workspaces is passed over; the first whose mapped workspaces include that directory ("w === this.localPrefix", the same path) becomes the prefix, and a .npmrc of the workspace is skipped ("ignoring workspace config at ${this.localPrefix}/.npmrc"). Without a match the prefix is the current directory ("this.localPrefix = this.cwd"). loadProjectConfig reads "resolve(this.localPrefix, '.npmrc')" as the project configuration, except in global mode and when that path is the userconfig file. Workspaces (@npmcli/map-workspaces 6.0.0, the version npm 12.2.1 locks, with glob 13.0.6 and minimatch 10.2.5, https://github.com/npm/map-workspaces/blob/v6.0.0/lib/index.js): an array of patterns or an object with a packages array, else EWORKSPACESCONFIG, and an entry that is not text throws too; the leading ! are removed and an odd number of them negates, then a leading ./ or leading slashes ("pattern.replace(/^\\.?\\/+/, '')"); a pattern drops the earlier negated patterns it matches as text, and each negated pattern drops the patterns it matches as text and is given to glob as ignore, with \*\*/node_modules/\*\*; glob gets every pattern with a trailing / (directories only) and its defaults: \* and \*\* do not match a name that starts with a dot, \*\* does not follow symlinked directories, and matching ignores case on macOS and Windows; a match without package.json (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) is no workspace, another error and two workspaces of one name throw, and npm stops. normalize (https://github.com/npm/package-json/blob/v8.0.0/lib/normalize.js, steps bin and binDir) throws for a bin list with an entry that is not text and for directories.bin that is not text when bin is not set. No .git or home directory stops the walk. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/index.js)
- `extra.childEnvironment`: setEnvs gives the scripts and commands npm runs (npm run, npx, npm exec) every setting that is not its default as npm_config\_\<key> in lower case with - as \_, whichever file or flag set it, unless the definition has envExport: false (allow-scripts, min-release-age and min-release-age-exclude in 11.21.1 and 12.2.1); keys npm does not know, such as pnpm keys in .npmrc, are exported too. userconfig is always exported, because its default is the literal \~/.npmrc and the value the resolved path. It also sets npm_execpath to the npm it runs. The same in 10.9.4 and 12.2.1 (12.x and 11.x also export npm_config_node_gyp and npm_config_npm_version). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.21.1/workspaces/config/lib/set-envs.js)
- `extra.denyList`: A false entry in the root package.json allowScripts is an explicit denial: deny wins over allow, and denied packages are skipped silently, also under strict-allow-scripts ("const verdict = isScriptAllowed(node, policy); if (verdict === true || verdict === false) { continue }", the same in 11.16.0 check-allow-scripts.js). npm install-scripts deny writes a name-only false entry. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/arborist/lib/unreviewed-scripts.js)
- `extra.trustedPublishing`: Publishing from GitHub-hosted runners with OIDC instead of a token. Provenance is generated automatically, only for a public package from a public repository. A new trusted publisher configuration expires unless its first publish succeeds within 2 days. It can be limited to npm stage publish (the default for configurations created after 2026-09-03). [↗](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/packages-and-modules/securing-your-code/trusted-publishers.mdx)
- `extra.stagedPublishing`: Staging needs no 2FA, so CI can do it; approving or rejecting needs 2FA (CLI or npmjs.com). Staging a package that does not exist yet creates it with the public placeholder version 0.0.0-stage. Pre-release versions need an explicit --tag. --provenance also applies to npm stage publish. Rejecting the only staged version of such a new package also unpublished the placeholder (observed 2026-10-29 with npm 11.21.1), and after a whole package is unpublished its name is blocked for 24 hours (https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/main/content/policies/unpublish.mdx). [↗](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/cli/v12/commands/npm-stage.mdx)
- `extra.trustCommand`: Configures a trusted publisher from the CLI; needs 2FA on the account and write access, and the package must already exist. At least one permission flag is required. [↗](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/cli/v12/commands/npm-trust.mdx)
- `extra.tarballIdentity`: What npm installs for an entry of package-lock.json is the tarball of resolved (after replace-registry-host), whatever its version field says: #extractOrLink in workspaces/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js extracts \<name>@\<resolved> when resolved is set, and \<name>@\<version> only without it (12.2.1; the same code in 10.9.9). The allowScripts matcher of npm 12.2.1 takes the name and version of a registry package from resolved with this function (getTrustedRegistryIdentity in workspaces/arborist/lib/script-allowed.js: "Never use node.packageName / node.version here: those read from the tarball's own package.json and can be forged"): the path part after the last /-/ must be the file name of the URL, the part before it ends with the name, with the scope before it when that starts with @ (separated by / or %2f), and the file name is \<name>-\<version>.tgz with a version that semver.parse reads (semver 7.8.5 in npm 12.2.1: three numbers without leading zeros, an optional pre-release and build, an optional leading v, at most 256 characters; the version drops the v and the build). A path in another layout gives no name and version. versionFromTgz reads the whole URL, so a query or a fragment after the file name (.tgz?x=1, .tgz#x) gives none either, while npm still fetches the tarball: pacote 22.0.0 (the version npm 12.2.1 locks) fetches resolved as it is, or, when replace-registry-host replaces its host, new URL(path, registry) without query or fragment (lib/remote.js), and minipass-fetch 6.0.0 requests pathname and search, never the fragment (lib/request.js). The registry serves the file the path names, with its percent-escapes decoded as an HTTP server reads a path (decision D-136). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/arborist/lib/version-from-tgz.js)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Entries under packages: resolved is the registry tarball URL, the git URL with its commit (git+ssh://… or git+https://…#sha), file:\<path> for local tarballs and directories, or the link target when link is true. hasInstallScript marks a preinstall, install or postinstall script (prepare scripts of non-registry sources are not flagged). npm tells registry tarballs from other URLs with the registryTarball pattern (workspaces/arborist/lib/install-scripts.js), so a tarball URL on a registry host looks like a registry package. An entry without resolved is installed as \<name>@\<version> (workspaces/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js, #extractOrLink, in 11.19.1 and 12.2.1), so its version field is the source then. Entries keep the dependency fields of their package.json: dependencies, optionalDependencies and peerDependencies for every package, devDependencies for the root (workspaces/arborist/lib/shrinkwrap.js, pkgMetaKeys and the isTop branch, in 11.21.1 and 12.2.1); a dependency declared there as a URL comes from that URL even when it is a registry tarball. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-lock-json.md)
- `extra.overrides`: Only the root package.json counts. Keys are package names, optionally with a version or range (name@range), and nest to any depth to scope an override under a parent; "." inside a nested object overrides the parent package itself; values take any dependency specifier, including tarball URLs, and $name refers to the spec of a direct dependency. Overrides are not written to package-lock.json (checked with npm 11.21.1), so a URL override of a registry tarball looks like a registry package there. With replace-registry-host at its default npmjs, npm writes the configured registry in place of registry.npmjs.org in resolved URLs (workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.21.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md#overrides)
- `extra.npmrcScope`: Only the .npmrc at the root of the project npm runs in is read. Inside a workspace package npm moves the prefix to the workspace root (using-npm/workspaces.md) and warns "ignoring workspace config" for the package .npmrc (workspaces/config/lib/index.js). The project .npmrc "is not read in global mode, such as when running npm install -g" (same page, v11.21.1 and v12.2.1). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/npmrc.md)
- `extra.npmrcFormat`: npm reads .npmrc with the ini package: 7.0.0 in npm 12.2.1, and 6.0.0, whose lib/ini.js is the same, in npm 11.10.0 to 11.21.1 (package-lock.json of npm/cli). A line whose first non-blank character is # or ; is a comment. An unquoted key or value ends at the first # or ; that is not escaped with a backslash, so ignore-scripts=true # note sets true; a value in double quotes is parsed as a JSON string and one in single quotes loses its quotes, both keeping # and ;. A line without = sets the key to true. A [name] header at the start of a line, with nothing but spaces after it, starts a section: the keys below it belong to that section until the next header. npm applies only the top-level keys as settings (#loadObject in workspaces/config/lib/index.js at v12.2.1), so a key below a header has no effect. [↗](https://github.com/npm/ini/blob/v7.0.0/lib/ini.js)
- `extra.npmrcListSyntax`: Array values are written by adding [] after the key, one line per value, e.g. min-release-age-exclude[]=@myorg/\*. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/npmrc.md)
- `extra.allowAllScripts`: Boolean, default false: runs every dependency install script whether or not allowScripts approves it; --ignore-scripts still wins. First present in the 11.16.0 definitions. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: min-release-age-exclude takes package names or minimatch globs from its first version. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Marked as the latest GitHub release on 2026-10-28; the 11.x line is still maintained (11.21.1). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v12.2.1)
- `extra.beforeInteraction`: before is a date: npm installs only versions available on or before it. In 11.10.0 to 11.14.x the definitions of min-release-age and before name each other as exclusive, and npm stops with "--min-release-age cannot be provided when using --before" (or the reverse) once both are set in its config sources (#loadObject in workspaces/config/lib/index.js and definitions.js at v11.14.1). Since 11.15.0 both may be set: "If before and min-release-age are both set in the same source, before wins"; across sources the usual precedence applies (cli > env > project > user > global), so a before in the project .npmrc replaces its own min-release-age (definitions.js at v11.15.0 and v12.2.1; release notes of 11.15.0). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.strictAllowScripts`: strict-allow-scripts=true makes the install fail on a dependency with install scripts that allowScripts does not cover, instead of running them with a notice (default false). Entries denied with false are skipped silently; --ignore-scripts and --dangerously-allow-all-scripts override it. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.16.0/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.strictAllowScriptsEffect`: npm 12.2.1 still defines strict-allow-scripts (default false): "If true, turn the install-script policy from a warning into a hard error: any dependency with install scripts that is not covered by allowScripts will fail the install instead of being blocked with a warning." Dependencies denied with false are still skipped silently; --ignore-scripts and --dangerously-allow-all-scripts override it. So the same .npmrc line keeps npm 11.16 to 11.x from running such scripts and makes npm 12 stop the install at them. The 11.16.0 effect is the one in strictAllowScripts (definitions.js at v11.16.0). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.unknownNpmrcKeys`: Matters for generated .npmrc files: keys npm does not know (e.g. pnpm-only keys) print a warning on every npm command. The 12.0.0 entry: unknown CLI flags "now throw instead of warning. (Unknown .npmrc configs still warn by default; opt into erroring with the new strict-npmrc config.)"; lib/base-cmd.js at 12.2.1 does the same. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.commandLine`: Aliases of install (add, i and the typo aliases in, ins, inst, insta, instal, isnt, isnta, isntal, isntall), install-test (it), exec (x) and init (create, innit), the same in 11.19.1. install-test takes the same arguments as install (docs/lib/content/commands/npm-install-test.md). npm exec and npx take the packages to download from --package; -p means --package only in npx (in npm it is --parseable); without --package the first positional argument names the package, and -c/--call takes a command string that runs with the packages, shell operators included (npm-exec.md). npm init \<initializer> runs npm exec create-\<initializer>: foo → create-foo, @usr → @usr/create, @usr/foo@2.0.0 → @usr/create-foo@2.0.0 (npm-init.md). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/utils/cmd-list.js)
- `extra.runnerOptions`: npm parses its whole command line with nopt and the types of every setting (load in workspaces/config/lib/index.js at v12.2.1), and lib/commands/exec.js takes the packages from the setting package and the command line from call, so --package and --call count wherever they stand before --: before exec (npm --package=x exec y) and after the arguments. npm-exec.md ("npx vs npm exec"): "npm exec foo@latest bar --package=@npmcli/foo" resolves @npmcli/foo and runs foo@latest bar, and "a double-hyphen -- flag can be used to suppress npm's parsing of switches and options that should be sent to the executed command". npx puts -- before its first positional argument (bin/npx-cli.js), so there the options after it belong to the command. npm init and npm create do not pass --package on (lib/commands/init.js). Decision D-160. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/commands/npm-exec.md)
- `extra.valueOptions`: npm options that always take a value: every definition whose type does not include Boolean, as --name, and the short forms -C (prefix), -L (location), -c (call), -m (message) and -w (workspace). Options whose type includes Boolean (such as color and browser) may stand alone, so they are taken for flags. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.flagOptions`: npm options whose type includes Boolean, which may stand alone: the definitions of 12.2.1 and of 11.21.1 (where shrinkwrap is one too; 12.2.1 adds ignore-existing, ignore-extension, ignore-patch-failures, allow-unused-patches, keep-edit-dir and strict-npmrc). With valueOptions they are every npm option, so an abbreviated option can be resolved as npm resolves it. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.parsing`: The shorthands npm passes to nopt: the list in definitions/index.js and the short names of the definitions (the same in 11.21.1). nopt (node_modules/nopt/lib/nopt-lib.js, versions 8.1.0 in npm 10.9.4, 9.0.0 in 11.21.1 and 10.0.1 in 12.2.1, same parse and resolveShort) strips every leading dash, so -reg, --reg and -registry work; takes an exact option first, then an exact shorthand, then a word of one-letter shorthands (-gD), then an unambiguous prefix of an option name (abbrev), then a prefix of a shorthand; and reads --no-\<name> as a negated flag that takes no value. After the shorthands (resolveShort) nopt strips every leading no- in any case, each one inverting the flag, and then takes \<name> as an exact option or an unambiguous prefix (abbrevs), so --no-ign is --no-ignore-scripts where no other option starts with ign (npm 11; npm 12 has ignore-existing too) and --no-no-ignore-scripts sets ignore-scripts to true; a negated flag takes a following true or false, inverted (definitions/index.js and definitions.js at v12.2.1 and lib/nopt-lib.js of nopt 10.0.1, read again 2026-11-01). npm 10 expands abbreviations silently, npm 11 warns "Expanding --regis to --registry. This will stop working in the next major version of npm." and npm 12 refuses them with EUNKNOWNCONFIG (abbrevHandler in workspaces/config/lib/index.js of 11.21.1 and 12.2.1). Shorthands are expanded only on the command line, not in .npmrc or npm_config\_ variables. npx turns -p into --package and expands exact shorthands itself before npm exec reads the rest (bin/npx-cli.js). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/index.js)
- `extra.versionSelection`: tag (default latest): "If you ask npm to install a package and don't tell it a specific version, then it will install the specified tag"; like any setting it comes from --tag, npm_config_tag or .npmrc. A name without a version is name@\* (npm-package-arg 14.0.0, lib/npa.js). npm-pick-manifest 12.0.0 (node_modules/npm-pick-manifest/lib/index.js) picks the version of that dist-tag when the range is \* or the version satisfies the range, unless it is deprecated; otherwise the highest satisfying version, preferring versions that are not deprecated; prereleases match a range only when it names one, so name@\* with latest on a prerelease installs that prerelease. npm exec and npm init pick with the same settings. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.packageSpecs`: Forms of npm install \<spec>: a folder; a tarball file, whose name must end in .tar, .tar.gz or .tgz; a tarball URL, which must start with http:// or https://; a git remote URL with the protocol git, git+ssh, git+http, git+https or git+file; \<githubname>/\<githubrepo> or github:\<githubname>/\<githubrepo>; gist:, bitbucket: and gitlab: shorthands; \<alias>@npm:\<name>. The file: prefix for local paths is documented in docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md (Local Paths). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/commands/npm-install.md)
- `extra.registryConfig`: userconfig, the location of user-level settings, defaults to \~/.npmrc; registry is the base URL of the npm registry (default https://registry.npmjs.org/); a per-project .npmrc can set it like any config key (docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md). npm config set @myco:registry=http://reg.example.com associates a scope with a registry, and any npm install of a package with that scope then requests it from there (https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/scope#associating-a-scope-with-a-registry). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: registry is a URL; userconfig and globalconfig are the user and global configuration files. Putting --foo bar on the command line sets the foo configuration parameter, and environment variables that start with npm_config\_ are configuration parameters too, without regard to case (docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md); @scope:registry is the key of a scope's registry (https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/using-npm/scope). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.configCommands`: npm config set sets keys (in the user configuration unless location is given), delete (also rm and del) removes keys from every configuration file, edit opens a configuration file in an editor and fix repairs invalid items; get and list (ls) only read (the switch in exec, and docs/lib/content/commands/npm-config.md). npm set \<key>=\<value> runs npm config set with its arguments and fails without any (lib/commands/set.js); npm get only reads (lib/commands/get.js). npm pkg set, delete and fix write package.json back, get only reads (lib/commands/pkg.js). Other spellings of these commands come from commandNames. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/commands/config.js)
- `extra.commandNames`: deref resolves a command name: camelCase to kebab-case (installTest is install-test), an exact command, a direct alias, else a unique abbreviation of the commands and alias names (abbrev 5.0.0, node_modules/abbrev/lib/index.js: every prefix that only one name starts with, and each name itself), whose aliases are followed to the command (npm install-cl is install-clean, then ci). So npm c, npm con, npm conf and npm confi are npm config, npm pk is npm pkg, npm exe is npm exec, npm ini is npm init and npm cre is npm create, so npm init; npm ex (exec, explain, explore) and npm install- are ambiguous. lib/npm.js resolves the first word with deref, and lib/cli/entry.js prints the usage and exits with 1 when it finds no command. deref and its use are the same in v11.21.1 and v10.9.9; their lists differ (11.21.1 also has adduser, add-user, shrinkwrap, star, stars and unstar and not patch; 10.9.9 has hook and run-script with the alias run, and not approve-scripts, deny-scripts, install-scripts, stage, trust, undeprecate or u, which the 11.13.0 changelog adds), and with them no word is install, install-test, install-ci-test, ci, update, exec, init, config, set or pkg that is not one with the lists of 12.2.1 (ad is install only with those of 12.2.1, u is update from 11.13.0). Decision D-162. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/utils/cmd-list.js)
- `extra.installOverrides`: Settings that a single npm command can change on its command line or in its environment: "Putting --foo bar on the command line sets the foo configuration parameter", "--flag without specifying any value will set the value to true", "Any environment variables that start with npm_config\_ will be interpreted as a configuration parameter", case-insensitive, and an environment configuration without a value is true (docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md at v12.2.1). Types in definitions.js at v12.2.1: ignore-scripts Boolean, default false ("If true, npm does not run scripts specified in package.json files"); min-release-age null or Number of days; before null or Date; min-release-age-exclude a list exempt from min-release-age and before; dangerously-allow-all-scripts Boolean, which bypasses the allowScripts policy; allow-scripts a list of packages whose install scripts may run. A value other than true for ignore-scripts, any true value of dangerously-allow-all-scripts (the false values as in user.variables), any allow-scripts, before or min-release-age-exclude, and a min-release-age shorter than the policy weaken what depcurfew apply wrote. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.settingOverrides`: The settings depcurfew apply writes into .npmrc for installScripts and sources that installOverrides (the options and variables the install guard asks about) does not list, for doctor (decision D-166). npm takes its configuration from, "sorted by priority", the command line ("Putting --foo bar on the command line sets the foo configuration parameter", "Using --flag without specifying any value will set the value to true"), then the environment ("Any environment variables that start with npm_config\_ will be interpreted as a configuration parameter", "Config values are case-insensitive", with underscores instead of dashes), then the .npmrc files, so either replaces a key of the project .npmrc for the commands it reaches; a --no- prefix sets false (booleanWords). In definitions.js at v12.2.1 strict-allow-scripts is a Boolean (default false), and parseField (workspaces/config/lib/parse-field.js) turns only "false", "null" and "undefined" into values that turn it off, so those weaken it where .npmrc sets it to true (apply writes it for an npm 11.16 to 11.x in use, which runs uncovered scripts without it). allow-git, allow-remote, allow-file and allow-directory take all, none or root; apply writes none for a source the policy denies, root allows the dependencies listed in the root package.json, and a value npm does not accept is reported as invalid and replaced by the default (all before npm 12; user.invalidValueFails), so every value but none weakens a denied source. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: prefix (short C, so -C dir is --prefix dir): "The location to install global items. If set on the command line, then it forces non-global commands to run in the specified folder." loadLocalPrefix in workspaces/config/lib/index.js (v12.2.1) reads it only from the command line ("this.#get('prefix', 'cli')"), takes it as the local prefix as given and does not walk up, so npm_config_prefix and .npmrc do not move a command; the project .npmrc is the one in that folder. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.booleanWords`: nopt, which parses the npm command line, also supports "--bool true or --bool false": a Boolean option followed by the word true or false takes it as its value and skips it, and a --no- prefix inverts the value (parse in lib/nopt-lib.js at v10.0.1, used by npm 12.2.1, and the same code at v9.0.0, used by npm 11.21.1). [↗](https://github.com/npm/nopt/blob/v10.0.1/lib/nopt-lib.js)
- `extra.installCommands`: Commands that install packages into the project and their aliases: install (add, i, typo aliases, install-test and it), ci (clean-install, ic, install-clean, isntall-clean) with install-ci-test (cit, clean-install-test, sit), and update (up, upgrade, udpate; u only from npm 11.13.0, whose changelog adds it, so left out). The same in v10.9.9 (lib/utils/cmd-list.js). npm also accepts unique abbreviations of command names, which are not listed. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/utils/cmd-list.js)
- `extra.globalOption`: global (short g) "Operates in global mode, so that packages are installed into the prefix folder instead of the current working directory" and sets location to global; npm install -g npm@\<version> replaces the npm that runs (docs/lib/content/commands/npm-install.md: "In global mode (ie, with -g or --global appended to the command)"). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)
- `extra.unknownConfigKeys`: npm 10 loads every key of an .npmrc without checking whether it knows it (#loadObject only checks deprecated and exclusive keys), so a setting it does not have yet, such as min-release-age, is ignored without any message. checkUnknown first appears in v11.2.0 (workspaces/config/lib/index.js), which warns: Unknown project config "\<key>". This will stop working in the next major version of npm. The 11.2.0 changelog does not name the change; the version comes from reading the code at the tags. npm 12 collects unknown keys to fail the command (v12.2.1), with the exact behavior not read. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v10.9.9/workspaces/config/lib/index.js)
- `extra.cleanInstall`: npm ci (the clean commands of installCommands): "The project must have an existing package-lock.json"; "If dependencies in the package lock do not match those in package.json, npm ci will exit with an error, instead of updating the package lock"; "It will never write to package.json or package-lock.json: installs are essentially frozen." lib/commands/ci.js at v12.2.1 loads the lockfile (loadVirtual), builds the ideal tree, throws "\`npm ci\` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync" when validateLockfile finds a difference, and reifies with packageLock: true and save: false. So npm ci installs exactly the versions package-lock.json records, and a release-age delay cannot change which versions it installs; the settings of its params (ignore-scripts, allow-scripts, strict-allow-scripts, allow-git, allow-remote, allow-file, allow-directory) still apply. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/commands/npm-ci.md)
- `extra.scriptsOff`: ignore-scripts (Boolean, default false; definitions.js at v12.2.1: "If true, npm does not run scripts specified in package.json files") is one of the params of npm ci and npm install (lib/commands/ci.js). On the command line --ignore-scripts sets it; "Any environment variables that start with npm_config\_ will be interpreted as a configuration parameter", with underscores for dashes, and "Config values are case-insensitive, so NPM_CONFIG_FOO=bar will work the same". depcurfew counts only the value true (and the flag without a value) as off: parseField turns only "true" into true, and loadEnv skips empty values (user.variables). [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/using-npm/config.md)
- `extra.nodeEngines`: engines.node of npm/cli package.json, the same at the tags v11.0.0, v11.10.0, v11.16.0, v11.19.1 and v11.21.1 (^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0) and at v12.0.0 and v12.2.1 (^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/package.json). On a Node.js outside the range npm only warns that it does not support it: lib/cli/entry.js at v11.19.1 runs log.warn('cli', validateEngines.unsupportedMessage) when !satisfies(node, engines), for a Node.js "still unsupported and untested and might not work reliably", and lib/cli/validate-engines.js prints "ERROR: npm ... is known not to run on Node.js ..." when it fails with a SyntaxError. So npm install -g npm@11 on Node.js 18 installs an npm that is not meant to run there. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/package.json)
- `extra.rootLifecycleScripts`: A bare npm install in a project runs the lifecycle scripts of the project itself with runScript, outside arborist and its allowScripts gate: "const runRootLifecycle = !args.length && !isGlobalInstall && !ignoreScripts", preinstall before reify and install, postinstall, prepublish, preprepare, prepare and postprepare after it. npm ci does the same "if (!ignoreScripts)" (lib/commands/ci.js), and so do install.js and ci.js at v11.16.0. collectUnreviewedScripts in workspaces/arborist/lib/unreviewed-scripts.js skips "node.isProjectRoot || node.isWorkspace", so strict-allow-scripts never stops at them. using-npm/scripts.md: prepare "Runs on local npm install without package arguments (runs with flags like --production or --omit=dev, but does not run when installing specific packages like npm install express)". [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/lib/commands/install.js)
- `extra.omitOptional`: omit: [Array, "dev", "optional", "peer"], "Dependency types to omit from the installation tree on disk"; include: "Dependency types specified in --include will not be omitted, regardless of the order in which omit/include are specified on the command-line"; optional: deprecated, "Alias for --include=optional or --omit=optional" (buildOmitList: obj.optional === false pushes optional to omit, true to include; omit then drops what include lists). --no-optional sets optional to false. Each is one key: the value of the highest layer that sets it wins (command line, then npm_config\_\* variables in any case, then the project .npmrc). parseField in workspaces/config/lib/parse-field.js splits a list from the environment at two line breaks ("list types get put in the environment separated by double-\\n"), so NPM_CONFIG_OMIT=optional omits them and dev,optional is one unknown value. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js)

### pnpm

- `cooldown.configFiles`: pnpm-workspace.yaml works in every version that has the setting. The global config.yaml exists only from 11.0.0 ("the new global config.yaml"); pnpm 10 reads user-level settings from \~/.npmrc and \<configDir>/rc instead (see user.files). pnpm 10 also reads minimum-release-age from .npmrc; pnpm 11+ reads only auth and registry settings from .npmrc and ignores the package.json "pnpm" field. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0)
- `cooldown.unit`: Integer number of minutes, e.g. 1440 = 1 day; no duration strings. [↗](https://pnpm.io/settings/dependency-resolution)
- `cooldown.default`: The built-in 1440 is non-strict: pnpm adds immature versions to minimumReleaseAgeExclude instead of failing (see strictMode). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/main/versioned_docs/version-11.x/settings/dependency-resolution.md)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: No setting bypasses the delay. Since 11.0.0, pnpm audit --fix adds the minimum patched version of each advisory to minimumReleaseAgeExclude (since 11.22.0 only while it is still inside the window). [↗](https://pnpm.io/cli/audit)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Unreviewed builds only warn in pnpm 10; strictDepBuilds is true by default since 11.0.0, so they fail the install. Prepare scripts of git-hosted dependencies are blocked since 10.26.0. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v10.0.0)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: Replaced onlyBuiltDependencies, which was removed in 11.0.0 (see legacyAllowList). Since 12.11.0, permissions.\<package>.build takes precedence over allowBuilds (extra.buildPermissions). [↗](https://pnpm.io/settings/build)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Default false; --ignore-scripts on the CLI. Also skips the project's own scripts. It does not stop the pnpmfiles (.pnpmfile.mjs, .pnpmfile.cjs, the pnpmfile and globalPnpmfile settings and the pnpmfiles of config-dependency plugins, extra.pnpmfiles), whose hooks still run and can change every setting; only ignorePnpmfile does ("Useful together with --ignore-scripts when you want to make sure that no script gets executed during install", pnpm/docs/pnpmfile.md at v12.17.0). resolve_pnpmfile_paths in pnpm/crates/cli/src/config_deps/hooks.rs at v12.17.0 tests ignore_pnpmfile only. [↗](https://pnpm.io/cli/install)
- `sources.git.setting`: Blocks git repositories and tarball URLs for transitive dependencies only; no setting blocks them as direct dependencies. [↗](https://pnpm.io/10.x/settings)
- `sources.remoteTarball.setting`: Blocks git repositories and tarball URLs for transitive dependencies only; no setting blocks them as direct dependencies. [↗](https://pnpm.io/10.x/settings)
- `project.workspaces`: Globs with ! exclusions. Without packages only the root is in the workspace; pnpm still reads settings from the file in single-package projects. pnpm ignores workspaces in package.json. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/main/versioned_docs/version-10.x/pnpm-workspace_yaml.md)
- `user.files`: getConfigDir: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pnpm when it is set, else \~/Library/Preferences/pnpm on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%/pnpm/config on Windows (\~/.config/pnpm without LOCALAPPDATA) and \~/.config/pnpm elsewhere; the same in 10.34.9 (config/config/src/dirs.ts) and 12.17.0 (pnpm/crates/config-dir/src/lib.rs). pnpm 10 reads \<configDir>/rc, INI with kebab-case keys (config/config/src/index.ts at 10.34.9; first version not tracked), and also \~/.npmrc for every setting, which beats rc: loadNpmConf reads the command line, npm_config\_\* variables, the project and workspace .npmrc, \~/.npmrc (userconfig, path.resolve(os.homedir(), ".npmrc") in https://github.com/pnpm/npm-conf/blob/v3.0.3/lib/defaults.js) and the global npmrc, and only then is rc added as "pnpm-global", below all of them (index.ts at 10.34.9). From 11.0.0 the settings file is \<configDir>/config.yaml with camelCase keys (11.0.0 changelog: "the new global config.yaml"), and \~/.npmrc and \<configDir>/auth.ini carry only auth, registry and network settings. The 11.x and 12.x docs page cli/config.md still names a global rc file for registry and auth settings, which that code no longer reads. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/config/reader/src/dirs.ts)
- `user.settings`: pnpm 10 reads the kebab-case keys from rc as from any .npmrc (config/config/src/types.ts: only-built-dependencies at 10.0.0, strict-dep-builds at 10.3.0, minimum-release-age and minimum-release-age-exclude at 10.16.0, block-exotic-subdeps at 10.26.0); since 10.13.0 build settings from these files apply only to projects whose package.json "pnpm" field and pnpm-workspace.yaml set none of dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds, onlyBuiltDependencies(File), neverBuiltDependencies or allowBuilds, and always to global installs. pnpm 11+ applies a config.yaml key only when isConfigFileKey accepts it and it is camelCase: the minimumReleaseAge keys and blockExoticSubdeps since 11.0.0, strictDepBuilds since 11.0.7 (in excludedPnpmKeys in 11.0.0-11.0.6). allowBuilds is project-only from 11.0.0 and dropped with a warning, so pnpm 11+ has no user-level allow-list. pnpm 12 silently drops blockExoticSubdeps from config.yaml although its key gate accepts it (clear_workspace_resolution_fields in pnpm/crates/config/src/workspace_yaml/workspace_scope.rs, 12.0.0 to 12.17.0). pnpm self-update takes the minimumReleaseAge settings only from config.yaml, the environment and the command line, never from the project. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/config/reader/src/configFileKey.ts)
- `user.weakening`: A key in pnpm-workspace.yaml replaces the user value, lists included (applyWorkspaceSetting: pnpmConfig[key] = value); PNPM_CONFIG\_\* variables and the command line beat both. In pnpm 10 the same keys in \~/.npmrc beat rc, and since 10.13.0 build settings from either file reach only projects without build settings of their own, and global installs (config/config/src/index.ts at 10.34.9; before 10.13.0 dangerously-allow-all-builds also joined a project's onlyBuiltDependencies). In config.yaml, dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds also overrides a project's allowBuilds: false in pnpm 11 and 12.0.0-12.11.x (see extra.allowAllBuilds). pnpm 10 has no default delay and its strict-dep-builds and block-exotic-subdeps default to false, so 0 or false there weakens nothing; trustLockfile is a global key since it appeared in 11.3.0. The switch that allows every build is on for any value pnpm does not read as off, because pnpm tests it for truth (see extra.allowAllBuilds): in config.yaml only false, 0, null and an empty string are off, so "false", yes and "true" (strings for js-yaml) are on; in rc and \~/.npmrc pnpm 10 parses values with parseField of @pnpm/npm-conf (lib/util.js at https://github.com/pnpm/npm-conf/blob/v3.0.2/lib/util.js, the same in 3.0.3, which pnpm 10.28.0 and 10.34.9 use), which turns only "false", "null" and "undefined" into falsy values, an empty value of a Boolean setting into true, and leaves yes, 1 and 0 as strings, which are true. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/config/reader/src/getConfig/workspaceManifestSettings.ts)
- `user.variables`: pnpm 11 reads pnpm_config\_\<key> in lower case or PNPM_CONFIG\_\<KEY> in upper case, not mixed case (getEnvKeySuffix), over pnpm-workspace.yaml and under the command line; pnpm 12 reads the same two forms (pnpm/crates/config/src/env_overlay.rs at 12.17.0). pnpm 11+ ignores npm_config\_\* except npm_config_userconfig, which then moves only the auth .npmrc. The 11.0.0 release notes (https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0): "pnpm no longer reads npm_config\_\* environment variables", "Added support for loading environment variables whose names start with pnpm_config\_ into config"; pnpm 10.34.9 reads pnpm_config\_ only for verify-deps-before-run (config/config/src/index.ts). pnpm 10 reads npm_config\_\* in any case, skipping empty values (addEnv in lib/conf.js of @pnpm/npm-conf 3.0.3), under pnpm-workspace.yaml (npmrcPrecedence), and parses them with the same parseField as .npmrc, so npm_config_dangerously_allow_all_builds is off only for false, null and undefined (1 and yes stay true strings); its npm_config_userconfig defaults to \~/.npmrc (lib/defaults.js). pnpm 11 parses a Boolean pnpm_config\_ value with parseBoolean of env.ts, which takes only true as true (false gives false, any other text no value). XDG_CONFIG_HOME and LOCALAPPDATA move the config directory (user.files). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/config/reader/src/env.ts)
- `extra.environmentNames`: pnpm 11 reads pnpm_config\_\<key> only with the prefix and the key in lower case, or PNPM_CONFIG\_\<KEY> with both in upper case (getEnvKeySuffix with isLowerSnakeCase and isUpperSnakeCase), so Pnpm_Config_Registry sets nothing; pnpm 12 looks up PNPM_CONFIG\_\<KEY> and then pnpm_config\_\<key> (read_env in pnpm/crates/config/src/env_overlay/string_reader.rs, https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/crates/config/src/env_overlay/string_reader.rs). pnpm 10 reads npm_config\_\* in any case: addEnv in lib/conf.js of @pnpm/npm-conf 3.0.3 filters with /^npm_config\_/i, and envKeyToSetting lowercases the key (https://github.com/pnpm/npm-conf/blob/v3.0.3/lib/envKeyToSetting.js). Decision D-143. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/config/reader/src/env.ts)
- `extra.denyList`: allowBuilds: { pkg: false } records a denial: the build is decided, not reported as unreviewed and does not fail strictDepBuilds ("A recorded build the policy denies was decided on purpose"). pnpm 10.26 maps false to ignoredBuiltDependencies, which only silences the report. Under dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds a denied package still builds before pnpm 12.12.0. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/building/policy/src/index.ts)
- `extra.projectInstall`: Commands that install the dependencies of the project: "pnpm install is used to install all dependencies for a project", "Aliases: i". pnpm add (commandLine.add) adds packages. pnpm without a command does not install. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/7aded9fe30ceb31d4302b4189fcac84c958582b0/docs/cli/install.md)
- `extra.commandLine`: From cli/add.md, cli/pnx.md, cli/create.md and pnpm-cli.md at that commit. pnx (pnpm 12) has the aliases pnpm dlx and pnpx; pnpm 10 documents pnpm dlx with the alias pnpx (versioned_docs/version-10.x/cli/dlx.md). --shell-mode (-c) runs the command inside a shell, e.g. pnx --package cowsay -c 'echo hi | cowsay'. pnpm create maps foo and create-foo to create-foo, @scope to @scope/create and @scope/foo to @scope/create-foo, and runs it with pnx. --registry and --allow-build are shown with =, the other value options with a separate value. --package belongs to pnx (pnpm dlx) only and is listed there; before dlx it counts too (runnerOptions). -F is the short form of --filter (filtering.md). --reporter takes the name of a reporter (cli/install.md) and --loglevel a level (the loglevel setting in settings/cli.md, given as a flag); both take a separate value too. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/tree/7aded9fe30ceb31d4302b4189fcac84c958582b0/docs/cli)
- `extra.runnerOptions`: pnpm 10 parses the command line twice with @pnpm/nopt: first with the universal options and those of add and install, to find the command (there --package is taken for package-import-method, its only unambiguous expansion, so the word after it is its value), then the whole line with the options of that command, so the options of dlx count before dlx too, up to the first argument after dlx, from which on every word goes to the command (SPECIALLY_ESCAPED_CMDS). pnpm 11 does the same (https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts; package-import-method is still the only option of add and install that starts with package). pnpm 12 moves the options of the invoked subcommand that stand before it to right after it (relocate_pre_subcommand_flags, https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/crates/cli/src/flag_relocation.rs), and its dlx has --package and -c (pnpm/crates/cli/src/cli_args/dlx.rs). The documentation shows pnpm --package=@pnpm/meta-updater dlx meta-updater --help and pnpm --package cowsay --package lolcatjs -c dlx 'echo "hi pnpm" | cowsay | lolcatjs' (versioned_docs/version-10.x/cli/dlx.md in pnpm/pnpm.io). pnpm exec has no --package (exec/plugin-commands-script-runners/src/exec.ts at v10.34.9), and pnpm stops at an option the command does not know (pnpm/src/main.ts), so pnpm --package=x exec y downloads nothing. Decision D-160. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.34.9/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts)
- `extra.packageSpecs`: Sources of pnpm add: the npm registry, jsr:, crate: and pypi: (other registries), workspace packages (the workspace: range protocol, docs/workspaces.md), local directories (./dir is saved as link:, file:./dir is copied), local tarballs ending in .tar, .tar.gz or .tgz, remote tarballs starting with http:// or https://, and git repositories as user/repo (github: by default), github:, bitbucket:, gitlab:, gist: or a full URL such as git+ssh://… or https://github.com/….git. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/7aded9fe30ceb31d4302b4189fcac84c958582b0/docs/package-sources.md)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: registry and @scope:registry are read from the command line over .npmrc (docs/npmrc.md in pnpm/pnpm.io). Every pnpm_config\_\<key> or PNPM_CONFIG\_\<KEY> variable whose key is a setting sets it (src/env.ts, parseEnvVars), registry included. The user-level .npmrc, which may set any registry, is the file named by --npmrc-auth-file, --userconfig, pnpm_config_npmrc_auth_file, pnpm_config_userconfig, npmrcAuthFile in the global config.yaml or npm_config_userconfig (getNpmrcAuthFile; src/loadNpmrcFiles.ts reads it in place of \~/.npmrc). pnpm 10 reads npm_config\_\* variables as npm does. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.16.1/pnpm11/config/reader/src/index.ts)
- `extra.parsing`: pnpm parses its command line with @pnpm/nopt 0.3.1 (github.com/pnpm/nopt, lib/nopt.js), a fork of nopt: every leading dash is stripped, an exact shorthand or a word of one-letter shorthands is expanded, and an unambiguous prefix of an option of the command is taken for that option, so pnpm add --reg=\<url> sets registry; --no-\<name> is a negated flag: lib/nopt.js strips every leading no- in any case, each one inverting it, before the prefix is resolved, so --no-ign is --no-ignore-scripts when no other option of the command starts with ign (parse-cli-args, shorthands.ts and pnpm/nopt read again 2026-11-01). Options pnpm does not know make it stop with an error (pnpm11/pnpm/src/main.ts, dropUnknownOptions). --config.\<key>=\<value> sets the setting \<key> (separateConfigDotArgs, normalizeOptions), also in pnpm 10.34.9 (cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts). The shorthands are pnpm11/pnpm/src/shorthands.ts; pnpm 10.34.9 has the same without y. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.16.1/pnpm11/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts)
- `extra.booleanWords`: The nopt fork pnpm imports (@pnpm/nopt, imported by pnpm11/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts at v12.16.1) reads a Boolean option followed by the word true or false as that value and skips the word, inverted after --no- (parse in lib/nopt.js). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/nopt/blob/7f8522c60a84c04bed2ac792204d8c22172d295f/lib/nopt.js)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: -C \<path>, --dir \<path>: "Run as if pnpm was started in \<path> instead of the current working directory." -C is the shorthand of --dir (parsing.shorthands). pnpm11/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts at v12.16.1 takes dir from the options nopt parsed from the whole command line ("let dir = parsedOpts['dir']") and looks for the workspace from it ("findWorkspaceDir((dir ?? process.cwd()) as string)"). -w, --workspace-root ("Run as if pnpm was started in the root of the workspace") is not listed: it names no directory. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/7aded9fe30ceb31d4302b4189fcac84c958582b0/docs/pnpm-cli.md)
- `extra.configCommands`: pnpm config (aliases: c) manages the configuration files: set \<key> \<value>, get \<key>, delete \<key> and list; get and list only read. pnpm pkg "Manages the contents of package.json from the command line": get, set, delete and fix, no aliases (docs/cli/pkg.md). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/main/docs/cli/config.md)
- `extra.installOverrides`: pnpm add takes --ignore-scripts ("Same as the ignoreScripts setting") and --allow-build, which lists packages allowed to run postinstall scripts (docs/cli/add.md in pnpm/pnpm.io; a ! prefix denies one instead, still asked about). Any setting can be given as --config.\<key>=\<value>, the key kept as written (normalizeOptions in pnpm11/cli/parse-cli-args/src/index.ts at v12.16.1), so both spellings are listed and the scanner reads the key without --config.. pnpm_config\_\<key> and PNPM_CONFIG\_\<KEY> set the setting of the camel-cased key; a Boolean only from the exact words true and false, a number with Number (parseEnvVars in env.ts). pnpm 10 reads npm_config\_\* variables as npm does (registryOverrides). minimumReleaseAgeStrict false installs a younger version when no older one matches (user.weakening). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.16.1/pnpm11/config/reader/src/env.ts)
- `extra.minimumReleaseAgeStrict`: When false, pnpm falls back to a version that does not meet minimumReleaseAge; when true, resolution fails. It defaults to true when minimumReleaseAge is set explicitly, except in 11.0.0-11.0.3 and 12.0.0-12.2.x (see strictMode): pnpm 11.0.0 and 12.0.0 installed a version 4 hours old with minimumReleaseAge: 4320 on 2026-10-29, and 12.0.0 added it to minimumReleaseAgeExclude. [↗](https://pnpm.io/settings/dependency-resolution)
- `extra.cooldownExactVersions`: pnpm 10.17.0: "Don't ignore the minimumReleaseAge check, when the package is requested by exact version". pnpm 10.16.0 installed typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261029.1, 4 hours old, with minimumReleaseAge: 4320 on 2026-10-29. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v10.17.0)
- `extra.lockfileDocuments`: A lockfile whose first line is --- has two YAML documents: a boot document with configDependencies and packageManagerDependencies, written when the project has config dependencies, declares devEngines.packageManager or pins pnpm 12 or newer; then the project lockfile (importers, packages, snapshots), which is always the last document. Seen with pnpm 12.16.1 and packageManager pnpm@12.16.1 on 2026-10-29. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/main/docs/lockfile.md)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: lockfileVersion 9.0 (pnpm 9 to 12). Registry packages are keyed name@version; git dependencies name@git+\<repo>#\<commit> with resolution type git, or a tarball from a git host (gitHosted: true; older lockfiles lack the flag, so the host decides); tarball URLs name@https://…; local tarballs name@file:….tgz; local directories have resolution type directory; link: and workspace: dependencies appear only under importers. requiresBuild was removed in lockfile v9, so install scripts are not recorded. A tarball URL under the configured registry is resolved as that registry package and version (resolving/npm-resolver/src/parseBareSpecifier.ts in v10.34.9), so it is keyed name@version and keeps the URL only in the importer specifier; seen in lockfiles written by pnpm 10.34.9 and 12.16.1. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.34.9/lockfile/types/src/index.ts)
- `extra.npmrcPrecedence`: pnpm 10 applies pnpm-workspace.yaml settings over .npmrc and npm_config\_\* variables; command-line options win over both (same order on v10.16.0). The 10.18.3 changelog says pnpm config set --location=project writes to pnpm-workspace.yaml "matching read priority". The 10.x docs do not state the order. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.34.9/config/config/src/index.ts)
- `extra.npmrcCooldownKey`: pnpm 10 reads minimum-release-age from .npmrc as a number and maps it to minimumReleaseAge (minutes), so the value means the same in both files; pnpm-workspace.yaml wins when both set it (npmrcPrecedence). pnpm 11.0.0 stopped reading it from .npmrc (ignoredSince). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.34.9/config/config/src/types.ts)
- `extra.sharedWorkspaceLockfile`: Same name and default in pnpm 11 and 12, where it is read only from pnpm-workspace.yaml. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.io/blob/7aded9fe30ceb31d4302b4189fcac84c958582b0/versioned_docs/version-10.x/workspaces.md)
- `extra.ignoredSince`: Structured form of npmrcIgnored: from 11.0.0 on, other .npmrc settings and the package.json "pnpm" field have no effect. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0)
- `extra.allowAllBuilds`: off: the values that leave it off. pnpm tests the value for truth and checks no type: pnpm 10 and 11 read pnpm-workspace.yaml with js-yaml (extra.yamlMergeKeys) and copy each key as it is (getOptionsFromPnpmSettings at 10.28.0, applyWorkspaceSetting at 11.28.10), so a string such as "false", "no" or "true" is on; depcurfew treats every value but false, 0, null and an empty string as on. pnpm 12 reads it into an Option\<bool> (dangerously_allow_all_builds in pnpm/crates/config/src/workspace_yaml/settings.rs at 12.16.1) with the YAML 1.1 words of serde-saphyr 0.0.29 (parse_yaml11_bool: true, yes, y, on and false, no, n, off, in any case and also quoted), and stops on any other value, so no value is on there that depcurfew reads as off. Boolean, default false; added in 10.9.0 ("Added a new setting, dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds, for automatically running any scripts of dependencies without the need to approve any builds", pnpm/CHANGELOG.md at v10.26.0). Packages set to false in allowBuilds (or build: false in permissions) stay blocked only from pnpm 12.12.0 (release notes at https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.12.0: "A package set to false in allowBuilds no longer runs its build scripts when dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds is true", "Previously, dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds ignored the denials"). pnpm 10, 11 and 12.0.0-12.11.x run them too: createAllowBuildFunction returns before it reads the lists ("if (opts.dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds) return () => true" in building/policy at 11.28.10 and builder/policy/src/index.ts at 10.34.9; allow_build_policy.rs at 12.0.0). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/building/policy/src/index.ts)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Globs such as @myorg/\* in minimumReleaseAgeExclude since 10.17.0. [↗](https://pnpm.io/10.x/settings)
- `extra.onlyBuiltDependencies`: The allow-list before allowBuilds: package.json pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies, added in 6.32.0 ("If this field exists, only mentioned packages will be able to run install scripts") and working since 6.32.1 ("released with a bug in v6.32.0"); also pnpm-workspace.yaml since 10.5.0 (10.5.0 changelog); removed in 11.0.0 (settings/build.md, see legacyAllowList). Before pnpm 10 any list, even an empty one, lets only the listed packages build (createAllowBuildFunction in @pnpm/builder.policy 3.0.0, which pnpm 9.15.0 uses). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.26.0/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.ignoredBuiltDependencies`: The record of denied builds before allowBuilds (denyList): package.json pnpm.ignoredBuiltDependencies since 10.1.0 ("for explicitly listing packages that should not be built. When a package is in the list, pnpm will not print an info message about that package not being built"), and pnpm-workspace.yaml since 10.5.0 ("Allow to set the \\"pnpm\\" settings from package.json via the pnpm-workspace.yaml file"). The 10.26.0 entry for allowBuilds says that allowBuilds: { core-js: false } "achieves the same result as" ignoredBuiltDependencies: [core-js]. It only silences the report: createAllowBuildFunction (builder/policy/src/index.ts at v10.25.0) does not read it, so a package onlyBuiltDependencies names still builds. Deprecated in 10.26.0 and removed in 11.0.0 (see legacyAllowList). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.26.0/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.npmrcBuildSettings`: pnpm 10 reads dangerously-allow-all-builds from the project .npmrc as from every .npmrc, with parseField of @pnpm/npm-conf, so every value but false, null and undefined is on (user.weakening). From 10.13.0 config/config/src/index.ts takes the build settings of all .npmrc files and npm_config\_\* variables aside (extractAndRemoveDependencyBuildOptions) and applies them only when pnpm-workspace.yaml and the "pnpm" field of package.json (from which getOptionsFromRootManifest takes onlyBuiltDependencies, onlyBuiltDependenciesFile and neverBuiltDependencies) set none of projectKeys (hasDependencyBuildOptions: a key that is not null or undefined); the list gained allowBuilds in 10.26.0 (dependencyBuildOptions.ts at 10.13.0, 10.25.0, 10.26.0 and 10.28.0; the file does not exist in 10.12.1). Before 10.13.0 the .npmrc value applies unless pnpm-workspace.yaml sets dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds itself (npmrcPrecedence). pnpm 11 reads only auth and registry settings from .npmrc (ignoredSince). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.28.0/config/config/src/dependencyBuildOptions.ts)
- `extra.yamlMergeKeys`: pnpm-workspace.yaml and the global config.yaml (readWorkspaceManifest with cfgFileName) are read with read-yaml-file, which calls load of js-yaml with its default schema, and that schema has the merge type: read-yaml-file 3.0.0 with @zkochan/js-yaml 0.0.11 in 11.28.10, read-yaml-file 2.1.0 with @zkochan/js-yaml 0.0.9 in 10.28.0 and 0.0.11 in 10.34.9 (workspace/read-manifest/src/index.ts and pnpm-lock.yaml at those tags; lib/schema/default.js of the packages). pnpm 12 reads both files with serde_saphyr::from_str (pnpm/crates/config/src/workspace_yaml/parse_settings.rs at 12.16.1), whose default MergeKeyPolicy is Merge (serde-saphyr 0.0.29). So \<\<: \*defaults brings the keys of the anchored map into the map, and settings set that way apply (a review run with pnpm 10.28.0: pnpm config get dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds gave true and installs ran scripts). A key written in the map itself wins over a merged one whatever their order (mergeMappings of js-yaml adds only missing keys; serde-saphyr adds merged entries whose key is not seen), and earlier maps of \<\<: [\*a, \*b] win over later ones; a quoted "\<\<" is an ordinary key. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/workspace/workspace-manifest-reader/src/index.ts)
- `extra.latestVersion`: pnpm 12.0.0 shipped on 26 Aug and 11.0.0 on 28 Apr (GitHub shows no year; 2026 inferred from release order). 11.x and 10.x still receive patches. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1)
- `extra.buildPermissions`: permissions.\<package>.build in pnpm-workspace.yaml: true lets the package run its build scripts, false denies them; the keys take the same forms as those of allowBuilds, and the entry outranks the package's allowBuilds entry (decided_build_approvals and apply_permissions in pnpm/crates/config/src/workspace_yaml/permissions.rs at v12.16.1, which warns when a package is in both). A string is an undecided placeholder (AllowBuild::Undecided in sections.rs). Added in 12.11.0 (docs/settings/build.md and docs/cli/permissions.md); pnpm approve writes a build decision there only when the file already has permissions. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.16.1/pnpm/docs/settings/build.md)
- `extra.strictDepBuilds`: When true, an unreviewed dependency build script fails the install. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0)
- `extra.strictMode`: In non-strict mode pnpm silently writes immature picks into minimumReleaseAgeExclude. Strict mode fails CI installs with ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.3.0)
- `extra.tarballResolution`: pnpm fetches a registry package of pnpm-lock.yaml (a key name@version) from the tarball URL get-npm-tarball-url builds from the name and version, unless its resolution has tarball: then from that URL, resolved against the registry (new url.URL(resolution.tarball, registry)). pnpm 11.28.10 does the same (resolveTarballUrl in pnpm11/lockfile/utils/src/pkgSnapshotToResolution.ts). assertRegistryShapedResolution (lockfile/utils/src/assertRegistryShapedResolution.ts at v10.34.9) accepts any http(s) URL there for such a key, and a relative path without a scheme or a leading slash, which "is resolved against the configured registry", while the allowBuild policy "derives a trusted package identity from that key shape". pnpm writes tarball for a registry package whose tarball is not at the URL it would build. The fetch requests the path and the query of the URL, never the fragment, and the registry serves the file the path names. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.34.9/lockfile/utils/src/pkgSnapshotToResolution.ts)
- `extra.rootLifecycleScripts`: pnpm 11.28.10 runs the projects' own lifecycle scripts after linking "if (!opts.ignoreScripts && !opts.virtualStoreOnly)" (runProjectLifecycleScripts), with PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_STAGES = preinstall, install, postinstall, preprepare, prepare, postprepare for a full install and only the install stages for --prod or deploy (exec/lifecycle/src/runLifecycleHooksConcurrently.ts); allowBuilds only goes to the build of dependencies (allowBuild). pnpm 10.34.9 does the same in pkg-manager/core/src/install/index.ts and, for a frozen lockfile, pkg-manager/headless/src/index.ts ("if (!opts.ignoreScripts && !opts.ignorePackageManifest) await runLifecycleHooksConcurrently([preinstall, install, postinstall, preprepare, prepare, postprepare], ...)"). pnpm 12.16.1 picks PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_STAGES for a full install with devDependencies (project_script_stages in pnpm/crates/package-manager/src/install/lifecycle/uninstall.rs). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v11.28.10/pnpm11/installing/deps-installer/src/install/linkResolvedProjects.ts)
- `extra.managesOwnVersion`: 10.0.0: "manage-package-manager-versions: enabled by default. pnpm now manages its own version based on the packageManager field in package.json by default" (added in 9.7.0, off by default: "pnpm will switch to the version specified in the packageManager field of package.json ... This is the same field used by Corepack"). The 11.0.0 release notes replace the setting with pmOnFail, which "directly sets the onFail behavior of both packageManager and devEngines.packageManager" (https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0); pnpm 12 documents pmOnFail with the default download: "download and run the declared pnpm version (this is the default and matches the previous managePackageManagerVersions: true behavior)" (pnpm/docs/settings/cli.md at v12.16.1). So any pnpm 10 or later honors a pnpm pin without Corepack. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v10.26.0/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.configIncludes`: "Added in: v12.15.0" (12.15.0 release notes, 21 Oct: "can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new include field"). include in the root pnpm-workspace.yaml maps a source to the settings it may define: a list of settings, which the source both may define and owns ("A list both permits and reserves its settings ... no other source may define them, even when the file omits them"), or '\*' for a local file, which then owns the settings it defines that no other source owns. A local source starts with ./ or ../, is resolved from the workspace root, must end in .yaml or .yml and exist; a glob is rejected, and so is a file named twice or the root itself. Every other source is a config dependency named in configDependencies, which always needs a list. Settings defined in pnpm-workspace.yaml itself belong to it; a setting reserved twice, or defined where another source owns it, fails with ERR_PNPM_DUPLICATE_SETTING, a listed file that defines another setting with ERR_PNPM_SETTING_NOT_DELEGATED, a bad source with ERR_PNPM_INVALID_WORKSPACE_INCLUDE. A delegated setting the owner omits is not set by the project. Writes go to the owner: a delegated setting to its file even when the file omits it, a setting a '\*' file defines stays there, one no source owns goes to pnpm-workspace.yaml, and one a config dependency owns cannot be changed (ERR_PNPM_SETTING_OWNED_BY_CONFIG_DEPENDENCY). Relative paths in an included file are relative to that file. The included files are read with merge keys like the root (normalize.rs applies \<\<). The spellings share one owner, so permissions and allowBuilds are one setting for ownership (canonical_setting_name in pnpm/crates/workspace/src/include/selector.rs); catalog is catalogs.default, catalogs.\<name> one catalog and catalogs every catalog. Code: pnpm/crates/workspace/src/include.rs, include/selector.rs (parse_source, is_package_name_shaped, parse_delegation, SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN_TO_PACKAGES in include.rs), include/ownership.rs (reservations before definitions; the owner of a setting is its reservation, else its definition), include/package.rs (a config dependency's settings come from the YAML file its package.json names in pnpm.config, read from node_modules/.pnpm-config/\<name> once installed); the same code at v12.15.0. Decision D-164. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/docs/config-includes.md)
- `extra.bootConfig`: bootConfig in pnpm-workspace.yaml sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm resolves and installs config dependencies and the pnpm version of packageManager under, before the settings of config dependencies are loaded (12.15.0 release notes: "The new bootConfig setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies"). A setting it leaves unset or null takes its regular value; for a setting a config dependency owns, the value of the global config.yaml, the environment or the built-in default. The environment and the command line beat bootConfig (for_boot in pnpm/crates/config/src/boot_config.rs at v12.17.0). A config dependency cannot be delegated bootConfig (configIncludes.notForDependencies). Config dependencies pinned with version+integrity keep that pin (docs/config-dependencies.md). depcurfew neither writes nor checks it. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/docs/config-includes.md)
- `extra.pnpmfiles`: hooks.updateConfig "Allows you to modify the configuration settings used by pnpm" and "runs after the settings are merged and can still change any of them" (config-includes.md); since v12.4.1 it receives the resolved configuration, and since v12.8.0 only a setting given on the command line wins over it. Added in 10.8.0 ("Experimental. A new hook is supported for updating configuration settings. The hook can be provided via .pnpmfile.cjs", pnpm/CHANGELOG.md at v10.34.9). The project pnpmfile sits next to the lockfile (the workspace root): .pnpmfile.cjs since 6.0.0 ("pnpmfile.js renamed to .pnpmfile.cjs"); since 11.0.0 .pnpmfile.mjs, which "takes priority over .pnpmfile.cjs when present" (11.0.0 release notes). When the pnpmfile setting is set, also to [], pnpm does not look for these files ("Set pnpmfile: [] in pnpm-workspace.yaml when the workspace has no pnpmfile, so a new .pnpmfile.mjs is not picked up automatically", config-includes.md); its paths are relative to the file that sets it. globalPnpmfile is loaded first. ignorePnpmfile: true loads no pnpmfile, those of config-dependency plugins included: cli/cli-utils/src/getConfig.ts at v10.34.9, pnpm11/pnpm/src/getConfig.ts at v11.28.10 (installConfigDepsAndLoadHooks, tryLoadDefaultPnpmfile = config.pnpmfile == null), pnpm/crates/hooks/src/finder.rs (find_pnpmfiles) and pnpm/crates/cli/src/config_deps/hooks.rs (resolve_pnpmfile_paths, may_update_config) at v12.17.0; pnpm 12 does not take ignorePnpmfile from the global config.yaml (workspace_scope.rs). With sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false each project also runs the pnpmfile in its own directory (pnpmfile.md). ignoreScripts does not stop any of them (installScripts.disableAll). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/docs/pnpmfile.md)
- `extra.configPlugins`: "If your config dependency is named following the pnpm-plugin-\*, @\*/pnpm-plugin-\*, or @pnpm/plugin-\* pattern, pnpm will automatically load its pnpmfile.mjs (falling back to pnpmfile.cjs) from the package root." 10.13.0: "pnpm will now automatically load the pnpmfile.cjs file from any config dependency named @pnpm/plugin-\* or pnpm-plugin-\*"; 10.15.0: "Automatically load pnpmfiles from config dependencies that are named @\*/pnpm-plugin-\*" (pnpm/CHANGELOG.md at v10.34.9). The test is a prefix pnpm-plugin- or @pnpm/plugin-, or a scoped name containing /pnpm-plugin- (isPluginName in cli/cli-utils/src/getConfig.ts at v10.34.9 and pnpm11/pnpm/src/getConfig.ts at v11.28.10, is_plugin_name in pnpm/crates/hooks/src/finder.rs at v12.17.0). Such a pnpmfile loads also when the package supplies settings through include ("A config dependency whose name follows the plugin naming pattern still loads its pnpmfile", config-includes.md), unless ignorePnpmfile is true (extra.pnpmfiles). Config dependencies came in 10.0.0 ("configurational dependencies", then in the pnpm field of package.json); the docs of 10.x, 11.x and 12.17.0 declare them in pnpm-workspace.yaml. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.17.0/pnpm/docs/config-dependencies.md)
- `extra.knownPlugins`: The official plugin's updateConfig sets minimumReleaseAge: 1 \* 24 \* 60 ("1 day in minutes") and blockExoticSubdeps: true with Object.assign, so it replaces a longer delay of pnpm-workspace.yaml. Versions 0.1.0 to 0.2.1 (the pnpmfile.cjs of the published packages on registry.npmjs.org) set neither; 0.3.0, published on 2026-03-01, is the latest. pnpm/docs/pnpmfile.md at v12.17.0 names it as the example of the hook. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/plugin-better-defaults/blob/v0.3.0/src/pnpmfile.cjs)

### Yarn (Berry)

- `cooldown.configFiles`: Also YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE (general YARN\_ env rule) and, since 4.17.0, npmScopes.\<scope>.npmMinimalAgeGate. package.json cannot set it. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc)
- `cooldown.unit`: npmMinimalAgeGate is a DURATION setting with unit: DurationUnit.MINUTES, and parseDuration (yarnpkg-core miscUtils.ts) takes a number without a unit in that unit, so bare numbers are minutes. Since 4.11.0 duration strings with ms, s, m, h, d or w (e.g. 3d, 1w) also work; on 4.10.x a string such as 7d silently had no effect. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-npm/sources/index.ts)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: The setting arrived in 4.10.0 (release notes, pull request and source; the security docs page at https://yarnpkg.com/features/security says 4.12). 4.10.2 fixed it: "Bust the metadata cache" (#6908) and "support registries without publish times using minimalAgeGate" (#6907). On 2026-10-29 Yarn 4.10.1 with npmMinimalAgeGate: 4320 refused zod@3.23.8 and esbuild@0.25.0, both over a year old ("No candidates found"), while 4.10.2, 4.10.3, 4.11.0 and 4.12.0 installed them and refused a version 4 hours old. depcurfew writes the setting from 4.10.2 on. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/releases/tag/%40yarnpkg%2Fcli%2F4.10.2)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Workspace scripts still run. Upgraded projects with an old lockfile get enableScripts: true written to .yarnrc.yml. Yarn 1 runs scripts unless --ignore-scripts is passed. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/releases/tag/%40yarnpkg%2Fcli%2F4.14.0)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: Root package.json only; ignored inside workspaces. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/manifest#dependenciesMeta)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Set in .yarnrc.yml; the default since 4.14.0. yarn install --mode=skip-build skips builds for one run. Berry ignores YARN_IGNORE_SCRIPTS. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc#enableScripts)
