- `sources.git.default`: Upgraded projects with an old lockfile get ["\*\*"] written to .yarnrc.yml. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/docusaurus/static/configuration/yarnrc.json)
- `project.lockfiles`: Yarn Classic uses the same name; see berryLockfileMarker and classicLockfileHeader to tell them apart. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-fslib/sources/path.ts)
- `project.workspaces`: Array of folder glob patterns. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/manifest#workspaces)
- `user.files`: Configuration.find adds .yarnrc.yml from the home folder (folderUtils.getHomeFolder: os.homedir(), else /usr/local/share) with the lowest priority, also for projects outside the home folder; the name stays .yarnrc.yml even when YARN_RC_FILENAME is set. The yarnrc page does not describe it; yarn config set -H writes the home file (https://yarnpkg.com/cli/config/set). The lookup is the same in 4.0.0, and the 2.2.0 changelog already speaks of the home configuration file; the first version was not tracked. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `user.settings`: Configuration.use knows no project-only settings, so the home file sets these wherever the version has them; the first versions are those of cooldown, cooldown.exclude and sources.git, and enableScripts is checked in 4.0.0. enableScripts: false denies every dependency build script (scriptsSwitch); buildsDeny is the closest purpose, since Yarn has no strict mode. The allow-list dependenciesMeta.\<package>.built is read from the root package.json only (Project.getDependencyMeta), so Yarn has no user-level allow-list. depcurfew does not write npmScopes.\<scope>.npmMinimalAgeGate. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `user.unknownKeys`: Configuration.use sets a key it does not know aside without an error when it comes from the home file, even with enableStrictSettings; other files throw. The 2.2.0 changelog: "Unsupported options will simply be silently ignored." [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `extra.environmentNames`: getEnvironmentSettings lowercases every name of process.env and takes those that start with yarn\_ (ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX), and getRcFilename compares the lowercased name with yarn_rc_filename, so yarn_enable_scripts and Yarn_Enable_Scripts set enableScripts as YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS does (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `extra.registrySettings`: npmRegistryServer: "Define the registry to use when fetching packages"; npmScopes: "Per-scope registry configurations", whose entries take npmRegistryServer ("See npmRegistryServer"), keyed by the scope without @. "While Yarn will automatically find them in the parent directories, they should usually be kept at the root of your project". Yarn (Berry) does not read registry= from .npmrc. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc)
- `extra.yamlMergeKeys`: parseSyml reads .yarnrc.yml with load of js-yaml and FAILSAFE_SCHEMA, which has no merge type (only strings, sequences and maps), so \<\<: \*defaults is an ordinary key named \<\<: Configuration.use rejects it as an unrecognized setting in a project .yarnrc.yml (enableStrictSettings, default true) and sets it aside in the home file, so merged values never apply. Every scalar is a string to Yarn, which parses it per setting (parseValue in packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-parsers/sources/syml.ts)
- `extra.classicUserFile`: Yarn Classic (1.x, last release 1.22.22) reads .yarnrc and .npmrc from the project, its parent folders, the home folder (homeConfigLoc = \~/.yarnrc) and the global prefix (getPossibleConfigLocations in src/registries/npm-registry.js), and of .yarnrc.yml only yarnPath (yarnPathRuns), whose other settings only Yarn 2 and later read. depcurfew does not configure Yarn Classic. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/blob/v1.22.22/src/registries/yarn-registry.js)
- `extra.yarnPathRuns`: Yarn Classic 1.18.0 and later read yarnPath from .yarnrc.yml (CHANGELOG 1.18.0: "Adds support for reading yarnPath from v2-produced .yarnrc.yml files", #7350): getRcPaths in src/util/rc.js looks for .yarnrc and .yarnrc.yml in the folder and its parents, loadRcFile in src/rc.js keeps only yarnPath of a .yml file, resolved against its folder, and start() in src/cli/index.js runs node \<yarnPath> before anything else, also before the check that packageManager names Yarn 1 (which only main() does). Yarn 2 and later do the same (run and runYarnPath in packages/yarnpkg-cli/sources/lib.ts at @yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1), unless YARN_IGNORE_PATH is set. So a release committed under yarnPath is the Yarn that runs, whichever Yarn starts, with or without Corepack, and its version (from the file name, extra.yarnPath) is the version of the project (decision D-165). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/blob/v1.22.22/src/cli/index.js)
- `extra.setVersion`: setVersion saves the release as .yarn/releases/yarn-\<version>.cjs, points yarnPath of the project .yarnrc.yml to it (a path relative to the project) and sets packageManager of package.json to yarn@\<version>. In 4.18.1 it keeps yarnPath when the project already has one, when the release cannot be represented by Corepack, with --yarn-path or without Corepack enabled; otherwise it removes yarnPath and sets only packageManager. 3.6.4 always writes both (the same file at https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/3.6.4/packages/plugin-essentials/sources/commands/set/version.ts). The command runs in the Yarn yarnPath names, which is the one to upgrade. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-essentials/sources/commands/set/version.ts)
- `extra.classicLockfile`: Yarn Classic (1.22.22) reads yarn.lock with its own parser: a comment that says yarn lockfile v\<N> with N above LOCKFILE_VERSION 1 (src/constants.js) makes it throw "Can't install from a lockfile of version N"; indentation is two spaces per level (an odd count throws), keys and values are JSON strings in double quotes or words, several keys separated by commas share one value, key: value and key value both set a value, and a later key replaces an earlier one. A file with git conflict markers is read as its two sides, the second side winning per key (parseWithConflict). When the parser fails Yarn retries the file as YAML (FAILSAFE_SCHEMA), and a file with \_\_metadata (Yarn 2 and later) is ignored (src/lockfile/index.js). Each top-level key is a pattern name@range (normalizePattern), an npm: range names another package (registry-resolver.js: npm:\<name>@\<range>), and its value is an entry, or a string naming another pattern that Yarn follows (Lockfile.getLocked). Lockfile.getLockfile writes version, resolved and integrity of an entry, and its name only when it differs from the name of the pattern, which it never does. An entry with resolved is fetched from that URL without the part after # (explodeHashedUrl in src/util/version.js; getLocked in src/package-request.js), with git (git+\<protocol>:// or git://) for URLs that match gitResolved and from the disk for file: and relative paths (src/fetchers/tarball-fetcher.js), whatever its version field says; an entry without resolved is resolved again from its pattern. file:, link:, ./, ../ and absolute paths are local (file-resolver.js, link-resolver.js), whose entries have no resolved. depcurfew reads the name and version of a registry tarball URL as for package-lock.json (npm extra.tarballIdentity and lockfileFormat.registryTarball). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/blob/v1.22.22/src/lockfile/parse.js)
- `extra.denyList`: With built: false in the root package.json, Yarn reports that the build "has been explicitly disabled through configuration" as an info message instead of the warning that all build scripts are disabled; built: false also wins over enableScripts: true. Only the top-level manifest counts (CHANGELOG 2.0.0). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-pnp/sources/jsInstallUtils.ts)
- `extra.projectInstall`: The install command ("install the project dependencies") has the paths [\`install\`] and Command.Default, so yarn without a command installs too. yarn add (commandLine.add) adds packages. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-essentials/sources/commands/install.ts)
- `extra.commandLine`: dlx.ts (documented at https://yarnpkg.com/cli/dlx) downloads the package named by the command, or the ones given with -p/--package, into a temporary environment and runs it. create.ts (yarn create, not on yarnpkg.com) takes -p/--package as well and runs create-\<name>: @foo becomes @foo/create, @foo/app becomes @foo/create-app, foo becomes create-foo, and a name that already matches ^create(-|$) is kept (so is create alone). yarn add (https://yarnpkg.com/cli/add) takes packages as arguments; of its options only --mode takes a value. yarn workspace \<workspaceName> \<commandName> … runs a command within that workspace, e.g. yarn workspace components add -D react (https://yarnpkg.com/cli/workspace). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/tree/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-dlx/sources/commands)
- `extra.runnerOptions`: Clipanion, the command-line parser of Yarn, registers the options of a command with a path also before that path ("We allow options to be specified before the path"), so yarn -p x dlx y and yarn --package=x dlx y download x, as yarn dlx -p x y does; the words after the command go to it (Option.Proxy in packages/plugin-dlx/sources/commands/dlx.ts). lib/core.js of clipanion 4.0.0-rc.2, the version yarn.lock of @yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1 resolves, does the same; Clipanion has no release tags for its 4.0.0 releases, so the source is the commit of master that is 4.0.0-rc.4. Yarn passes its command line to Clipanion after taking a leading --cwd (checkCwd in packages/yarnpkg-cli/sources/lib.ts at @yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1). Decision D-160. [↗](https://github.com/arcanis/clipanion/blob/434b5a6e0063c58b5e2f0a62498a7de0b308308f/sources/core.ts)
- `extra.packageSpecs`: Protocols besides npm: and git: exec:, file:, jsr:, link:, patch:, portal: and workspace:. link: connects an external directory (https://yarnpkg.com/protocol/link), portal: a relative path to a package folder (https://yarnpkg.com/protocol/portal) and file: copies a folder or tarball. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/protocols)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: Environment variables that start with yarn\_ (any case) set the setting named by the camel-cased rest, so YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER sets npmRegistryServer, the registry packages are fetched from (https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc#npmRegistryServer). getRcFilename reads yarn_rc_filename (any case) as the name of the configuration file instead of .yarnrc.yml. npmScopes, an object, cannot be set this way. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `extra.registryFetch`: Yarn fetches a registry package of yarn.lock by its resolution: getLocatorUrl builds \<registry>/\<name>/-/\<name>-\<version>.tgz from the name of the locator and the version after npm:, cleaned by semverUtils.clean (packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/semverUtils.ts, which drops leading spaces, v and = and trailing spaces and keeps pre-release and build), and supports only a reference whose part before ? semver.valid accepts. The version field of the entry goes into the package Yarn builds from the lockfile (setupResolutions in packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Project.ts) and is not used for the fetch. A patch: locator wraps the locator it patches, URL-encoded, up to #. An npm: reference with an \_\_archiveUrl parameter is fetched from that URL instead (NpmHttpFetcher.ts). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-npm/sources/NpmSemverFetcher.ts)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Each entry has resolution: name@\<locator>: npm:\<version> for the registry, \<repository>#commit=\<sha> for git (GitHub shortcuts become https://github.com/\<owner>/\<repo>.git), an http(s) URL for tarballs, file:\<path> (a .tgz or .tar.gz path is a tarball, anything else a directory), portal: and link: for directories, workspace: for workspace packages, and patch: around the URL-encoded original locator. No field records install scripts; dependenciesMeta.built: false is a user opt-out. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/@yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Project.ts)
- `extra.durationStrings`: The 4.11.0 release notes list "Core: Create DURATION settings type" (#6942): npmMinimalAgeGate accepts a number followed by ms, s, m, h, d or w (e.g. 3d, 1w) since 4.11.0 (the pattern ^(\\d\*\\.?\\d+)(ms|s|m|h|d|w)?$ in the settings schema at 4.18.1); on 4.10.x such a string silently had no effect. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/releases/tag/%40yarnpkg%2Fcli%2F4.11.0)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Name globs such as @scope/\* or package\* in npmPreapprovedPackages. [↗](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc#npmPreapprovedPackages)
- `extra.classicLockfileHeader`: Written as # yarn lockfile v${LOCKFILE_VERSION} with LOCKFILE_VERSION = 1 (src/constants.js). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/blob/v1.22.22/src/lockfile/stringify.js)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Yarn 6 is still in preview. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/releases/tag/%40yarnpkg%2Fcli%2F4.18.1)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: checkCwd takes --cwd \<dir> or --cwd=\<dir> only as the first argument ("argv[0] === \`--cwd\`", "argv[0].startsWith(\`--cwd=\`)"), and for yarn add also as the last two words ("argv[0] === \`add\` && argv[argv.length - 2] === \`--cwd\`"; "CRA adds \`--cwd\` at the end of the command"), removes them and runs the command with cli.defaultContext.cwd = ppath.resolve(cwd). Yarn finds the project and its .yarnrc.yml files from that directory. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-cli/sources/lib.ts)
- `extra.configCommands`: plugin-essentials registers config get, config set and config unset next to config (commands/config/\*.ts at 4.18.1). yarn config set updates the project configuration, or the home configuration with -H/--home (commands/config/set.ts); yarn config and yarn config get only print settings (commands/config.ts: "This command prints the current active configuration settings"). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-essentials/sources/index.ts)
- `extra.installOverrides`: yarn add declares noTimeGate = Option.Boolean(\`--no-time-gate\`), "Disable the minimum release age check for this command" (plugin-essentials/sources/commands/add.ts at 4.18.1). getEnvironmentSettings lowercases every environment variable, keeps those starting with yarn\_ and camel-cases the rest into a setting (ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX), so YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE sets npmMinimalAgeGate, YARN_NPM_PREAPPROVED_PACKAGES npmPreapprovedPackages and YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS enableScripts; the values that keep scripts off are those of user.variables. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts)
- `extra.perScopeGate`: getMinimalAgeGate: for a scoped package, a number in npmScopes.\<scope>.npmMinimalAgeGate (the scope name without @) replaces the global gate, longer or shorter, and 0 turns the gate off for that scope (acceptance tests "npmScopes override" in features/npmMinimalAgeGate.test.ts at 4.18.1; the code is the same in 4.17.0 and absent in 4.16.0). Each npmScopes entry is a shape whose unset properties get their defaults (parseShape and getDefaultValue in yarnpkg-core Configuration.ts), so a scope listed only for its registry gets the default of 1d (scopablePackageGateSettings in plugin-npm index.ts) instead of the global gate; read from the code, no test covers that case. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-npm/sources/npmConfigUtils.ts)
- `extra.upgradeMigration`: LOCKFILE_MIGRATION_RULES: a lockfile of version below 9 gets approvedGitRepositories ["\*\*"] and enableScripts true, below 10 npmMinimalAgeGate 0, each only when no configuration source sets the key (configuration.sources.get(rule.name) === undefined), saved with Configuration.updateConfiguration ("Migrated your project to the latest Yarn version"). Explicit values written by depcurfew prevent the migration. [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-essentials/sources/commands/install.ts)
- `extra.missingPublishTime`: shouldBeQuarantined: with a gate, a version whose publish time is missing from the registry document (publishTimes?.[version] undefined) is quarantined; since 4.10.2 ("fix: support registries without publish times using minimalAgeGate", #6907). [↗](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/plugin-npm/sources/npmConfigUtils.ts)

### Bun

- `cooldown.configFiles`: Also the global $HOME/.bunfig.toml or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml; local keys override global ones. Bun's .npmrc support has no min-release-age key. [↗](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: bun install, add and update; bunx honors it only since 1.4.4. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.3.0/docs/cli/install.md)
- `cooldown.unit`: Plain numbers are seconds; 0 turns it off. Since 1.4.4 duration strings such as 90m, 12 hours, 3d or 2 weeks also work (the bunfig reference still documents seconds only). [↗](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#install-minimumreleaseage)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: Since 1.4.4 --minimum-release-age-excludes replaces the bunfig list for one command. [↗](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4#minimumreleaseage-supports-units-and-per-version-exclusions)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Dependency scripts run only for Bun's built-in trusted list (npm-registry packages only since 1.4) or trustedDependencies; the root project's scripts run. First version of this policy not tracked. [↗](https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle#trusteddependencies)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: Replaces the built-in default list rather than extending it. bun pm trust and bun add --trust write it. [↗](https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle#trusteddependencies)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Default false. Also --ignore-scripts or ignore-scripts=true in .npmrc. Skips the project's own scripts and trustedDependencies too. [↗](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#install-ignorescripts)
- `project.workspaces`: Full glob syntax, including ! patterns. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/docs/pm/workspaces.mdx)
- `project.workspacesObjectKey`: The object form also holds catalog and catalogs. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/docs/pm/catalogs.mdx)
- `user.files`: Since 1.4.4 get_home_config_path takes the first of XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME that is a fully qualified path ("The XDG specification says to ignore $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when it is empty or a relative path"; docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx at 1.4.4: "When XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set to an absolute path, Bun reads the file there and not the one in $HOME"); HOME is USERPROFILE on Windows (src/bun_core/env_var.rs). Before 1.4.4 Bun uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME whenever it is set, also to an empty or relative value (XDG_CONFIG_HOME.get().or_else(HOME) in src/bunfig/arguments.rs at bun-v1.4.3; the same in 1.4.0 and, in Zig, getHomeConfigPath in src/cli/Arguments.zig at bun-v1.3.0 and bun-v1.3.14), and joins it with join_abs_string_buf, which puts a / in place of the first character of a value without a leading separator (\_joinAbsStringBuf in src/resolver/resolve_path.zig at bun-v1.3.0, src/paths/resolve_path.rs at bun-v1.4.0): XDG_CONFIG_HOME=cfg gives /fg/.bunfig.toml, an empty value /bunfig.toml, so Bun then reads neither the file below the current directory nor \~/.bunfig.toml. Only one file is read, with no fallback when the XDG one is missing. Only package manager commands read it (bun install, add, remove, update, pm, bunx and so on), before the project bunfig.toml, whose keys win. 1.2.0 already reads it; the first version was not tracked. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/bunfig/arguments.rs)
- `user.settings`: parse_install reads both from the user file as from bunfig.toml (only globalDir and globalBinDir are user-only), as in 1.3.0 (bunfig.zig). trustedDependencies exists only in package.json and bunfig has no such key, so Bun has no user-level allow-list; install.ignoreScripts only turns scripts off. Write whole seconds: duration strings need 1.4.4. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/bunfig/bunfig.rs)
- `user.unknownKeys`: The parser looks up only the keys it knows (install_obj.get), so another key, such as install.minimumReleaseAge before 1.3.0, is neither read nor reported. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/bunfig/bunfig.rs)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: load_global_bunfig ends the process through report_bunfig_load_failure when the user file has a value Bun cannot read, e.g. minimumReleaseAge = "3d" before 1.4.4 ("Expected number of seconds for minimumReleaseAge"), so every package manager command fails; 1.3.0 crashed the same way. A file Bun cannot read at all is skipped. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/bunfig/arguments.rs)
- `user.weakening`: Both files fill one set of options, the user file first, so a key in the project bunfig.toml replaces the user value; an empty minimumReleaseAgeExcludes list is skipped, so a project's [] does not clear the user list. 0 turns the delay off (src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerOptions.rs keeps only values above 0). The command line beats both files. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/bunfig/bunfig.rs)
- `extra.environmentNames`: Options::load looks up BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY, NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY and npm_config_registry with env.get, each spelling as written; the map behind env.get (HashTable in src/dotenv/env_loader.rs, https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/dotenv/env_loader.rs) is a StringArrayHashMap outside Windows and a CaseInsensitiveAsciiStringArrayHashMap on Windows, where names are not told apart by case. Decision D-143. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerOptions.rs)
- `extra.registrySettings`: "Put bunfig.toml in your project root, alongside your package.json"; the global $HOME/.bunfig.toml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml) is loaded too, and local keys win. "The default registry is https://registry.npmjs.org/. To change it": [install] registry, a string or { url, token }. "To configure a registry for a particular scope (for example, @myorg/\<package>), use install.scopes": a key per scope (myorg = "https://registry.myorg.com/" or a table with url). [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx)
- `extra.projectInstall`: "if your project has a package.json, you can use bun install"; the page names no alias, so none is listed. bun add (commandLine.add) adds packages. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/da867c60bf0bcbf9d6d36994f8ca0efa42075115/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx)
- `extra.commandLine`: Options of bun add (snippets/cli/add.mdx) and bunx (snippets/cli/bunx.mdx) typed string or number; --catalog takes its name only after =. -p is --package for bunx but the flag --production for bun add, so it is listed with bunx only. The short forms -F (--filter) and -c (--config) of bun add are left out because bunx does not document them, and an option wrongly read as taking a value would hide the package after it. bunx is an alias for bun x (docs/pm/bunx.mdx). bun create \<template> runs the create-\<template> package from npm unless a local template has that name; it also takes GitHub repositories and local paths (docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx). [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/tree/da867c60bf0bcbf9d6d36994f8ca0efa42075115/docs/snippets/cli)
- `extra.runnerOptions`: bun x reads every option before the package name, also those before x: Options::parse gets the command line after bun, with x as the subcommand name, and takes --package \<name>, --package=\<name>, -p \<name> and -p=\<name> wherever they stand before it, so bun --package=x x y and bun -p=x x y download x. bun finds its command by skipping each word that starts with - (which in src/runtime/cli/mod.rs at bun-v1.4.4), so in bun --package x x y it takes the value x for the command, and bun x runs only when that value is x. Decision D-160. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/runtime/cli/bunx_command.rs)
- `extra.commandNames`: Command::which compares the first word that does not start with - with each name as written (RootCommandMatcher::case, no prefixes and no other case): add and a run AddCommand, create and c CreateCommand (bun_create, which reads the word after the command word as the template whatever the command word was, so bun c foo runs bunx create-foo), install and i InstallCommand, or AddCommand with -g or --global anywhere on the line, ci InstallCommand, update and up, r, remove, rm and uninstall, build and bun; deploy, cloud, config, use, auth, login and logout are reserved, whoami and list run bun pm. Any other word runs a script, a file or a binary of the project (AutoCommand). AddCommand runs the same Subcommand::Add whichever word chose it (src/runtime/cli/add_command.rs). Decision D-162. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/runtime/cli/mod.rs)
- `extra.packageSpecs`: Git dependencies: "Bun supports a variety of protocols, including github, git, git+ssh, and git+https", with the examples git@github.com:moment/moment.git and github:colinhacks/zod. Tarball URLs, local folders and local .tgz files are accepted too. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/da867c60bf0bcbf9d6d36994f8ca0efa42075115/docs/pm/cli/add.mdx)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: bun add takes --registry and --config (-c), a configuration file (snippets/cli/add.mdx). BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY sets the npm registry and environment variables take priority over bunfig.toml (pm/cli/install.mdx). [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/tree/da867c60bf0bcbf9d6d36994f8ca0efa42075115/docs)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: bun.lock (text, the default since 1.2) maps each package to a tuple starting with name@\<spec>: name@\<version> followed by the registry for npm, name@git+\<repo>#\<sha> and name@github:\<owner>/\<repo>#\<sha> for git, name@https://… for tarball URLs, name@./x.tgz (without file:) for local tarballs, name@file:\<dir> and name@link:\<dir> for directories, name@workspace:\<dir> for workspace packages. The info object carries hasInstallScript: true only since 1.4.4, with no lockfileVersion change, so a missing flag proves nothing for older files. bun.lockb is an undocumented binary format. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/install/lockfile/bun.lock.rs)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Since 1.4.4 minimumReleaseAge also takes duration strings such as 90m, 12 hours, 3d or 2 weeks; plain numbers stay seconds. [↗](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4#minimumreleaseage-supports-units-and-per-version-exclusions)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: minimumReleaseAgeExcludes takes exact package names (and name@version since 1.4.4), no wildcards. [↗](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4#minimumreleaseage-supports-units-and-per-version-exclusions)
- `extra.trustedDependenciesReplacesDefaults`: So an empty list trusts no package: without the field Bun 1.4.4 ran esbuild's postinstall (esbuild is on the built-in list); with "trustedDependencies": [] it blocked it (bun pm untrusted listed it), tested on 2026-10-29. [↗](https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle#behavior-of-the-trusteddependencies-field)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: bun add: \<ParamField path="--cwd" type="string"> "Set a specific current working directory" (Global Configuration & Context); bun install has the same option, "Set a specific cwd" (docs/snippets/cli/install.mdx at the same tag, General Configuration). [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/docs/snippets/cli/add.mdx)
- `extra.installOverrides`: bun add @types/bun --minimum-release-age 259200 # seconds: "A number is in seconds", or a number with a unit such as 90m, 12 hours, 3d or 2 weeks (durationStrings). The page lists no environment variable for it. bun add --trust "adds the package to trustedDependencies in the project's package.json and installs it", so its lifecycle scripts run (docs/snippets/cli/add.mdx and docs/pm/lifecycle.mdx at bun-v1.4.4); lifecycle.mdx names no variable that turns scripts on, and ignore-scripts read from the environment "only turns scripts off". [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx)

### Deno

- `cooldown.setting`: A number or string, or the object form { "age": ..., "exclude": [...] }. Covers npm and JSR packages. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/deno_json/#minimum-dependency-age)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: min-release-age in .npmrc since 2.8; also NPM_CONFIG_MIN_RELEASE_AGE. This page does not state precedence; denoland/deno#35458 gives CLI flag, deno.json, .npmrc, environment, built-in default. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/packages/supply_chain/#minimum-dependency-age)
- `cooldown.fileSettings`: NpmRc::parse reads min-release-age "in days" (min_release_age_days: Option\<u64>; "npm interprets the value as a number of days"), the same in the .npmrc next to package.json or deno.json and in the home one (discover_npmrc in libs/resolver/npmrc.rs at v2.9.8); deno.json and --minimum-dependency-age take minutes (unit). [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/npmrc/lib.rs)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: Alias --min-dep-age since 2.9.3. deno install honors it since 2.5.5; deno add, deno remove and deno x since 2.9.4. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/deno_json/#minimum-dependency-age)
- `cooldown.unit`: Numbers are minutes; strings may be an ISO-8601 duration (P3D, PT72H), an absolute date or an RFC3339 timestamp; 0 turns it off. The .npmrc format differs (see npmrcFormat). [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `cooldown.default`: Since 2.9 a 24-hour minimum applies when nothing is configured; set 0 to turn it off. Whether the default covers JSR is not stated. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/deno_json/#minimum-dependency-age)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: Before 2.9.2 wildcard entries were stored literally and never matched. No CLI flag or .npmrc key for exclusions. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: npm lifecycle scripts run only when approved, and only with a node_modules directory. deno x / dx runs them after its download prompt is accepted. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/install/)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: deno approve-scripts writes it. --allow-scripts=npm:pkg on the CLI exists since 1.45. [↗](https://deno.com/blog/v2.6#granular-control-over-postinstall-scripts-with-deno-approve-scripts)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: Must be set at the workspace root. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/examples/npm_lifecycle_scripts_tutorial/)
- `sources.git.setting`: git+https: and git+ssh: dependencies are not supported in package.json. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/examples/local_unpublished_packages_tutorial/#what-is-not-supported)
- `sources.remoteTarball.setting`: Tarball URL dependencies are not supported in package.json. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/examples/local_unpublished_packages_tutorial/#what-is-not-supported)
- `sources.file.setting`: No setting. Since 2.8 file: and link: entries are silently skipped (scope disputed, see fileLinkSkipped); deno.json "links" overrides dependencies with local packages. [↗](https://docs.deno.com/examples/local_unpublished_packages_tutorial/#what-is-not-supported)
- `sources.directory.setting`: No setting; local directories behave like file: and link: entries (see fileLinkSkipped). [↗](https://docs.deno.com/examples/local_unpublished_packages_tutorial/#what-is-not-supported)
- `project.lockfiles`: The default location; lock.path in deno.json can move it and "lock": false turns it off. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/docs/blob/main/runtime/reference/deno_json.md)
- `project.workspaces`: Paths of members; globs and ! exclusions since Deno 2.1. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/docs/blob/main/runtime/fundamentals/workspaces.md)
- `user.files`: Deno has no user configuration file of its own (deno.json is looked up from the working directory upwards). It reads .npmrc next to package.json or deno.json and in the home directory (HOME, USERPROFILE on Windows), not the file named by NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG and not under XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Home discovery arrived in 1.45.0 (#24021); since 2.1.8 (#27119) the project and home files are merged key by key, before that a project .npmrc hid the home one (Releases.md). This is the \~/.npmrc that npm reads. A home .npmrc Deno may not read is skipped; one that does not parse stops the command. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/resolver/npmrc.rs)
- `user.settings`: 2.8.0: "feat(npmrc): support min-release-age (#33983)". A whole number of days (cooldownUnit); the same line sets npm's min-release-age, also in days. minimumDependencyAge.exclude and allowScripts exist only in deno.json (allowScripts at the workspace root), so Deno has no user-level exclusions or script settings. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/Releases.md)
- `user.cooldownUnit`: NpmRc::parse reads min-release-age "in days" (min_release_age_days: Option\<u64>; "npm interprets the value as a number of days"): an INI number of 0 or more, or a text that parses as a whole number after ${VAR} expansion; anything else, such as 72h or 1.5, is ignored without a message, so the age comes from the next source. The project .npmrc wins over the home file (libs/resolver/npmrc.rs), and the days count only where deno.json and --min-dep-age set nothing; those take minutes, an ISO-8601 duration or an RFC 3339 date (libs/config/util.rs, libs/cli_parser/src/defs.rs). [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/npmrc/lib.rs)
- `user.unknownKeys`: NpmRc::parse reads registry, auth, replace-registry-host, min-release-age and trust-policy keys and skips every other key without a message. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/npmrc/lib.rs)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: A min-release-age that is not a whole number of days, such as 72h, is ignored without a message (test "invalid value is ignored"), so the age silently comes from the next source. A home .npmrc that does not parse at all stops the command (libs/resolver/npmrc.rs). [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/npmrc/lib.rs)
- `user.weakening`: The age comes from the command line, then minimumDependencyAge in deno.json, then .npmrc (the project file over the home file), then NPM_CONFIG_MIN_RELEASE_AGE, then the built-in 1440 minutes; 0 from .npmrc turns it off (apply_minimum_dependency_age_fallbacks). The same line turns npm's delay off too. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/resolver/factory.rs)
- `extra.denyList`: The object form "allowScripts": { "allow": [...], "deny": ["npm:pkg"] } (schema since 2.6.0: "List of npm package constraints to deny running lifecycle scripts for"); deny beats allow, and a denied package is not added to the packages whose scripts were not run, so Deno does not warn about it. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/npm_installer/lifecycle_scripts.rs)
- `extra.commandLine`: install.md: deno install [PACKAGES] installs packages and adds them to deno.json or package.json, deno add is its alias, deno install --global installs a package or script as a binary, and deno install --entrypoint (-e) [FILES] installs what the files use. -n/--name, --root, --os and --arch take a value; --allow-scripts and --node-modules-dir are shown with =. Since Deno 2.8 a name without a prefix is an npm package; JSR packages need jsr: (add.md). x.md: deno x runs a package from npm or JSR without installing it, like npx (deno x npm:create-vite my-app); --package (-p) names the package when the binary differs (deno x -p typescript tsc), and npm:\<package>/\<binary> picks one binary; deno x --install-alias creates the dx alias. In Deno 2.9.8 (github.com/denoland/deno, cli/args/flags.rs) an executable whose name ends in dx, denox or dnx runs as deno x, and libs/cli_parser/src/defs.rs (X_SUBCOMMAND with COMPILE_ARGS, PERMISSION_ARGS, RUNTIME_MISC_ARGS and INSPECT_ARGS) gives the options of deno x that take a separate value; the permission flags take theirs after =. -L/--log-level is a global option with a value. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/docs/tree/74beb7585f7e798fe0bc8d867295bff23fc2e38e/runtime/reference/cli)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: deno.lock version 5 (the default since Deno 2.3) marks npm packages with lifecycle scripts as scripts: true (hasInstallScript from the registry or a preinstall, install or postinstall script, libs/npm/resolution/graph.rs); version 4 has no such field. An npm key is name@version, followed by \_ and the versions of its peer dependencies when it has some: libs/lockfile/lib.rs takes the part before the first \_ as name@version (key.split_once('\_')). tarball is written only for registries other than the default one. Deno rejects git and http(s) dependencies in package.json and keeps file: dependencies out of the lockfile. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/libs/lockfile/printer.rs)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Strings are ISO-8601 durations (P3D, PT72H), an absolute date or an RFC3339 timestamp; the last two set a fixed cut-off instead of a delay. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `extra.ageObjectKey`: In the object form of minimumDependencyAge, age holds the delay and exclude the exemptions. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: A trailing \* matches by prefix (npm:@scope/\*) since 2.9.2; earlier wildcard entries never matched. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `extra.npmSpecifierPrefix`: Exclusions and allowScripts entries name npm packages as npm:\<name>. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `extra.allowAllScripts`: allowScripts: true allows every npm lifecycle script. Only the JSON value true does: to_allow_scripts_config (libs/config/deno_json/mod.rs at v2.9.8) gives every package for true, none for false and null, and stops with "expected string array, boolean, or object" for a string or a number, so "true" or 1 cannot turn it on silently. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.9.8/cli/schemas/config-file.v1.json)
- `extra.installOverrides`: deno install --minimum-dependency-age=P3D: deno.json and the flag accept an ISO-8601 duration such as P3D or PT72H, or an integer of minutes, and 0 turns it off; --min-dep-age is its alias (cooldown.cliFlag). deno install --allow-scripts=\<packages> lets those packages run their lifecycle scripts, which Deno does not run by default (runtime/reference/cli/install.md in denoland/docs). [↗](https://github.com/denoland/docs/blob/main/runtime/packages/supply_chain.md)

### uv

- `cooldown.setting`: Limits candidate packages to those uploaded before a date or, since 0.9.17, a duration ago. Compared with the upload time of each file, not the release date. false turns off a value from a lower-priority source (since 0.11.24). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: Top level of uv.toml or the [tool.uv] table of pyproject.toml. uv searches the current directory and its parents and uses the first directory with uv.toml or a pyproject.toml that has [tool.uv]; uv.toml wins over [tool.uv] in the same directory, with a warning. In a workspace only the root is read. User (\~/.config/uv/uv.toml) and system (/etc/uv/uv.toml) files are merged below the project file; uv tool and uvx read only those. UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER overrides the files. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: Also the UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER environment variable. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `cooldown.unit`: A "friendly" duration such as 24 hours, 1 week or 30 days, or an ISO 8601 duration such as P7D; months and years are rejected, a day is always 24 hours. An RFC 3339 timestamp is a fixed cutoff instead of a rolling delay. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/resolution.md)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: Durations ("dependency cooldowns") since 0.9.17; before that exclude-newer took only dates, which do not move with time. Tested on 2026-10-30: uv 0.9.16 printed a warning that "100000 days" is not a date and resolved with no delay at all; 0.9.17 and later held back every version. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/changelogs/0.9.x.md#0917)
- `cooldown.default`: No default: without a value every upload time is accepted. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: A table mapping package names to false (exempt), a date or a duration; package values take precedence over the global and index values. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/resolution.md)
- `cooldown.exclude.availableSince`: The table exists since 0.8.4 (dates); false, which exempts a package, since 0.9.25. Tested on 2026-10-30: with a false entry, uv 0.9.17 warned "data did not match any variant of untagged enum" and ignored the whole [tool.uv] table, the delay included; 0.9.25 and 0.13.6 exempted the package. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/changelogs/0.9.x.md#0925)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: Keys are package names, compared after name normalization. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: no-build defaults to false: source distributions, git and directory dependencies are built, which runs their build backend. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: With no-build = true, the packages in no-binary-package are the only ones built from source ("Allow \`all\` to be overridden by specific binary exclusions"). Their wheels are not used, so they are always built. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-configuration/src/build_options.rs)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: Or uv.toml; the same table as exclude-newer. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: Project settings no-build, no-build-package, no-binary and no-binary-package; uv sync and related commands respect them since 0.4.6. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/changelogs/0.2.x.md#0212)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Operations that need to build a source distribution fail. Workspace members, editable requirements and wheels built earlier and kept in the cache are still used. With uv 0.13.6 on 2026-10-30, uv sync refused a git dependency and a non-editable local directory dependency as well ("marked as --no-build but has no binary distribution"), so those need an exception too. An explicit no-build = false in a higher-priority file makes uv ignore no-build-package. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `project.lockfiles`: Created next to pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/projects/layout.md)
- `project.workspaces`: The [tool.uv.workspace] table of the root pyproject.toml lists members and exclude (globs or paths); exclude wins over members, and the root is a member too. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/projects/workspaces.md)
- `project.workspacesObjectKey`: The workspace guide calls members required, while the settings reference (crates/uv-workspace/src/pyproject.rs) gives it a default of []. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/projects/workspaces.md)
- `user.files`: User-level configuration is \<config dir>/uv/uv.toml: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/uv, else \~/.config/uv on Linux and macOS (not \~/Library), %APPDATA%\\uv, else uv in the Roaming AppData known folder, on Windows (FilesystemOptions::user in crates/uv-settings/src/lib.rs). The directory comes from the etcetera crate (crates/uv-dirs/src/lib.rs), which uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME only when it is an absolute path. Keys sit at the top level, as in [tool.uv] without the prefix; "User- and system-level configuration files cannot use the pyproject.toml format" (docs/concepts/configuration-files.md). The system file (/etc/uv/uv.toml, %PROGRAMDATA%\\uv\\uv.toml) is merged below it. Same path code at 0.9.0, 0.9.16 and 0.13.6; earlier versions are not tracked. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/reference/storage.md#configuration-directories)
- `user.settings`: Settings of uv.toml are merged with project-level configuration taking precedence over the user-level configuration: a project exclude-newer or no-build wins, exclude-newer-package tables are merged with the project keys winning, and lists such as no-build-package and no-binary-package are concatenated (crates/uv-settings/src/combine.rs). uv tool and uvx read only the user and system files, so the user file is the only file that gives them these settings; uv pip applies the top-level keys unless its [pip] table overrides them. The versions are those of the values depcurfew writes: a duration in exclude-newer since 0.9.17, package = false in exclude-newer-package since 0.9.25. no-build-package takes effect only while no-build is unset. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `user.unknownKeys`: uv.toml is parsed with deny_unknown_fields (OptionsWire), and fields allowed only in pyproject.toml (workspace, sources, dev-dependencies, conflicts, managed, package and others) are rejected by validate_uv_toml (crates/uv-settings/src/lib.rs, Error::PyprojectOnlyField); both are errors of the user file (see invalidValueFails). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: FilesystemOptions::user() returns nothing only for a missing, not-a-directory or unreadable file; a TOML or schema error (Error::UvToml) is passed on, and crates/uv/src/lib.rs stops every command that reads configuration with it, unlike an invalid pyproject.toml, which is only warned about. So a value the installed uv does not know (a duration before 0.9.17, package = false before 0.9.25, exclude-newer = false before 0.11.24) breaks every uv command instead of being dropped. A required-version mismatch is reported before a schema error. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/lib.rs)
- `user.weakening`: Tables are merged with the project keys winning, lists are extended and scalars come from the project when it sets them (combine.rs); with no-build = false, NoBuild::from_args ignores the package list (crates/uv-configuration/src/build_options.rs). exclude-newer = false (since 0.11.24) turns off a value from a lower-priority source, the system file included. Read from the code, not run: a [pip] exclude-newer in the user file is combined above the top-level keys for uv pip, so it can override a project exclude-newer there, and a user [[index]] with exclude-newer = false (preview, 0.11.5) exempts the packages of that index. The [pip] table configures "just the uv pip command line interface", and its settings win over the top-level ones there ("many of the settings in this section have corollaries in the top-level namespace which do apply to the uv pip interface unless they are overridden by a value in the uv.pip section", docs/concepts/configuration-files.md); PipOptions has exclude-newer (false disables it), exclude-newer-package, no-build and no-binary (a list, :all: for every package), and the top level no-binary = true builds every package from source (settings.rs). [pip] no-build = false weakens nothing: PipSettings::combine passes it to NoBuild::from_pip_args, which gives NoBuild::None (or the [pip] only-binary list) for false, and combines that with the top-level no-build and no-build-package (NoBuild::combine: All wins, None gives the other side), so it cannot turn the top-level no-build or no-build-package off; a project [tool.uv.pip] no-build wins over the user value anyway (crates/uv-cli/src/settings.rs and crates/uv-configuration/src/build_options.rs at 0.13.6, the same in crates/uv/src/settings.rs at 0.9.17). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/combine.rs)
- `user.variables`: "Settings provided via environment variables take precedence over persistent configuration, and settings provided via the command line take precedence over both" (docs/concepts/configuration-files.md). UV_NO_BUILD_PACKAGE since 0.6.5, UV_NO_BINARY and UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE since 0.5.30 (lists separated by spaces), UV_NO_CONFIG since 0.2.30, UV_CONFIG_FILE since 0.1.34. UV_NO_BUILD, UV_NO_BINARY and UV_NO_CONFIG are flags parsed with the BoolishValueParser of clap (crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs), whose true values are y, yes, t, true, on and 1 and false values n, no, f, false, off and 0, in any case (https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.7/clap_builder/src/util/str_to_bool.rs, the clap_builder version in the Cargo.lock of uv); a false value leaves the flag unset (flag() in crates/uv-cli/src/options.rs gives None), so the files decide (with UV_NO_BUILD=0 uv 0.11.32 still refused to build in a review test on 2026-10-31). XDG_CONFIG_HOME and APPDATA move the user directory (see files). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-static/src/env_vars.rs)
- `extra.environmentNames`: The options take their variables through clap (env = EnvVars::UV_PROJECT and the others), and clap_builder Arg::env reads the variable with env::var_os(name) (https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.7/clap_builder/src/builder/arg.rs, the clap_builder version in the Cargo.lock of uv), which outside Windows finds only that spelling, so uv_project sets nothing (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `extra.registrySettings`: ResolverInstallerSchema: index ("The package indexes to use when resolving dependencies", [[tool.uv.index]] with name and url), index-url ("The URL of the Python package index (by default: \<https://pypi.org/simple>)"), extra-index-url ("Extra URLs of package indexes to use, in addition to --index-url") and find-links ("Locations to search for candidate distributions, in addition to those found in the registry indexes"); PipOptions ([tool.uv.pip]) has index-url, extra-index-url and find-links too. uv.toml takes the same keys at its top level (extra.configTables). docs/concepts/indexes.md: "Indexes are prioritized in the order in which they're defined", the default index is "always treated as lowest priority", with the default first-index strategy uv "will stop at the first index on which a given package is available", default = true replaces PyPI ("set default = true on another index entry" to "exclude PyPI from the list of indexes"), so an entry without it adds an index that is asked before the default one, and an explicit = true index is used only for packages pinned to it in tool.uv.sources. Each [[index]] entry is read as entries says (decision D-120): explicit = true counts only for the packages tool.uv.sources pins to it by name, default = true replaces PyPI, any other entry adds an index (see INDEX_ENTRIES). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: uv export --format pylock.toml (and uv pip compile to pylock.toml) writes created-by = "uv". The project itself and workspace members are written as directory = { path = …, editable = true }, with the path relative to the lock file, "." for the project. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-lock/src/lock/export/pylock_toml.rs)
- `extra.configTables`: Settings sit in [tool.uv] in pyproject.toml and at the top level of uv.toml. uv.toml cannot hold workspace, sources and a few other project fields. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `extra.pyprojectTable`: A pyproject.toml without a [tool.uv] table is ignored when uv searches for configuration. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `extra.configPrecedence`: A nested pyproject.toml with any [tool.uv] table hides the configuration of its parent directories. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `extra.configFileOrder`: "configuration will be read from uv.toml, and the [tool.uv] section in the accompanying pyproject.toml will be ignored"; uv prints a warning listing the ignored fields. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `extra.workspaceRootOnly`: "In workspaces, uv will begin its search at the workspace root, ignoring any configuration defined in workspace members." Project fields such as tool.uv.sources of a member still apply. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/configuration-files.md)
- `extra.buildSwitch`: The project setting that forbids building source distributions. It also stops git and local directory dependencies (uv sync with uv 0.13.6 on 2026-10-30) and source archives, which also need a build; workspace members and editable requirements are still built. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/changelogs/0.2.x.md#0212)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Either a "friendly" duration (24 hours, 1 week, 30 days) or an ISO 8601 duration (PT24H, P7D, P30D). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/resolution.md)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Units in the documented examples: 24 hours, 1 week, 30 days. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/resolution.md)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: exclude-newer-package keys are exact package names. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `extra.excludeValue`: exclude-newer-package = { name = false } exempts the package from the delay. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/changelogs/0.9.x.md#0925)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: Unless the package is exempt, or the index has its own exclude-newer value or is exempt with [[tool.uv.index]] exclude-newer = false. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/docs/concepts/resolution.md)
- `extra.requiredVersion`: A PEP 440 specifier; uv exits with an error when its version does not match. Also at the top level of uv.toml. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs)
- `extra.lockedSettings`: uv.lock records these in [options] (a relative exclude-newer as exclude-newer-span); after a change uv lock --check and uv sync --locked fail until uv lock runs again ("Resolving despite existing lockfile due to addition of global exclude newer", seen with uv 0.13.6 on 2026-10-30). no-build and no-binary-package are not recorded. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-lock/src/lock/serialize.rs)
- `extra.lockOptions`: write_options writes [options] when exclude-newer is set: an absolute value as exclude-newer = "\<timestamp>"; a relative one as exclude-newer = the placeholder "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z" (with the comment "This has no effect and is included for backwards compatibility when using relative exclude-newer values") and exclude-newer-span = the span as jiff prints it, ISO 8601 (P3D, P1W); since 0.11.8 exclude-newer may be missing next to exclude-newer-span. [options.exclude-newer-package] holds name = "\<timestamp>", name = { timestamp = \<placeholder>, span = "P3D" } or name = false. The placeholder is ExcludeNewerValue::PLACEHOLDER in crates/uv-distribution-types/src/exclude_newer.rs. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-lock/src/lock/serialize.rs)
- `extra.lockComparison`: ExcludeNewer::compare (lock against the settings, in crates/uv-lock-operations/src/validated_lock.rs after lock.filter_exclude_newer) resolves again on an added or removed global value, a span that differs (ExcludeNewerSpan compares self.0.fieldwise() == other.0.fieldwise() in crates/uv-distribution-types/src/exclude_newer.rs, so "7 days" and P1W differ), a span added to or removed from an absolute value, and an absolute timestamp that is earlier than the locked one (a later one does not count); only a new timestamp of the same span is ignored. Per package (only names of locked packages and names the lock already records, filter_exclude_newer in crates/uv-lock/src/lock/mod.rs): a cutoff removed, a disabled one enabled, an enabled one added, or a changed value; an enabled one that is now disabled does not count. A date without a time (2026-01-01) is the start of the next day in the system time zone, so the timestamp it gives depends on the machine. Messages such as "Resolving despite existing lockfile due to change of exclude newer span from \`P3D\` to \`P1W\`" come from the Display of ExcludeNewerValueChange. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-configuration/src/exclude_newer.rs)
- `extra.spanSyntax`: jiff 0.2.37 is the version in Cargo.lock of uv 0.13.6. uv parses a relative exclude-newer with jiff's Span (FromStr of ExcludeNewerValue tries a timestamp, then a date, then a span), which reads the friendly format ("3 days", "1w", "2 weeks, 3 days", with each unit at most once, larger units first, a leading sign or a trailing "ago") and ISO 8601 (P3D, PT36H). Span prints as ISO 8601 by default, which is what uv.lock records. uv rejects years and months ("use days instead", crates/uv-distribution-types/src/exclude_newer.rs). The friendly format also has HH:MM:SS and fractions of hours and smaller units, which depcurfew does not read. [↗](https://github.com/BurntSushi/jiff/blob/0.2.37/crates/jiff/src/fmt/friendly/mod.rs)
- `extra.commandLine`: clap arguments of uv add, uv pip install, uv tool install, uv run and uv tool run (uvx), with the global options, IndexArgs, ResolverInstallerArgs, BuildOptionsArgs and DependencyConstraintsArgs they share. --opt value, --opt=value, -o value and -ovalue all work; long options cannot be shortened. Options of uv run, uv tool run and uvx come before the command. --with, --with-editable and --with-executables-from add packages, as a list split at commas outside [...] that are not followed by !, =, \<, > or \~ (comma.rs). uvx and uv tool run take the package from the first argument (name@version is ==version, name@latest the newest) unless --from names it; a first argument such as python, python3.12, pypy@3.8 or graalpy runs an interpreter (PythonRequest::try_from_tool_name in uv-python-types, implementation names cpython, pypy, graalpy and pyodide). uv run runs a command and downloads only what --with names, or a script given as an http or https URL. -e takes a path in uv pip install but is a flag in uv tool install, and --editable a flag in uv add; --no-binary and --only-binary take values in uv pip install only, -m is --marker in uv add and --module in uv run. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: IndexArgs (lib.rs): --index adds an index (name=url allowed), --default-index replaces PyPI, --index-url and --extra-index-url are their deprecated forms, --find-links adds a page or directory of archives; each has the variable named here. --config-file and UV_CONFIG_FILE name a uv.toml that may set any index. uv does not read pip.conf or PIP_INDEX_URL (docs/pip/compatibility.md). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-static/src/env_vars.rs)
- `extra.selection`: VersionSelectionArgs: --prerelease takes disallow, allow, if-necessary, explicit or if-necessary-or-explicit (UV_PRERELEASE); allow considers pre-releases of every package and disallow none (docs/concepts/resolution.md); --prerelease-package takes PACKAGE=MODE; the hidden --pre means allow. BuildOptionsArgs of uv add, uv run, uv tool install and uv tool run (uvx): --no-binary (UV_NO_BINARY, a boolean) installs every package from source, --binary turns it off, --no-binary-package names one package (UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE, separated by spaces). uv pip install takes --no-binary and --only-binary as lists separated by commas with :all: and :none:, as pip does (PipInstallArgs). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-26. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: GlobalArgs (global = true, so before or after the subcommand): --directory "Change to the given directory prior to running the command. Relative paths are resolved with the given directory as the base", env UV_WORKING_DIR; --project "Discover a project in the given directory. All pyproject.toml, uv.toml, and .python-version files will be discovered by walking up the directory tree from the project root … Other command-line arguments (such as relative paths) will be resolved relative to the current working directory … This setting has no effect when used in the uv pip interface", env UV_PROJECT. crates/uv-static/src/env_vars.rs: UV_WORKING_DIR is "Equivalent to the --directory command-line argument. UV_WORKING_DIRECTORY (added in v0.9.1) is also supported for backwards compatibility", UV_PROJECT "Equivalent to the --project command-line argument". [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `extra.installOverrides`: ExcludeNewerArgs: #[arg(long, env = EnvVars::UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER)] exclude_newer accepts RFC 3339 timestamps, local dates, friendly and ISO 8601 durations, and false to disable it; PackageExcludeNewerArgs adds --exclude-newer-package PACKAGE=DATE and is flattened into ResolverArgs, InstallerArgs and ResolverInstallerArgs. A date is not compared with the policy, so it is asked about. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs)
- `extra.pipTable`: For uv pip commands, PipSettings::combine merges the [pip] table of a configuration file above its top-level keys ("Merge the top-level options (\`tool.uv\`) with the pip-specific options (\`tool.uv.pip\`), preferring the latter"): [pip] exclude-newer replaces the top-level value (false turns the delay off), [pip] exclude-newer-package entries win over top-level entries for the same package, and [pip] no-binary (package names, or :all:) is added to the top-level no-binary-package (NoBinary::combine in crates/uv-configuration/src/build_options.rs). [pip] no-build and only-binary are joined with the top-level no-build, so they cannot turn it off. Commands outside uv pip ignore [pip] ("These values will be ignored when running commands outside the \`uv pip\` namespace", PipOptions in crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs). keys maps each top-level key depcurfew writes to the [pip] key that overrides or extends it. The same code in 0.11.32 (crates/uv/src/settings.rs). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/settings.rs)

### pip

- `cooldown.setting`: Only files uploaded before the given time are considered; applies to packages from remote indexes, not to local files, find-links directories or VCS requirements. Isolated build environments get the same cutoff. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: pip reads no configuration from the project: only the global, user and site (virtual environment) pip.conf, the file named by PIP_CONFIG_FILE and PIP\_\* environment variables. --uploaded-prior-to is not allowed in requirements files, so a project sets it through PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO or the command line, e.g. in CI. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: pip install, download, wheel, lock, index and list; environment variable PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `cooldown.unit`: A duration is written PnD, a whole number of days (P3D, matched by ^P(\\d+)D$); P1W, PT24H and "7 days" are rejected. An ISO 8601 date or time is a fixed cutoff instead. A day is always 24 hours. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: pip 26.1 accepts a duration in days ("P3D for 3 days ago"); the option itself exists since 26.0 with dates only. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless given. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: pip builds a source distribution when no wheel fits, which runs its build backend; the secure-installs guide recommends --only-binary :all:. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/secure-installs.md)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: After --only-binary=:all:, a package named in --no-binary may only be installed from source: a name wins over :all:, so its wheels are not used. --only-binary=:all: given after it clears the exception. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/models/format_control.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: --only-binary and --no-binary are among the options a requirements file may contain. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.format`: Each use adds to the set; :all: and :none: are special values. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Allowed in requirements files and pip.conf (only-binary). Enforced only for packages from indexes and find-links: VCS, local directory and direct URL source requirements are still built. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/secure-installs.md)
- `project.lockfiles`: pip lock (experimental since 25.1) writes pylock.toml; pip install -r pylock.toml is experimental since 26.1. The specification also allows pylock.\<name>.toml (extra.lockfilePattern). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst#file-name)
- `project.manifests`: "requirements.txt is usually what these files are named (although, that is not a requirement)"; the format is meant only for pip. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/reference/requirements-file-format.md)
- `user.files`: The user file is pip.conf (pip.ini on Windows) in appdirs.user_config_dir("pip") (configuration.py), written in INI with [global] and per-command sections. Linux: $HOME/.config/pip/pip.conf, "which respects the XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable" (used when it is not empty after stripping spaces, vendored platformdirs \_xdg.py). A relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME is used as it is, so pip reads \<value>/pip/pip.conf relative to the directory each command runs in: XDGMixin.user_config_dir in src/pip/\_vendor/platformdirs/\_xdg.py at 26.2.2 returns the stripped value with no absolute-path check, \_append_app_name_and_version (api.py) only joins the app name, and utils/appdirs.py and configuration.py (os.path.join, then os.path.exists and parser.read) make nothing absolute; 26.1.1 (platformdirs 4.5.1, Unix.user_config_dir in unix.py) does the same without stripping the value. From 26.3 ("Upgrade platformdirs to 4.12.4", NEWS.rst at 26.3) \_xdg_dir in src/pip/\_vendor/platformdirs/\_xdg.py returns the stripped value only when posixpath.isabs, so a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME is ignored and pip reads \~/.config/pip/pip.conf. macOS: \~/Library/Application Support/pip when that directory exists, else \~/.config/pip, where XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not used (utils/appdirs.py: \_macos_user_config_dir takes platformdirs user_data_dir when os.path.isdir); since 26.2 that user_data_dir is $XDG_DATA_HOME/pip when XDG_DATA_HOME is not empty after stripping spaces, so with XDG_DATA_HOME set the Library directory is skipped and \~/.config/pip is used unless $XDG_DATA_HOME/pip exists (XDGMixin in src/pip/\_vendor/platformdirs/\_xdg.py at 26.2.2; src/pip/\_vendor/vendor.txt names platformdirs 4.10.0 in 26.2 and 4.5.1 in 26.1.1, whose macos.py has no XDG handling); from 26.3 only an absolute XDG_DATA_HOME counts, so a relative one leaves the Library directory in use (XDGMixin.user_data_dir with \_xdg_dir at 26.3). Windows: %APPDATA%\\pip\\pip.ini; platformdirs asks Windows for the Roaming AppData known folder, which APPDATA normally names. The legacy \~/.pip/pip.conf (%HOME%\\pip\\pip.ini) is loaded as well, below this file. Same path code in 25.0; earlier versions are not tracked. A command reads [global] and the section named after itself, which wins key by key (override_order ["global", self.name, ":env:"] in cli/parser.py); the options doctor --user checks (index_group and package_selection_group in cli/cmdoptions.py) belong to install, download, wheel, lock, index and list (src/pip/\_internal/commands at 26.2.2). Keys are read without regard to case, with underscores as dashes and without a leading -- (\_normalize_name in src/pip/\_internal/configuration.py at 26.2.2 and 26.3: name.lower().replace("\_", "-") and removeprefix("--"), the same in 25.0), so only_binary and --only-binary in a file are the setting only-binary. pip parses each file with configparser.RawConfigParser, whose strict mode (strict=True by default, Lib/configparser.py of CPython 3.9 to 3.14) raises DuplicateSectionError for a section given twice and DuplicateOptionError for a key given twice in one section; pip turns that into ConfigurationFileCouldNotBeLoaded and stops (\_construct_parser). Before 26.3 the parser compares keys in lower case only (the default optionxform), so only_binary next to only-binary in one section is read as one setting and the later line wins (\_normalized_keys); from 26.3 the parser normalizes the names itself (\_RawConfigParser.optionxform calls \_normalize_name), so such a file stops pip. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#location)
- `user.settings`: depcurfew writes them in [global], which reaches every command that has the option (install, download, wheel, lock, index, list) and the resolver of pipenv lock; [install] reaches only pip install. "Accept --no-binary and --only-binary via pip.conf" (7.1.0); uploaded-prior-to is read from pip.conf like every long option ("To override a duration set in configuration, pass P0D on the command line", user_guide.rst). 26.1.0 because depcurfew writes a PnD duration: pip 26.0 takes dates only and aborts on P7D, and 25.x ignores the key. uv does not read pip.conf. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `user.unknownKeys`: "Ignore options not present in this parser": a key that is not an option of the command is skipped without a word (same code in 25.0), so pip before 26.0 ignores uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/parser.py)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: A pip.conf that is not valid INI stops pip (ConfigurationFileCouldNotBeLoaded, configuration.py), and a value an option rejects ends the command with a usage error: pip 26.0 aborts on uploaded-prior-to = P7D in every command that has the option, as it rejected PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO=P100000D in a test on 2026-10-30 (configuration values and PIP\_\* variables go through the same parsing). Commands without the option ignore the key. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/parser.py)
- `user.weakening`: In any section of any pip.conf: [install] beats [global], and a later file (a virtual environment pip.conf, PIP_CONFIG_FILE) beats the user file per key, an empty value removing it (cli/parser.py). :all: in one of the lists clears the other and :none: clears its own (handle_mutual_excludes). P0D overrides a configured duration, and "Local package files are allowed regardless of the --uploaded-prior-to setting", find-links directories included (user_guide.rst). A requirements file can also pass --no-binary or --only-binary, but not --uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/models/format_control.py)
- `user.variables`: "Note that if a file exists at the location that this is set to, the user config file will not be loaded." PIP\_\<NAME> variables are applied after the [global] and command sections of all files, and the command line beats them (cli/parser.py, override_order). --isolated, a flag, ignores environment variables and user configuration. XDG_CONFIG_HOME (Linux) and XDG_DATA_HOME (macOS, 26.2) move the user directory, from 26.3 only when they are absolute paths (see files). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `extra.environmentNames`: get_environ_vars takes the variables of os.environ whose names start with PIP\_ (key.startswith("PIP\_"), the prefix in upper case) and lowercases the rest (key[4:].lower()), so PIP_index_url sets index-url and pip_index_url sets nothing (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/configuration.py)
- `extra.configCommand`: pip config: "Manage local and global configuration"; "set: Set the command.option=value", "unset: Unset the value associated with command.option", "edit: Edit the configuration file in an editor". Without --user, --global or --site it changes the configuration file of the active virtual environment when that file exists, otherwise the user file. So a CI step or RUN with pip config set can give the later pip installs a release-age delay that no environment variable shows (decision D-115). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/commands/configuration.py)
- `extra.configSections`: "Each subcommand can be configured optionally in its own section. This overrides the global setting with the same name", and "A command specific section in the config file \`[\<command>] host = bar\` overrides the option with same name in the \`[global]\` config file section" (Precedence / Override order). pip reads only [global], the section of the running command and :env: (override_order = ["global", self.name, ":env:"] in cli/parser.py), so a managed key in [install] wins over [global] for pip install; depcurfew comments such keys out in every section other than [global]. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: pip lock writes created-by = "pip". [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/utils/pylock.py)
- `extra.requirementsOptions`: SUPPORTED_OPTIONS in pip 26.2.2 (--pypi-url is a second name of --index-url in cmdoptions.py); per requirement also --hash and -C/--config-settings (extra.requirementsParser). Any other option, --uploaded-prior-to included, makes the file fail to parse. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `extra.requirementsParser`: build_parser reads each line with optparse.OptionParser(add_help_option=False) holding SUPPORTED_OPTIONS and SUPPORTED_OPTIONS_REQ (--hash, -C/--config-settings), with the names from cmdoptions.py in pip 26.2.2. optparse takes a long option shortened to a prefix that names exactly one of them (\_match_abbrev; an exact name wins), so --no-bin :all: is --no-binary :all:, and an ambiguous prefix such as --no is an error. --hash and --config-settings belong to the requirement on their line; on a line of their own they are accepted and ignored. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `extra.configFileNames`: CONFIG_BASENAME is pip.ini on Windows and pip.conf elsewhere; pip looks for it only in the global, user and site locations, never in the project. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/configuration.py)
- `extra.configFileVariable`: Names a configuration file pip loads last; set to os.devnull it turns all configuration files off. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#environment-variable)
- `extra.environmentVariable`: Every long option has a PIP\_\<UPPER_LONG_NAME> variable with dashes replaced by underscores. Tested on 2026-10-30: pip 25.3 ignored PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO=P100000D without a word, 26.0 rejected the duration (dates only), 26.1 and 26.2.2 found no version. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#environment-variables)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Only whole days, written PnD, are accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: Upload times exist only in the JSON form of the simple repository API (PEP 700); indexes that serve only HTML have none. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Each [[packages]] entry has exactly one of vcs (always built), directory (always built), archive (a source tree or wheel at a URL or path) or sdist and wheels from an index. A package with an sdist and no wheels is built when installed. A relative directory path is relative to the lock file. The required top-level created-by records the name of the tool that wrote the file, preferably its normalized Python package name. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst)
- `extra.requirementsFormat`: VCS requirements start with git+, hg+, svn+ or bzr+, alone or after "name @"; a direct reference is "name @ URL" (PEP 508); -e installs a project path or VCS URL in editable mode. The legacy #egg= fragment names the project of a VCS URL. Lines ending with a backslash continue on the next line, and # starts a comment (requirements-file-format.md). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/vcs-support.md)
- `extra.requirementsIncludes`: Option names from cli/cmdoptions.py. A relative path is relative to the directory of the file that includes it, and a file given as an http, https or file URL is downloaded (req_file.py, \_parse_and_recurse); a file that includes itself is an error. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/reference/requirements-file-format.md#referring-to-other-requirements-files)
- `extra.requirementsPaths`: A requirement that contains a path separator (/, and \\ on Windows) or starts with . looks like a path (\_looks_like_path): a directory there is a project built from source. A name with an archive extension (utils/filetypes.py) is a local archive, even when the file does not exist. http, https, ftp and file URLs are links (utils/urls.py, is_url). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/constructors.py)
