- `extra.lockfilePattern`: A named lock file, next to or instead of pylock.toml; pip lock -o writes any name. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst#file-name)
- `extra.commandLine`: pip and pip3 are the console scripts of the package (pyproject.toml). The options of pip install (install.py) and the general options of every command (cmdoptions.py, general_group), which may also come before install. pip reads them with optparse: --opt value and --opt=value, -rFILE and -r FILE, grouped short flags, and a long option shortened to any prefix that names one option (cli/parser.py keeps optparse's matching), so --extra means --extra-index-url. -e takes a local project path or a VCS URL to install in editable mode. -r, -c, --requirements-from-script and --group read requirements from files of the project. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/commands/install.py)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: index_group: --index-url (alias -i, --pypi-url) is the base URL of the package index, --extra-index-url adds indexes, --find-links (-f) adds an HTML page or a directory of archives. Every long option can be set as PIP\_\<UPPER_LONG_NAME>, dashes replaced by underscores (docs/html/topics/configuration.md); PIP_CONFIG_FILE names a configuration file loaded last, which may set any index. Requirements files may set --index-url, --extra-index-url and --find-links too (req/req_file.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `extra.selection`: --pre includes pre-release and development versions (pip only finds stable versions by default) and stands for --all-releases :all:; --all-releases and --only-final take :all:, :none: or package names separated by commas and allow or forbid pre-releases of those packages (models/release_control.py, allows_prereleases: a named package first, then :all:). --no-binary and --only-binary take the same lists: --no-binary keeps pip from using wheels, so the package is built from source, --only-binary from using source distributions (models/format_control.py, handle_mutual_excludes and get_allowed_formats). Each long option can also be set as PIP\_\<NAME> (docs/html/topics/configuration.md), which the command line overrides. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `extra.pipxSelection`: pipx forwards the standard PIP\_\* variables to pip (except PIP_USER, PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK, PIP_TARGET and PIP_KEYRING_PROVIDER); the uv backend ignores them (docs/how-to/use-private-index.rst). pipx has no option of its own for pre-releases or source builds; --pip-args may carry them. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/docs/reference/environment-variables.rst)
- `extra.pipxCommandLine`: pipx installs applications from PyPI with pip (or uv) in environments of their own. pipx install takes one or more package specs, a VCS URL, a local path or archive, or a script (--preinstall adds packages to the environment; -f is --force, not find-links). pipx run takes the app first (argparse REMAINDER, so its options come before it), --spec names the package to install and run, --with adds packages; a first argument ending in .py is a local script, or a script to download when it is a URL (docs/how-to/run-scripts.rst). argparse accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/src/pipx/main.py)
- `extra.pipxRegistryOverrides`: --index-url is the base URL of the index; --pip-args is split and handed to pip, so it may carry --extra-index-url, --find-links or --no-index. With the pip backend pipx passes the PIP\_\* variables on to pip; with the uv backend it ignores them and uv reads its own (docs/how-to/use-uv-backend.rst); both kinds are registry variables of pip and uv. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/src/pipx/main.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-20. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `extra.configCommands`: pip config list, edit, get, set, unset and debug: set and unset change a value and save the file, edit opens it in an editor, list, get and debug only read. Without --user, --global or --site the site file is used if one exists, else the user file. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/commands/configuration.py)
- `extra.installOverrides`: --uploaded-prior-to (metavar datetime_or_duration): "Only consider packages uploaded prior to the given value", an ISO 8601 datetime or a duration of whole days P\<n>D. PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO is its environment variable (environmentVariable). A datetime is not compared with the policy, so it is asked about. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)

### Poetry

- `cooldown.setting`: A version is ignored while any of its files was uploaded less than the given number of days ago. Applies when dependencies are resolved (poetry lock, add, update); poetry install installs the locked versions without checking. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The local configuration next to pyproject.toml (poetry config --local), not pyproject.toml itself. Environment variables (POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE) win over poetry.toml, which wins over the user config.toml. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#local-configuration)
- `cooldown.unit`: An integer; 0 (the default) turns it off. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Introduced in 2.4.0"; announced as dependency cooldowns. Tested on 2026-10-30: Poetry 2.3.4 locked with min-release-age = 100000 in poetry.toml without a word, while 2.4.0 and 2.5.1 found no version. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.default`: Default 0: all versions are considered. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Without installer.only-binary, packages are built from source distributions when no wheel fits, which runs their build backend. Git and directory dependencies are always built. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installeronly-binary)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: With installer.only-binary = [":all:"], the packages named in installer.no-binary are the only ones built from source; explicit names take precedence over :all: since 2.2.0. Their wheels are rejected, so they are always built. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/installation/chooser.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: The docs recommend configuring it with --local for a project. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installerno-binary)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: "explicit package names will take precedence over :all:" (#10278). Before 2.2.0 a package listed in both settings has no file left to install. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.allowList.format`: poetry config stores the value as a list; written by hand, a boolean is not normalized. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installerno-binary)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Since 2.0.0; the value [":all:"] forbids source distributions for every package. Applied only when installing: resolving dependencies may still build source distributions without static metadata, and git, path and url dependencies are built regardless. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installeronly-binary)
- `project.lockfiles`: Next to pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/factory.py)
- `user.files`: "Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pypoetry or \~/.config/pypoetry - Windows: %APPDATA%\\pypoetry - macOS: \~/Library/Application Support/pypoetry". The code agrees on Linux and Windows: CONFIG_DIR = POETRY_CONFIG_DIR or user_config_path("pypoetry", appauthor=False, roaming=True) from platformdirs, without an override (src/poetry/locations.py; on Windows platformdirs asks for the Roaming AppData known folder, which APPDATA normally names). On macOS the directory depends on the installed platformdirs (libraryDirectories); the docs' directory is used when its version cannot be read. config.toml holds the settings as nested tables ([solver] min-release-age = 7); auth.toml next to it holds credentials. POETRY_CONFIG_DIR replaces the directory. Checked at 2.4.0 and 2.5.1; 2.0.0 removed the special handling of the platformdirs 2 macOS directory (#8916, CHANGELOG.md), and older versions are not tracked. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#config-directory)
- `user.libraryDirectories`: Poetry 2.5.1 allows platformdirs >=3.0.0,\<5 (pyproject.toml; its own lock has 4.11.8), and the official installer runs pip install without constraints in Poetry's virtual environment (python-poetry/install.python-poetry.org, install-poetry.py), so a new install gets the latest 4.x. The macOS user_config_dir by platformdirs version, read from the code at the tags: before 4.6.0 always \~/Library/Application Support/\<app> (4.5.1 macos.py has no XDG support); 4.6.0 "Honor XDG environment variables on macOS" (#375): a non-empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME wins, a relative one too (os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "").strip() in \_xdg.py), and otherwise the config directory is user_data_dir, so a non-empty XDG_DATA_HOME gives $XDG_DATA_HOME/\<app>; 4.9.6 "Fix macOS XDG variables leaking across user_config_dir, user_data_dir, and user_state_dir" (#473; 4.9.4 still returns user_data_dir); 4.11.8 "Ignore relative paths in XDG Base Directory environment variables and use the existing platform fallback" (#540, \_xdg_dir with posixpath.isabs); the same in 4.14.2. A relative value is used as it is, so the tool reads it from the directory each command runs in. [↗](https://github.com/tox-dev/platformdirs/blob/4.14.2/docs/changelog.rst)
- `user.settings`: Every setting of Config.default_config is read from the user config.toml ("As with all configurations described here, this is a user specific configuration", docs/configuration.md); dotted names are nested tables. A project poetry.toml replaces a user value, lists included (merge_dicts in src/poetry/utils/helpers.py), and POETRY\_\* variables beat both. Names in installer.no-binary win over installer.only-binary = :all: only since 2.2.0. solver.min-release-age-exclude is written as a TOML array (see extra.excludeFormat). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/config/config.py)
- `user.weakening`: Precedence: environment variables, then the local poetry.toml, then the global config.toml, then the default; a poetry.toml key replaces the user value, lists included. solver.min-release-age-exclude-source (2.4.0) takes source names from pyproject.toml or URLs. A source that gives no upload times is not filtered at all. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#configuration-sources)
- `user.variables`: Any setting can be set as POETRY\_ plus its name in capitals with dots and dashes replaced by underscores, and environment variables come first in the precedence ("Configuration sources"). POETRY_CONFIG_DIR replaces the platform directory (src/poetry/locations.py). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#using-environment-variables)
- `extra.environmentNames`: Config.get builds the name "POETRY\_" + the keys of the setting in upper case with \_ for - and reads it with os.getenv(env), and \_get_environment_repositories matches POETRY_REPOSITORIES\_(?P\<name>[A-Z\_]+)\_URL, so only the names in upper case count (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/config/config.py)
- `extra.installedPackage`: The installation page installs a given version with "pipx install poetry==1.8.4", in CI with "$POETRY_HOME/bin/pip install poetry==2.0.0", and manually with pip in a virtual environment ("$VENV_PATH/bin/pip install poetry"). So poetry==\<version> in such a command of a CI job or a Dockerfile is the Poetry the later commands run (decision D-115). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/_index.md)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: Poetry exports pylock.toml with its export plugin (poetry export --format pylock.toml), which writes created-by = "poetry-plugin-export". [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-plugin-export/blob/1.10.1/src/poetry_plugin_export/exporter.py)
- `extra.configTable`: poetry config writes dotted settings as nested tables, e.g. [solver] min-release-age = 7. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/config/file_config_source.py)
- `extra.pyprojectTable`: A [tool.poetry] table marks a Poetry project; Poetry also accepts a [project] table with a static name and version, which other tools use as well. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/blob/2.5.0/src/poetry/core/pyproject/toml.py)
- `extra.buildSwitch`: installer.only-binary was added in 2.0.0; [":all:"] forbids source distributions of index packages when installing. Git and directory dependencies, and source archives from a URL or path, are built regardless (src/poetry/installation/executor.py at 2.5.1). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Package names only. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age-exclude)
- `extra.requiredVersion`: A version constraint in pyproject.toml; a Poetry version outside it raises an error. Poetry 1.x does not know the key. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/pyproject.md#requires-poetry)
- `extra.commandLine`: poetry add takes package specs: a name, name@constraint, a PEP 508 requirement, a git URL, a path or an archive URL. Options with a value: --group (-G), --extras (-E), --optional, --python, --platform, --markers and --source of add, and the global --directory (-C) and --project (-P); -e/--editable, -D/--dev, --allow-prereleases, --dry-run and --lock are flags (src/poetry/console/commands/add.py). cleo reads -Gdocs and -G docs; long options cannot be shortened. poetry install takes no package specs. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/cli.md#add)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: --source names a package source of [[tool.poetry.source]] in pyproject.toml (or pypi) to take the package from. The POETRY_REPOSITORIES\_\<NAME>\_URL variables are for publishing only; no variable sets a package source. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/repositories.md)
- `extra.versionConstraints`: poetry add name@constraint takes any constraint valid in pyproject.toml, and name@latest the newest release; extras go before the @ (name[extra]@^4.0.0). ^ keeps the left-most non-zero part of major.minor.patch: ^1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 \<2.0.0, ^1.2 is >=1.2.0 \<2.0.0, ^1 is >=1.0.0 \<2.0.0, ^0.2.3 is >=0.2.3 \<0.3.0, ^0.0.3 is >=0.0.3 \<0.0.4, ^0.0 is >=0.0.0 \<0.1.0, ^0 is >=0.0.0 \<1.0.0. \~ allows patch changes, or minor changes when only a major version is given: \~1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 \<1.3.0, \~1.2 is >=1.2.0 \<1.3.0, \~1 is >=1.0.0 \<2.0.0. \* is any version, 1.\* is >=1.0.0 \<2.0.0, 1.2.\* is >=1.2.0 \<1.3.0. \~=, inequalities and == as in PEP 440, several separated by commas; a bare version (1.2.3) is that version only. Poetry prefers stable releases and takes a pre-release only when no stable release satisfies the constraint. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/dependency-specification.md#using-the--operator)
- `extra.selection`: installer.no-binary (POETRY_INSTALLER_NO_BINARY) disallows wheels for :all: or true, none for :none: or false, or the named packages separated by commas; installer.only-binary (POETRY_INSTALLER_ONLY_BINARY, since 2.0.0) takes the same values; explicit package names win over :all:. poetry add --allow-prereleases accepts pre-releases (src/poetry/console/commands/add.py). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-09-20. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: Global options: --directory=DIRECTORY (-C) "The working directory for the Poetry command (defaults to the current working directory). All command-line arguments will be resolved relative to the given directory."; --project=PROJECT (-P) "Specify another path as the project root. All command-line arguments will be resolved relative to the current working directory or directory specified using --directory option if used." The page names no environment variable for either. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/cli.md)
- `extra.registrySettings`: [[tool.poetry.source]] has name, url and priority. "If priority is undefined, the source is considered a primary source"; "All primary package sources are searched for each dependency without a source constraint" and "If you configure at least one primary source, the implicit PyPI source is disabled", so a primary source replaces PyPI. Supplemental sources "are only searched if no other (higher-priority) source yields a compatible package distribution": depcurfew does not know whether PyPI has a version the constraint takes, so such a source counts as one that adds. Explicit sources "are only searched when a package configuration explicitly indicates" them: a dependency with source = "name" in [tool.poetry.dependencies] or [tool.poetry.group.\<group>.dependencies], also in a list of constraint tables (docs/dependency-specification.md, docs/managing-dependencies.md). create_pool in src/poetry/factory.py reads Priority[source.get("priority", "primary").upper()], so the value is compared without regard to case; the schema (src/poetry/json/schemas/poetry.json) allows primary, supplemental and explicit, and another value (default or secondary of Poetry 1.x) fails in 2.5.1 and counts as primary here. A source whose name is pypi in any case is PyPI itself (PyPiRepository), which "cannot be configured with a custom url" (create_package_source). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/repositories.md)
- `extra.configCommands`: poetry config [options] [setting-key] [setting-value1] ... [setting-valueN] sets a key to a value (--local in poetry.toml of the project); --unset removes the key, --migrate migrates outdated settings and --list only shows them. "The source namespace groups subcommands to manage repository sources for a Poetry project": source add adds a source to pyproject.toml (also the priority of PyPI, with --priority), source remove removes one from it, and source show only shows them (docs/cli.md; src/poetry/console/commands/source/add.py and remove.py write pyproject.poetry_config["source"], and src/poetry/console/application.py lists source add, source remove and source show). The sources of pyproject.toml are where poetry add and poetry install take packages from (registrySettings). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/cli.md)
- `extra.installOverrides`: Settings can be set with environment variables prefixed by POETRY\_, the upper-case setting name with dots and dashes replaced by underscores; solver.min-release-age (int, days) is POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE. poetry add has no option for it. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md)

### PDM

- `cooldown.setting`: In the [tool.pdm.resolution] table of pyproject.toml: distributions uploaded after the cutoff are left out when dependencies are resolved (pdm lock, add, update). The --exclude-newer option of pdm lock wins over it, and it wins over strategy.exclude-newer in the PDM configuration. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The [tool.pdm.resolution] table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: pdm lock --exclude-newer, since 2.13.0. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.unit`: An RFC 3339 timestamp, a UTC date or a relative duration N{d|h|w} such as 7d, 12h or 3w, counted from the current UTC time. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Support exclude-newer in pyproject.toml in the [tool.pdm.resolution] table" (#3776); the pdm lock option exists since 2.13.0. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: No default: without a value every upload time is accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: A table [tool.pdm.resolution.exclude-newer-override] of package = false (no cutoff) or package = another date or duration; package-specific values win over the global cutoff. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.exclude.availableSince`: "Allow package-specific overrides for exclude-newer resolution limits" (#3809). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Without only-binary, PDM locks and installs source distributions when they fit, which builds them and runs their build backend. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: The packages in no-binary are locked and installed from source distributions only. A name in no-binary wins over only-binary = ":all:" (FormatControl of unearth, which PDM uses), so with both the named packages are the only ones built, and always from source. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: The [tool.pdm.resolution] table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: no-binary, only-binary and prefer-binary keys in [tool.pdm.resolution] (#2656). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: only-binary = ":all:" locks and installs only wheels. The variables PDM_ONLY_BINARY and PDM_NO_BINARY win over pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `project.lockfiles`: pdm.lock next to pyproject.toml; pdm lock --lockfile writes another name. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md)
- `user.files`: \<CONFIG_ROOT> is "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pdm (\~/.config/pdm in most cases) on Linux", "\~/Library/Application Support/pdm on macOS" and "%USERPROFILE%\\AppData\\Local\\pdm\\pdm on Windows". The code agrees on Linux and Windows: global_config = platformdirs.user_config_path("pdm") / "config.toml", without an override (src/pdm/project/core.py; on Windows the default appauthor repeats the name and roaming is off, so platformdirs asks for the Local AppData known folder). On macOS the directory depends on the installed platformdirs (libraryDirectories); the docs' directory is used when its version cannot be read. The home configuration is TOML whose nested tables are read as dotted keys ([strategy] exclude-newer is strategy.exclude-newer, load_config in src/pdm/project/config.py). -c/--config and PDM_CONFIG_FILE replace it; the site configuration is merged below it. Checked at 2.29.5; earlier versions are not tracked. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/config.md)
- `user.libraryDirectories`: PDM 2.29.5 does not pin platformdirs (pyproject.toml; its own lock has 4.9.6). The macOS user_config_dir by platformdirs version, read from the code at the tags: before 4.6.0 always \~/Library/Application Support/\<app> (4.5.1 macos.py has no XDG support); 4.6.0 "Honor XDG environment variables on macOS" (#375): a non-empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME wins, a relative one too (os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "").strip() in \_xdg.py), and otherwise the config directory is user_data_dir, so a non-empty XDG_DATA_HOME gives $XDG_DATA_HOME/\<app>; 4.9.6 "Fix macOS XDG variables leaking across user_config_dir, user_data_dir, and user_state_dir" (#473; 4.9.4 still returns user_data_dir); 4.11.8 "Ignore relative paths in XDG Base Directory environment variables and use the existing platform fallback" (#540, \_xdg_dir with posixpath.isabs); the same in 4.14.2. A relative value is used as it is, so the tool reads it from the directory each command runs in. [↗](https://github.com/tox-dev/platformdirs/blob/4.14.2/docs/changelog.rst)
- `user.settings`: "Allow configuring the default lock --exclude-newer value with strategy.exclude-newer" (2.27.0, #3795): a TOML string such as "7d", a date or an RFC 3339 time. It applies where neither [tool.pdm.resolution] exclude-newer in pyproject.toml nor a project pdm.toml sets it (docs/usage/lockfile.md), and with it in effect pdm lock resolves every package again (src/pdm/cli/commands/lock.py). only-binary, no-binary and exclude-newer-override cannot be set in any PDM configuration file: PDM reads them from [tool.pdm.resolution] in pyproject.toml, only-binary and no-binary also from PDM_ONLY_BINARY and PDM_NO_BINARY (environments/base.py, Project.env_or_setting), so at user level they can be set only through those variables. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `user.weakening`: use_uv (experimental since 2.19.0, PDM_USE_UV) can be set in config.toml and in a project pdm.toml, which wins. PDM passes the cutoff and the build settings to uv lock but not to uv sync --frozen (src/pdm/installers/uv.py), and passes no --no-config, so uv also reads the user uv.toml. A home strategy.exclude-newer cannot weaken a project that sets [tool.pdm.resolution] exclude-newer. use_uv is a switch that turns a protection off and is read with ensure_boolean (src/pdm/project/config.py at 2.29.5): a TOML boolean or number is kept, and a string is false only when empty or false, no or 0 in any case; depcurfew counts every other value as on (other spellings of false too, which errs towards a warning). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/uv.md)
- `user.variables`: env_or_setting returns os.getenv(var) or the pyproject.toml setting, so a non-empty PDM_ONLY_BINARY or PDM_NO_BINARY wins (environments/base.py). -c/--config and PDM_CONFIG_FILE name the home config file (src/pdm/core.py). PDM_USE_UV is the variable of use_uv, and variables beat pdm.toml and config.toml (src/pdm/project/config.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/core.py)
- `extra.environmentNames`: A configuration item takes its value from its env_var (PDM_PYPI_URL and the others) with os.environ[item.env_var], and the options read PDM_PROJECT and the other variables with os.getenv("PDM_PROJECT") (src/pdm/cli/options.py), so only those spellings count (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/config.py)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: PDM's pylock.toml export writes created-by = "pdm". [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/formats/pylock.py)
- `extra.configTables`: exclude-newer, its overrides, only-binary and no-binary share the table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.pyprojectTable`: PDM keeps its settings in [tool.pdm] of pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/reference/pep621.md)
- `extra.buildSwitch`: only-binary in [tool.pdm.resolution] since 2.15.0 (#2656). It covers packages from an index: git, URL and path requirements already name their source and are built regardless (candidates.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.durationStrings`: "pdm lock --exclude-newer now accepts relative durations in the format N{d|h|w}" (#3760). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Written as Nh, Nd and Nw. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Override keys are package names. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.excludeValue`: package = false disables the cutoff for that package. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: The index must give upload-time (PEP 700); an override of false lifts it for the package. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.lockedSettings`: pdm.lock keeps a content_hash of the whole [tool.pdm.resolution] table (PyProject.content_hash), or with canonical lock inputs (lock_inputs = true, since 2.28.1) the table itself (src/pdm/project/lockfile/freshness.py), so a change to any key in it, exclude-newer and only-binary included, makes the lockfile out of date. pdm lock --check and pdm install --check then exit with 1 ("Lockfile doesn't satisfy the project requirements"), pdm install without --check locks again first and pdm sync only warns (check_lockfile in src/pdm/cli/actions.py) until pdm lock runs again; with exclude-newer set, pdm lock resolves every package again (src/pdm/cli/commands/lock.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/project_file.py)
- `extra.lockHash`: PyProject.content_hash: json.dumps(dump_data, sort_keys=True) of sources (tool.pdm.source, default []), dependencies, dev-dependencies, optional-dependencies (default {}), requires-python (default "") and resolution (tool.pdm.resolution, default {}), encoded as UTF-8 and hashed with hashlib (sha256). dev-dependencies are the [dependency-groups] tables, each name normalized (normalize_name in src/pdm/utils.py: re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", name).lower(); a name twice is an error), then the lists of tool.pdm.dev-dependencies appended under their normalized names. pdm.lock keeps it as [metadata] content_hash = "sha256:\<hex>" (src/pdm/project/lockfile/pdmlock.py). Project.is_lockfile_fresh (src/pdm/project/core.py) compares it only while pdm.lock has no metadata.lock_inputs and resolution.lock_inputs is not true; a workspace root (tool.pdm.workspace set, WorkspaceManager.is_root in src/pdm/project/workspace.py) hashes the members too. PDM reads pyproject.toml with tomllib (src/pdm/project/toml_file.py), and without a [project] table it converts a Poetry or Flit project first (\_convert_pyproject). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/project_file.py)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: project_option: "-p", "--project", dest="project_path", help "Specify another path as the project root, which changes the base of pyproject.toml and \_\_pypackages\_\_ [env var: PDM_PROJECT]", default=os.getenv("PDM_PROJECT"). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/options.py)
- `extra.commandLine`: pdm add takes requirements as arguments and editable ones with -e; its options come from cli/options.py and the global ones (-c/--config, --pep582, -I, -n, --no-cache) from core.py. --venv and --pep582 take an optional value, so argparse takes the next word for it. PDM parses with argparse, which accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/commands/add.py)
- `extra.registrySettings`: [[tool.pdm.source]] has name, url, verify_ssl, type ("index or find_links, default to index") and include_packages and exclude_packages. "If you want to omit the default PyPI index, just set the source name to pypi and that source will replace it"; the source list is pypi.url (when no source is named pypi), then the sources of pyproject.toml, then pypi.\<name>.url of the configuration, and by default "all sources are treated as equal" and the best matching version across them is taken, so any other source adds an index. Project.get_sources (src/pdm/project/core.py) keys the sources by name and fills a source named pypi from pypi.url, so one without a URL is PyPI (or the pypi.url of the user's configuration, which depcurfew does not read); PDM compares the name pypi exactly, depcurfew without regard to case, which only compares more URLs. Variables in url (${PROJECT_ROOT}) are expanded by PDM, so depcurfew cannot read such a URL. include_packages and exclude_packages are not read: a source counts for every package. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/config.md)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: pypi.url, the index PDM uses when pyproject.toml names no source called pypi, can be set with PDM_PYPI_URL (docs/usage/config.md); -c/--config and PDM_CONFIG_FILE name another configuration file, which may set any index. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/config.py)
- `extra.configCommands`: pdm config [-l|--local] [-d|--delete] [-e|--edit] [key] [value]: with a key and a value it sets the key (\_set_config, in the home config.toml, with -l in the pdm.toml of the project), with -d it deletes the key, with -e it opens the file in an editor; a key alone shows its value, and without a key it lists the configuration. docs/usage/config.md sets the index this way: pdm config pypi.url "https://test.pypi.org/simple", pdm config --local pypi.url …, pdm config pypi.extra.url … for an extra index. PDM parses with argparse, which takes abbreviated long options and grouped short ones (commandLine). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/commands/config.py)
- `extra.selection`: pdm add --pre/--prerelease allows pre-releases of the added packages to be pinned and --stable only stable versions (prerelease_option; commands/add.py sets req.prerelease). PDM_NO_BINARY and PDM_ONLY_BINARY are lists of packages separated by commas, :all: for every package, of which no wheel, or only wheels, are locked and installed (docs/usage/lockfile.md; environments/base.py, \_setting_list). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/options.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-30. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)

### Pipenv

- `cooldown.setting`: In the [pipenv] section of the Pipfile: the resolver considers only versions uploaded at least that many days ago. Pipenv computes a cutoff (now minus N days, UTC) and hands it to pip as uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The [pipenv] section. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipenv-directives)
- `cooldown.unit`: A string in \<int>d format, e.g. "30d"; any other form is rejected (pipenv/vendor/plette/models/sections.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Added support for cool-down-period in the [pipenv] section of the Pipfile" under 2026.6.2 (repeated under 2026.7.0 and 2026.7.1). Checked against the wheels on 2026-10-30: missing in 2026.6.1, present in 2026.6.2. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless set. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Pipenv installs with pip, which builds source distributions when no wheel fits. Pipenv honors pip configuration and PIP\_\* variables, which may forbid building (PIP_ONLY_BINARY=:all:), but the Pipfile has no setting for it. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `project.lockfiles`: JSON, generated next to the Pipfile. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfilelock)
- `project.manifests`: TOML. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfile)
- `user.files`: Pipenv has no user configuration file of its own: it reads environment variables (set in a shell profile), the project .env file and pip configuration; pipenv/environments.py looks up no file. Since 2026.3.0 the pip install step runs with PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null (pipenv/utils/pip.py; CHANGELOG.md, #6066), so a user pip.conf no longer protects pipenv install and sync. The lock resolver still reads pip.conf, but only [global], because its pip command is named InstallCommand (pipenv/utils/resolver.py), and a Pipfile cool-down-period replaces its uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.settings`: No user file to write to; at user level only PIP\_\* variables reach the pip install step (see variables). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.unknownKeys`: No user file. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: No user file. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.weakening`: No user file; see variables. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.environmentNames`: get_from_env looks up f"{prefix}\_{arg}" with the prefix PIPENV (PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR, PIPENV_PIPFILE, PIPENV_DOTENV_LOCATION) through "positive_lookup in os.environ", that spelling only. PIP_NO_BINARY and PIP_ONLY_BINARY reach the pip Pipenv runs, which reads PIP\_ variables with the prefix in upper case and the rest in any case (pip extra.environmentNames). Decision D-143. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/environments.py)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: Pipenv writes created-by = "pipenv" in the pylock.toml it generates (docs/pylock.md). pipenv install -e . writes the project itself as { path = ".", editable = true } (docs/pipfile.md), and Pipfile.lock keeps it as "path": ".". [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/utils/pylock.py)
- `extra.configTables`: Directives such as cool-down-period and allow_prereleases live in [pipenv]. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipenv-directives)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Only whole days (\<int>d) are accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Whole days only. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: "When the index does not provide upload-time metadata (e.g. most private mirrors) the setting is accepted but has no filtering effect." [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Every key but \_meta is a category (default, develop and custom ones) mapping names to entries: index packages have version, hashes and index; git entries git and ref; remote archives file; local projects path, and editable = true for editable installs (Pipfile "Packages Section"). The version is written as a specifier ("version": "==1.2.3"). The hashes of wheels and source distributions are listed together, so the lockfile does not show which packages are built. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfilelock-structure)
- `extra.commandLine`: pipenv install takes packages as arguments (without any it installs the Pipfile) and editable ones with -e; -r imports a requirements file. The options of install and the global flags of pipenv, read with argparse, which accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/cli/options.py)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: --index names a package index by URL or by a source name of the Pipfile; --pypi-mirror and PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR replace PyPI. --extra-pip-args hands arguments to pip, which may name another index, and Pipenv loads PIP\_\* variables from the .env file that PIPENV_DOTENV_LOCATION names (options.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: Pipfile.location returns project.s.PIPENV_PIPFILE when it is set, and only otherwise searches the working directory and its parents (find_pipfile, PIPENV_MAX_DEPTH); project_directory is str(Path(self.location).parent.absolute()), and Project.\_\_init\_\_ (pipenv/project.py) changes to it for every command but run. pipenv/environments.py: "If set, this specifies a custom Pipfile location. When running pipenv from a location other than the same directory where the Pipfile is located, instruct pipenv to find the Pipfile in the location specified by this environment variable"; the path is taken relative to the working directory and made absolute. pipenv/cli/options.py has no option that moves the project (--where only prints it). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/utils/pipfile.py)
- `extra.registrySettings`: Each [[source]] has name, url and verify_ssl. "all packages are mapped to a single package index for security reasons"; "To install a package from a specific index, you must match the name of the index" (torch = {version = "\*", index = "pytorch"} in [packages]); to use another index as the default, "simply omit PyPI from your sources". A package without index comes from the default index, the first source: Resolver.create in pipenv/utils/resolver.py takes project.sources.get_default_index()["name"], which is pipfile_sources()[0] (pipenv/utils/sources.py), and without [[source]] the default is https://pypi.org/simple (pipenv/project.py). With install_search_all_sources = true in [pipenv], "pipenv install and pipenv sync will search all configured sources for packages, but only during installation", so every source adds. Names are compared exactly (get_index_by_name), depcurfew without regard to case; package categories are any top-level table ([packages], [dev-packages] and custom ones). Variables in url are expanded by Pipenv (expand_url_credentials), so depcurfew cannot read such a URL. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/indexes.md)
- `extra.selection`: pipenv install --pre allows pre-releases (and records allow_prereleases in the Pipfile, routines/install.py). Pipenv installs with pip, which reads PIP_NO_BINARY and PIP_ONLY_BINARY like --no-binary and --only-binary (see buildSwitch). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/cli/options.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-28. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/CHANGELOG.md)

### Composer

- `cooldown.setting`: Withholds versions published within the period when composer update or require resolves dependencies (also init and create-project when they pick a constraint). Measured from the publication time the repository reports (published-time, which Packagist.org provides and package authors cannot influence); a Composer repository that lacks it makes the command fail unless require-published-time is false on it, and packages from VCS, path or artifact repositories use the author-set time of their composer.json. Never withheld: dev versions, locked packages a partial update keeps, platform packages and versions without any date. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#cooldown)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: config is root-only: "It is only used for projects." COMPOSER_HOME/config.json is merged under it (only its config and repositories keys), and "the local configuration in the project's composer.json always wins" (03-cli.md#composer-home-config-json). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/04-schema.md#config)
- `cooldown.unit`: "A duration string in the form "\<number> \<unit>" where the unit is one of second, minute, hour, day or week (lowercase, singular or plural - e.g. "7 days", "24 hours", "30 minutes", "1 week"), an integer number of seconds, or null to disable." [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#period)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Added a cooldown policy to withhold newly released package versions for a configurable period" under 2.11.0-RC1 (2026-10-22); 2.11.0 was released on 2026-10-29. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: "Defaults to null (no cooldown period). The policy only takes effect once a period is set." [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#period)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: "Packages listed under ignore bypass the cooldown policy." The ignore format of the other policies: a list of names, or an object of names to a reason, to { constraint, reason, on-block, on-audit } or to a list of such rules. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#cooldown)
- `cooldown.exclude.availableSince`: Part of the cooldown policy added in 2.11.0-RC1. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: "package names support wildcards (e.g. vendor/\*)". [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#cooldown)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Only the root package's scripts run (articles/scripts.md: "If a dependency of the root package specifies its own scripts, Composer does not execute those additional scripts"); dependency code runs during Composer commands through plugins, packages of type composer-plugin. allow-plugins (2.2.0) "Defaults to {} which does not allow any plugins to be loaded": a plugin it does not list makes Composer ask in an interactive run and fail in a non-interactive one, or skips it when the plugin declares plugin-optional (PluginManager::isPluginAllowed, articles/plugins.md). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: "Use this setting to allow only packages you trust to execute code." [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: Root-only, like every config option. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/04-schema.md#config)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: "As of Composer 2.2.0, the allow-plugins option adds a layer of security". [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `installScripts.allowList.format`: parseAllowedPlugins turns each key into a pattern; isPluginAllowed returns the value of the first pattern that matches, in the order written. Config::merge puts the keys of COMPOSER_HOME/config.json after the project's, the project's values winning. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Plugin/PluginManager.php)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: "You can also set the config option itself to false to disallow all plugins"; --no-plugins does the same for one command (03-cli.md#global-options). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `project.lockfiles`: JSON next to composer.json. With COMPOSER=\<name>.json Composer reads another manifest and writes \<name>.lock (03-cli.md#composer); depcurfew reads composer.json and composer.lock only. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/01-basic-usage.md#commit-your-composer-lock-file-to-version-control)
- `project.manifests`: The root package; repositories, config and scripts are read only from it. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/04-schema.md)
- `extra.environmentNames`: Platform::getEnv looks the name up with array_key_exists($name, $\_SERVER), then in $\_ENV, then with getenv($name), so outside Windows only that spelling counts: COMPOSER and COMPOSER_HOME, not Composer or composer (decision D-143). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Util/Platform.php)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-30. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.durationStrings`: parseDuration: an integer, or a string of digits (/^\\d+$/D), is a number of seconds; otherwise only /^(\\d+)\\s\*(second|minute|hour|day|week)s?$/D is accepted (lowercase, one unit). The string is matched as it is, so a space before or after the value (" 14 days") is not accepted. null, "", 0 and "0" mean no cooldown; any other value makes the command fail with "Invalid policy.cooldown.period format", and so does such a COMPOSER_POLICY_COOLDOWN_PERIOD. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Policy/CooldownPolicyConfig.php)
- `extra.durationUnits`: The documented examples are "7 days", "24 hours", "30 minutes" and "1 week"; depcurfew writes whole days, rounded up. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#period)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: "package names support wildcards (e.g. vendor/\*)" in ignore. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#cooldown)
- `extra.denyList`: "The values are true to allow and false to disallow while suppressing further warnings and prompts." [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `extra.cooldownTime`: getEffectiveDate returns the published date, else the release date (time). A Composer repository must give published-time while a cooldown is configured, unless require-published-time is false on it (05-repositories.md#require-published-time: "That field is set by the package author, so the protection is weaker"); ArtifactRepository drops a published-time from the archive's composer.json. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Policy/CooldownPolicyConfig.php)
- `extra.lockedVersions`: "The cooldown policy applies when resolving dependencies during composer update/require"; "Locked packages that are not being updated" are never withheld. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#cooldown)
- `extra.contentHash`: getContentHash hashes name, version, require, require-dev, conflict, replace, provide, minimum-stability, prefer-stable, repositories, extra, config.platform and config.policy ("policy changes which versions an update may pick, so changing it should flag the lock as outdated"; CHANGELOG 2.11.0-RC1, #13149). With another hash composer install warns that "The lock file is not up to date with the latest changes in composer.json" (Installer.php) and composer validate fails (03-cli.md#validate); composer update --lock "Overwrites the lock file hash to suppress warning about the lock file being out of date without updating package versions" (03-cli.md#update-u-upgrade). allow-plugins is not hashed. Locker::getContentHash at 2.10.3 hashes config.platform but not config.policy, so a hash written by Composer 2.10 or older differs from what 2.11 computes for a composer.json with config.policy (https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.10.3/src/Composer/Package/Locker.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Package/Locker.php)
- `extra.pluginApiVersion`: Locker writes PluginInterface::PLUGIN_API_VERSION of the Composer that writes composer.lock into plugin-api-version (Locker.php; CHANGELOG 1.10.0: "so third-party tools can know which Composer version was used to generate a lock file"). It is 2.11.0 at 2.11.1 ("Bumped composer-plugin-api to 2.11.0" under 2.11.0-RC1) and 2.9.0 at 2.10.3, so a lower value was written by a Composer older than 2.11.0. It names the Composer that last wrote the lock, not every Composer that installs it. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Plugin/PluginInterface.php)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Each entry of packages and packages-dev has name, version, type and the source { type, url, reference } and dist { type, url, reference, shasum } it installs from, time and, from a repository that gives it, published-time. A package of a path repository has dist type path with the path as url (PathRepository.php); one of an artifact repository has the archive type and its file path as url (ArtifactRepository.php). Composer reads name and type in lower case (BasePackage::\_\_construct and ArrayLoader::configureObject: strtolower), so "Composer-Plugin" is a plugin too. Plugins are packages of type composer-plugin (04-schema.md#type), and Composer also loads the legacy type composer-installer as a plugin, under the same allow-plugins check (PluginInstaller::supports, PluginManager::registerPackage). A plugin whose extra.plugin-optional is true is skipped without a question when Composer runs without a terminal and it is not allowed (PluginManager::isPluginAllowed: elseif ($optional) return false). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Package/Dumper/ArrayDumper.php)
- `extra.legacyLockPlugins`: parseAllowedPlugins returns no rules when allow-plugins is empty ({} or missing) and composer.lock has a plugin-api-version below 2.2.0, or none (Locker::getPluginApi returns 1.1.0 then). In that mode Composer 2.2 to 2.9 load every plugin without asking when run without a terminal ("if no config is defined we allow all plugins for BC", PluginManager.php at 2.9.8); since 2.10.0-RC1 Composer stops with an error there instead ("Enforce allow-plugins even in non-interactive mode for very old pre-2.2 lock files", #12764 in CHANGELOG.md) and asks in a terminal. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Plugin/PluginManager.php)
- `extra.manifestSyntax`: JsonFile::parseJson at 2.11.1 reads composer.json with PHP's json_decode($json, true) and, when it fails, reports the error with JsonFile::validateSyntax (seld/jsonlint), so a comment or a trailing comma in composer.json stops every Composer command; json_decode takes strict JSON (RFC 8259), which has neither. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Json/JsonFile.php)
- `extra.sourceInstall`: getAvailableSources offers source when the package has a source type and dist when it has a dist type; a locked package without a dist is installed from its source, a checkout of the VCS repository the entry names, whatever repository composer.json declares. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Downloader/DownloadManager.php)
- `extra.registryDistHosts`: The archives Composer's VCS drivers give a package of the hosts Composer knows by default (github-domains github.com, gitlab-domains gitlab.com, forgejo-domains codeberg.org in Config.php, and Bitbucket): GitHubDriver::getDist https://api.github.com/repos/\<owner>/\<repo>/zipball/\<ref>, GitLabDriver::getDist \<scheme>://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/\<id>/repository/archive.zip, GitBitbucketDriver::getDist https://bitbucket.org/\<owner>/\<repo>/get/\<ref>.zip, ForgejoDriver::getDist \<host>/api/v1/repos/\<owner>/\<repo>/archive/\<ref>.zip; GitDriver::getDist gives none. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Repository/Vcs/GitHubDriver.php)
- `extra.repositoryArchiveHosts`: The hosts the archives of a Composer repository other than Packagist.org come from, by the host of the repository URL. WPackagist (the Composer repository https://wpackagist.org that its README tells composer.json to declare) gives each plugin version the dist https://downloads.wordpress.org/plugin/\<name>.\<version>.zip (Plugin::getDownloadUrl) and each theme version https://downloads.wordpress.org/theme/\<name>.\<version>.zip (Theme::getDownloadUrl in src/Entity/Theme.php), with a dist of type zip and a source of type svn on plugins.svn.wordpress.org or themes.svn.wordpress.org (Package::getPackageVersion in src/Entity/Package.php), all at commit 9b5db4a of the develop branch (the repository has no tags). The archive host of packages.drupal.org could not be read at its source (drupal.org is not reachable from where this was checked), so it is not listed. [↗](https://github.com/outlandishideas/wpackagist/blob/9b5db4a9e7477c97de1c8562498ecfff4cab9678/src/Entity/Plugin.php)
- `extra.branchVersions`: A locked version names a branch, not a release, when it starts with dev- or ends with -dev: "Composer automatically adds a -dev suffix to all numeric branches and prefixes all other branches imported from a VCS repository with dev-" (versions.md, Stabilities); a tag gives its own version (v7.3.4 or 3.9.0, as the tag is written). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/articles/versions.md#stabilities)
- `extra.repositoryTypes`: The repository classes of createRepositoryManager; 05-repositories.md describes composer, vcs (with the drivers bitbucket, github, gitlab, perforce, fossil, git, svn and hg; git-bitbucket is deprecated), path, package and artifact, and { "packagist.org": false } to disable Packagist.org. repositories is root-only. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Repository/RepositoryFactory.php)
- `extra.weakeningSettings`: "Set to false to disable all dependency policy enforcement"; malware "block: Defaults to true", "block-scope: Defaults to all", update blocks "only during update/require/remove"; cooldown block "Set to false to skip blocking for a cooldown period entirely". policy, cooldown and malware are compared with false exactly; block is read with PHP's (bool) cast after ?? true, so false, 0, "", "0" and [] turn blocking off, while a missing or null block keeps the default and "false" is true (Config.php, MalwarePolicyConfig.php, CooldownPolicyConfig.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#policy)
- `extra.transportSettings`: secure-http "Defaults to true. If set to true only HTTPS URLs are allowed to be downloaded via Composer"; disable-tls "Defaults to false. If set to true all HTTPS URLs will be tried with HTTP instead" and "will implicitly disable the secure-http option". Config::get reads both as $value !== "false" && (bool) $value (Config.php), so "false", false, 0, "", "0" and null are false. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#secure-http)
- `extra.allowAllPlugins`: "or true to allow all plugins to run (NOT recommended)". BasePackage::packageNameToRegexp turns a key into {^...$}i with \* as .\*, so keys match without regard to case and \* matches / too: a key made only of \* with at most one / between them ("\*", "\*/\*") with true allows every vendor/name plugin that no earlier key names. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/06-config.md#allow-plugins)
- `extra.repositoryWeakening`: require-published-time "Defaults to true"; false falls "back to the time field of each package's composer.json. That field is set by the package author, so the protection is weaker." Only false counts (ComposerRepository.php). "Set filter: false to opt out of every list this repository advertises", or an object that sets a list name to false to skip that list (#filter); Packagist.org advertises the list malware (repo.packagist.org/packages.json). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/05-repositories.md#require-published-time)
- `extra.environmentOverrides`: COMPOSER_POLICY: "Set to 0 to disable all dependency policy enforcement" (read with Platform::getBoolEnv: 0, false and off are false). COMPOSER_NO_BLOCKING and COMPOSER_NO_SECURITY_BLOCKING: BaseCommand::createPolicyConfig reads both with Platform::getBoolEnv(..., false), which takes only 0, 1, false, true, off and on and makes update, require, install, remove and create-project stop with "Invalid value for COMPOSER_NO_BLOCKING" for any other value but ""; 1, true and on turn blocking off there (PolicyConfig::withBlockingDisabled: advisories, malware, abandoned packages, the cooldown and custom lists). BaseCommand::initialize also sets --no-blocking and --no-security-blocking when (bool) getenv() is true, so false and off turn blocking off as well for the commands that have the option (update, require, install, remove, create-project). COMPOSER_POLICY_COOLDOWN_PERIOD "overrides the configured period", 0 disabling it; COMPOSER_POLICY_COOLDOWN_BLOCK and COMPOSER_POLICY_MALWARE_BLOCK set 0 to disable blocking (PolicyConfig.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/03-cli.md#environment-variables)
- `extra.packagistApi`: "Using the Composer v2 metadata": GET https://repo.packagist.org/p2/[vendor]/[package].json gives {"packages": {"[vendor]/[package]": [versions]}, "minified": "composer/2.0"}, each version with version, "time": [release datetime, as set by the package author] and "published-time": [datetime the version was published on packagist.org, not influenced by the package author]; the list "requires you to use Composer\\MetadataMinifier\\MetadataMinifier::expand"; "The p2/$vendor/$package.json file contains only tagged releases", branches are in p2/$vendor/$package\~dev.json; package pages are https://packagist.org/packages/[vendor]/[package]. https://repo.packagist.org is the url of the packagist.org repository Composer adds by default (Config::$defaultRepositories at 2.11.1). Composer reads a 404 as a package the repository does not have (ComposerRepository.php), expands a list marked composer/2.0 and loads each version with ArrayLoader.php: version_normalized (else the version normalized), type (lowercased, library when missing), time, published-time (an integer or a non-empty string) and abandoned (true or the name of a replacement). [↗](https://packagist.org/apidoc)
- `extra.metadataMinifier`: MetadataMinifier::expand: the first entry is a whole version; each later entry holds only the keys that changed since the previous version, a key with the value "\_\_unset" being removed; while the version built so far is empty (PHP: !$expandedVersion), the next entry is taken whole again. Composer 2.11.1 locks composer/metadata-minifier 1.0.1. [↗](https://github.com/composer/metadata-minifier/blob/1.0.1/src/MetadataMinifier.php)
- `extra.versionConstraints`: Exact version (1.0.2); ranges with >, >=, \<, \<=, != separated by a space or comma (logical AND) or || (logical OR, and | for backwards compatibility), AND binding tighter; the hyphenated range 1.0 - 2.0 (>=1.0.0 \<2.1, a partial right end completed with a wildcard); wildcard 1.0.\* (>=1.0 \<1.1); \~1.2 (>=1.2 \<2.0.0), \~1.2.3 (>=1.2.3 \<1.3.0), \~1 like \~1.0; ^1.2.3 (>=1.2.3 \<2.0.0), ^0.3 (>=0.3.0 \<0.4.0), ^0.0.3 (>=0.0.3 \<0.0.4); stability flags @\<stability>; a branch as dev-\<branch>, or \<version>.x-dev for a branch named like a version (versions.md). composer/semver 3.6.0 (src/VersionParser.php, which Composer 2.11.1 locks, https://github.com/composer/semver/blob/3.6.0/src/VersionParser.php) also reads = and == as exact, \<> as !=, x, X and \* as wildcards, "\<version> as \<alias>", #\<commit> after a branch, and appends -dev to the bound of \< and >= without an explicit stability, so that pre-releases of the bound are below it. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/articles/versions.md)
- `extra.stabilities`: minimum-stability "defaults to stable"; the options in order of stability are dev, alpha, beta, RC and stable, and stability flags allow another stability per package. BasePackage::STABILITIES at 2.11.1 gives the priorities (stable 0 to dev 20); StabilityFilter::isPackageAcceptable accepts a version whose stability priority is at most the flag of its package, else at most the minimum stability. RootPackageLoader::extractStabilityFlags takes the least stable @\<stability> of a requirement as its flag, else the stability of an explicit unstable version in it (2.0.0-beta1) when that is less stable than the minimum stability. VersionParser::parseStability (composer/semver 3.6.0): a version starting with dev- or ending with -dev is dev; a modifier beta or b is beta, alpha or a is alpha, RC is RC (in any case), anything else (patch, pl, p, none) is stable. Versions without a stability suffix are stable (articles/versions.md#stabilities). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/04-schema.md#minimum-stability-root-only)
- `extra.versionComparison`: Composer orders normalized versions with PHP's version_compare (VersionSelector.php at 2.11.1; Constraint::versionCompare in composer/semver 3.6.0, where a dev- branch only equals itself). php_canonicalize_version replaces -, \_ and + with a dot and puts a dot between a digit and a non-digit; the parts are compared one by one, numbers as numbers, words by the first special form they start with (dev \< alpha = a \< beta = b \< RC = rc \< # \< pl = p; a word that starts with none is lowest), a number against a word as the form # (#N#); when one version has parts left, a number makes it the greater and a word is compared with #N#. [↗](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/php-8.4.0/ext/standard/versioning.c)
- `extra.commandLine`: composer require (alias r) takes packages as "vendor/package:2.\*" or vendor/package2:dev-master, and picks a constraint itself for a package without one; composer global \<command> runs the command "as if you were running them from the COMPOSER_HOME directory"; composer create-project \<package> [\<directory>] [\<version>]; composer update (u, upgrade) takes packages, wildcards and constraints vendor/package:2.0.1, and --with foo/bar:1.0.0. "As Composer uses symfony/console you can call commands by short name if it's not ambiguous" (commandNames). The options with a value of require, update, create-project, install, config and repository (InputOption VALUE_REQUIRED or VALUE_OPTIONAL in src/Composer/Command/\*Command.php at 2.11.1) and the global --working-dir (-d) of src/Composer/Console/Application.php; symfony/console v5.4.55 (Input/ArgvInput.php) groups short options (-nd dir), takes a value attached (-ddir, --working-dir=dir) or the next word when it does not start with -, accepts options before and after the command, reads every word after -- as an argument and does not shorten long options. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/03-cli.md)
- `extra.commandNames`: Application::find: an exact command name or alias; otherwise every name and alias that starts with the word (for each part between colons, a name with more parts too), first with case and then without (ASCII letters only, PCRE without u), of which one must match the word whole; an alias is left out when the name of its command is in the list, a hidden command (\_complete) when others remain; one name is run, more are ambiguous (an error) and none is not defined. The names and aliases are those of Composer's getDefaultCommands (src/Composer/Console/Application.php at 2.11.1, setName and setAliases in each src/Composer/Command/\*Command.php) and of symfony/console (help, list, completion and the hidden \_complete). Scripts of composer.json (extra.scriptCommands) and commands of plugins are added as commands too, unless a command of that name exists. [↗](https://github.com/symfony/console/blob/v5.4.55/Application.php)
- `extra.commandArguments`: parseNameVersionPairs: an argument is split at the first =, : or space after the name; an argument without one takes the next argument as its constraint when that has no /, no \* next to a letter, digit, \_, / or - and is no platform package. require and create-project read their packages so (RequireCommand via PackageDiscoveryTrait, CreateProjectCommand::installRootPackage); update moves an argument with a constraint (\\S+[ =:]\\S+) to the temporary constraints of --with and takes lock, nothing and mirrors as --lock (UpdateCommand.php). create-project takes its stability from --stability (-s), else from the @\<stability> of its version, else from the version itself. Platform packages are PlatformRepository::PLATFORM_PACKAGE_REGEX (case-insensitive). The name pattern is the one 04-schema.md#name gives (ValidatingArrayLoader::hasPackageNamingError checks the same with possessive quantifiers); Composer lowercases the names it looks up. Both are written here as patterns of the same names whose repeated group starts with its separator (X+(?:[sep]X+)\*, decision D-136), so that a long name that fails at its end is read in linear time: X(?:[sep]?X+)\* can split a run of letters in exponentially many ways. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Package/Version/VersionParser.php)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: create-project --repository "Provide a custom repository to search for the package, which will be used instead of packagist" (and --repository-url, CreateProjectCommand.php at 2.11.1). COMPOSER sets the file name of composer.json, whose repositories then apply (#composer). COMPOSER_HOME sets the home directory (Factory::getHomeDir: "if ($home = Platform::getEnv('COMPOSER_HOME')) return $home"), whose config.json Factory::createConfig merges under the configuration of every project, its repositories included (03-cli.md#composer-home-config-json), and in which composer global runs, with the composer.json there (GlobalCommand::prepareSubcommandInput changes to the home directory of the configuration). Other commands take their repositories from composer.json only. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/03-cli.md#create-project)
- `extra.installOverrides`: createPolicyConfig: --no-blocking, --no-security-blocking (deprecated), COMPOSER_NO_BLOCKING and COMPOSER_NO_SECURITY_BLOCKING "disable ALL blocking (advisories + malware + abandoned + cooldown + custom)" (PolicyConfig::withBlockingDisabled); --no-cooldown disables only the cooldown blocking. initialize sets --no-blocking and --no-security-blocking on each command that has them when (bool) getenv() is true, so for every value but "" and "0" ("false" and "off" too); createPolicyConfig also reads both with Platform::getBoolEnv, which makes the command fail for a value other than 0, 1, false, true, off and on (src/Composer/Util/Platform.php), so such a value installs nothing. COMPOSER_POLICY (Config::get), COMPOSER_POLICY_COOLDOWN_BLOCK and COMPOSER_POLICY_MALWARE_BLOCK (PolicyConfig::fromConfig) are read with getBoolEnv: 0, false and off turn them off. COMPOSER_POLICY_COOLDOWN_PERIOD replaces the period (CooldownPolicyConfig::getEnvPeriod, in the syntax of durationStrings). create-project --no-secure-http "Disable the secure-http config option temporarily while installing the root package" (03-cli.md#create-project): CreateProjectCommand::installRootPackage merges secure-http false into the configuration it installs the project package with, and secure-http "Defaults to true. If set to true only HTTPS URLs are allowed to be downloaded via Composer" (06-config.md#secure-http). The options are on require, update, install, create-project and remove (03-cli.md). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Command/BaseCommand.php)
- `extra.configCommands`: composer config [options] [setting-key] [setting-value1] ... changes a setting of composer.json (with --global, -g, of COMPOSER_HOME/config.json; with --file, -f, of that file), --unset removes one and --editor (-e) opens the file; with a key alone it shows the value (src/Composer/Command/ConfigCommand.php at 2.11.1). composer repository (repo) add, remove (rm, delete), set-url (seturl), enable and disable change the repositories, list (ls, show) and get-url (geturl) only read them (RepositoryCommand.php). composer policy add-source changes config.policy (PolicyCommand.php). config, repository and policy all take --global (-g, "Apply command to the global config file") and --file (-f, "If you want to choose a different composer.json or config.json"). The same commands after composer global change the files of COMPOSER_HOME: GlobalCommand runs them in the home directory, where composer.json is the one of composer global and config.json the configuration that Factory::createConfig merges under that of every project. depcurfew reads neither file (decision D-133), so a change there counts also without an install next to it (unread). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/03-cli.md#config)
- `extra.configCommandValues`: composer config KEY VALUE writes the setting into config of composer.json (JsonConfigSource::addConfigSetting at 2.11.1; --global, -g, --file and -f write another file, configCommands). ConfigCommand::execute at 2.11.1 takes a key of the form policy.\<list> (policy.cooldown, policy.malware) and the block keys (policy.cooldown.block, policy.malware.block), secure-http, disable-tls and allow-plugins only with true, false, 1 or 0 ($booleanValidator) and stores $val !== 'false' && (bool) $val ($booleanNormalizer), so false and 0 are false; policy.cooldown.period takes a duration CooldownPolicyConfig::parseDuration reads, or null or the empty text for none, a number as an integer; policy.malware.block-scope one of all, update and install, as written. addConfigSetting nests a key that starts with policy. at its dots under config (policy.cooldown false gives "config": {"policy": {"cooldown": false}}), replacing the object that was there. So composer config policy.cooldown false in CI turns the cooldown off in the composer.json the later commands read. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Command/ConfigCommand.php)
- `extra.applicationOptions`: Composer finds the command name before it knows the command (getCommandNameBeforeBinding: "This ensures we can find the correct command name even if a global input option is present before it"): it binds the words to the input definition of the application, ignoring the error that stops the binding (an option it does not define, a missing value, a second argument), and takes $input->getFirstArgument(). The definition is that of symfony/console (Application::getDefaultInputDefinition at v5.4.55: the command argument, --help -h, --quiet -q, --verbose -v|vv|vvv, --version -V, --ansi|--no-ansi, --no-interaction -n) with the --profile, --no-plugins, --no-scripts, --working-dir -d (with a value) and --no-cache of Composer. ArgvInput::getFirstArgument (v5.4.55) passes over each word that starts with -, and also over the next word when the option is one the binding set (a long name, or the last letter of a short one) and that word equals its bound value; the first other word is the command. So only -d and --working-dir take the word after them before the command, an option of a command (--ignore-platform-req) does not, and that command later binds the word after it as its value (Input/ArgvInput.php: parse, addLongOption, parseShortOptionSet). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Console/Application.php)
- `extra.scriptCommands`: doRunComposer registers the scripts of the composer.json it runs with (Factory::getComposerFile, after -d) as commands when the command word is not the exact name of a command Composer found before (mayNeedScriptCommand: "$rawCommandName !== $commandName", so also for an alias, an abbreviation, another case or a word that names no command) or the command is run-script. Each key of scripts that is no event (the constants of src/Composer/Script/ScriptEvents.php, compared in upper case with - as \_) and not already a command or alias ($this->has($script): "A script named ... would override a Composer command and has been skipped") becomes a ScriptAliasCommand with the aliases that scripts-aliases gives it. Application::add of symfony/console (v5.4.55) maps the name and each alias to it, over an alias or name of another command; Command::setName and setAliases reject a name that is not parts without a colon separated by single colons (validateName), and ScriptAliasCommand an alias that is not a string, which stops Composer. find() then resolves the word among all of them: the exact name or alias, else the names that start with it. ScriptAliasCommand runs the script as composer run-script does (src/Composer/Command/ScriptAliasCommand.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Console/Application.php)
- `extra.scriptAliases`: 2.7.0: "Added \`scripts-aliases\` top level key in composer.json to define aliases for custom scripts you defined" (#11666). Application::doRunComposer at 2.6.6 and 2.2.25 (src/Composer/Console/Application.php) registers each script of composer.json as a ScriptAliasCommand without aliases ($this->add(new Command\\ScriptAliasCommand($script, $description))), and from 2.7.0 with $composer['scripts-aliases'\][$script]. So on Composer 2.2 LTS to 2.6 a word that scripts-aliases gives a script is still the Composer command or alias of that name (r is require). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.rootStability`: RootPackageLoader reads minimum-stability of the root composer.json through VersionParser::normalizeStability (composer/semver 3.6.0: lower case, one of stable, RC, beta, alpha and dev, else an exception) and prefer-stable as (bool) $config['prefer-stable']. composer require without a constraint takes the minimum stability of composer.json (PackageDiscoveryTrait::getMinimumStability) for the versions it considers and asks VersionSelector::findBestCandidate for a version with the preferred stability "stable" under prefer-stable, else the minimum stability (RequireCommand.php): versions at least that stable come first, the highest of them, else the most stable of the others. The solver orders the versions a constraint allows with DefaultPolicy::versionCompare: with prefer-stable the more stable one first, else the higher version, which a branch (dev-main aliased 3.x-dev) is. All at 2.11.1 (src/Composer/Package/Version/VersionSelector.php, src/Composer/DependencyResolver/DefaultPolicy.php, src/Composer/Command/PackageDiscoveryTrait.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Package/Loader/RootPackageLoader.php)
- `extra.installPreference`: DownloadManager::getAvailableSources offers source before dist (each only with a type) and reverses them "in case dist is the preferred source for this package": unless preferSource, when preferDist or resolvePackageInstallPreference says dist. BaseCommand::getPreferredInstallOptions sets preferSource for config.preferred-install "source" and preferDist for "dist" (Config::$defaultConfig has "dist"), and neither for "auto", another string or an object; Factory::createDownloadManager hands an object to setPreferences. resolvePackageInstallPreference takes the first key that matches the package name ({^pattern$}i with \* as .\*): "dist", or "auto" for a version that is not dev, gives dist, any other value source; with no match, source for a dev version (a branch) and dist for others. Config::merge turns the default "dist" into {"\*": "dist"} under an object of composer.json and moves the "\*" key to the end. --prefer-source, --prefer-dist and --prefer-install override it for one command. All at 2.11.1 (src/Composer/Command/BaseCommand.php, src/Composer/Factory.php, src/Composer/Config.php). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Downloader/DownloadManager.php)
