- `extra.sourceFallback`: 2.10.0: "Disabled automatic fallback to source checkout if dist/zip install fails, we have introduced a new source-fallback config option as a temporary way to restore the old behavior" (#12885); 2.11.0-RC1: "Removed the source-fallback config option which was added in 2.10 as a temporary measure, dist installs no longer fall back to source" (#13050). DownloadManager::download at 2.11.1 only falls back from source to dist ("Only fallback from dist to source is risky as it can silently switch to less-trusted code"). Composer before 2.10.0 installs a package from its source when the download of its archive fails. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.registrySourceHosts`: The host of the source that the VCS driver gives a package whose archive comes from a host of registryDistHosts: GitHubDriver::getSource https://github.com/\<owner>/\<repo>.git (git@github.com:\<owner>/\<repo>.git for a private repository) beside its archive on api.github.com; GitLabDriver::getSource the http_url_to_repo or ssh_url_to_repo of the project on gitlab.com; GitBitbucketDriver::getSource the URL of the repository on bitbucket.org; ForgejoDriver::getSource its clone URL on codeberg.org (src/Composer/Repository/Vcs/\*Driver.php at 2.11.1). [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Repository/Vcs/GitHubDriver.php)
- `extra.sourceHostAliases`: GitHubDriver::initialize at 2.11.1 reads the host of the repository URL in lower case and takes www.github.com for github.com ("if ($this->originUrl === 'www.github.com') { $this->originUrl = 'github.com'; }"), and GitHubDriver::supports compares the host without www. with github-domains. GitLabDriver::determineOrigin compares the host (with its port) with gitlab-domains as written, GitBitbucketDriver::supports takes only https://bitbucket.org/…, and ForgejoDriver compares the host with forgejo-domains as written (src/Composer/Repository/Vcs/\*Driver.php at 2.11.1), so only GitHub has such a host. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/src/Composer/Repository/Vcs/GitHubDriver.php)
- `extra.directoryOptions`: "--working-dir (-d): If specified, use the given directory as working directory." Application::doRunComposer changes to it before it reads composer.json (src/Composer/Console/Application.php at 2.11.1). Without it and without composer.json in the current directory (and for a command other than list, init, about, help, diagnose, self-update, global, create-project and outdated), Composer looks for the nearest parent with one, stopping before the home directory and the root of the file system: an interactive run asks whether to use it, use-parent-dir true uses it without asking, and a run without a terminal (stdin not a TTY, or COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION) with the default use-parent-dir "prompt" (Config::$defaultConfig in src/Composer/Config.php) stays in the current directory and only says so; with --working-dir it never looks at a parent. It then registers the scripts (Application.php) and reads minimum-stability (PackageDiscoveryTrait::getMinimumStability) of Factory::getComposerFile() in the directory it is in. getNewWorkingDir reads the directory with $input->getParameterOption(['--working-dir', '-d'], null, true), which in symfony/console v5.4.55 (Input/ArgvInput.php) takes the first word, up to --, that is --working-dir or -d (then the next word) or starts with --working-dir= or -d (then the rest of the word); a grouped -nd dir does not start with -d, so Composer stays where it is, although the command later binds -n and -d dir as options. [↗](https://github.com/composer/composer/blob/2.11.1/doc/03-cli.md#global-options)

### Bundler

- `cooldown.setting`: The cooldown: keyword of a source call in the Gemfile (source "https://rubygems.org", cooldown: 7): Dsl#source raises InvalidOption unless it is an Integer of 0 or more. It applies to the versions that come from that source (Source::Rubygems::Remote#effective_cooldown), cooldown: 0 exempts the source. The cooldown setting (bundle config set cooldown N, BUNDLE_COOLDOWN) and --cooldown N take its place for every source, also one with cooldown: 0 (extra.cooldownSetting). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/dsl.rb)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The keyword is written in the Gemfile, or in gems.rb, which Bundler reads in its place (extra.gemfileNames). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/shared_helpers.rb)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: bundle install, update, add and outdated take --cooldown N since 4.0.13, bundle lock and bundle cache since 4.0.18 ("Add --cooldown flag to bundle lock and bundle cache", #9725); method_option "cooldown" of these commands in lib/bundler/cli.rb. N is a whole number of days of 0 or more (CLI::Common.validate_cooldown!); it overrides the cooldown setting and the keyword of every source for that run, and 0 turns the cooldown off (bundle-install(1)). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.unit`: Resolver#cooldown_excluded? holds back a version while (now - created_at) \< days \* 86_400. The keyword and the flag take whole days only; the setting is read with to_i (extra.cooldownSetting). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/resolver.rb)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Add \`cooldown\` to delay newly published gem" (#9576) under 4.0.13 / 2026-06-03. Bundler 4.0.12 and 2.7.2 ignore an option of source they do not know without a word (extra.olderVersions). Until 4.0.14 the keyword of a Gemfile source was lost once Gemfile.lock existed (extra.cooldownWithLockfile). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: "Defaults to unset (no cooldown)"; the blog post calls the feature opt-in. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/bundle-config.1.ronn)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: The resolver holds back every version younger than the cooldown, a fix included (Resolver#cooldown_excluded? has no exception); the post names --cooldown 0 as the way to take "the freshest release" when "a fix lands for an actively exploited 0-day". [↗](https://blog.rubygems.org/2026/06/03/cooldown-let-new-gems-be-vetted.html)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Bundler::RubyGemsGemInstaller#install builds the native extensions of a gem whose gemspec lists any (build_extensions if spec.extensions.any?); Gem::Ext::Builder runs the extconf.rb, configure, Rakefile or mkrf_conf, CMakeLists.txt or Cargo.toml of the gem (lib/rubygems/ext/builder.rb at the same tag), code of the gem that runs when it is installed. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/rubygems_gem_installer.rb)
- `project.lockfiles`: SharedHelpers#default_lockfile: gems.locked for gems.rb, else the name of the Gemfile with .lock; BUNDLE_LOCKFILE names another file. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/shared_helpers.rb)
- `project.manifests`: SharedHelpers#gemfile_names; BUNDLE_GEMFILE names another file. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/shared_helpers.rb)
- `extra.latestVersion`: {"version":"4.0.23"} on 2026-11-03; 4.0.23 / 2026-10-14 in bundler/CHANGELOG.md. 4.1.0.beta3 (2026-10-28) is a pre-release. [↗](https://rubygems.org/api/v1/versions/bundler/latest.json)
- `extra.gemfileNames`: SharedHelpers#find_gemfile looks for gems.rb, then Gemfile, from the current directory up; with both in one directory Bundler warns ("Multiple gemfiles (gems.rb and Gemfile) detected") and reads gems.rb. find_file takes a name only when File.file? is true, so a directory (or another entry that is not a file) of that name is skipped; a symlink to a file counts. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/shared_helpers.rb)
- `extra.lockfileExists`: Definition#lockfile_exists? is lockfile && File.exist?(lockfile): any entry of that name counts, and a symlink is followed. Bundler reads the lockfile from there; depcurfew only tests whether it is there and never reads or edits it for the cooldown. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/definition.rb)
- `extra.gemfileEvaluation`: Dsl#eval_gemfile reads the Gemfile with Bundler.read_file (File.open(file, "r:UTF-8"), lib/bundler.rb) and runs it with instance_eval(contents, gemfile, 1), so Ruby's parser decides what in it is code (extra.rubySyntax). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/dsl.rb)
- `extra.rubySyntax`: How Ruby's lexer (parse.y) reads what decides where code ends. nextc reads \\r\\n as one newline everywhere (parser_cr), also inside a literal delimited by \\r, which only a \\r alone ends; a \\r alone between tokens is a space. parser_yylex ends the script at NUL, ^D (\\004) or ^Z (\\032) where a token starts, and at a line that is exactly \_\_END\_\_ (whole_match_p, with \\r\\n allowed); =begin at the start of a line starts a comment that ends with a line starting with =end (word_match_p: followed by whitespace, the end of the line, NUL, ^D or ^Z); # starts a comment to the end of the line. parse_percent: % starts a literal where an expression begins (IS_BEG), or after a method name with a space before % and none after it (IS_SPCARG), otherwise it is an operator; its type letter is one of Q, q, W, w, I, i, x, r, s (none means Q), the delimiter is any ASCII character that is no letter or digit, and ( [ { \< pair with ) ] } > and nest (tokadd_string). heredoc_identifier: \<\< with - or \~ and an identifier of letters, digits, \_ or non-ASCII characters, or any text in ', " or \` quotes on that line; not after a value (IS_END), after . or class, or after a method name without a space; here_document: the body starts on the line after the one with \<\<, after the bodies of earlier heredocs of that line, and ends at a line that is exactly the identifier (with - and \~ after leading whitespace, never with trailing spaces); in a heredoc with escapes a line after one that ends with a backslash is no terminator. Strings in double quotes, \`, %Q, %W, %I, %x, %r, /, :" and heredocs without ' interpolate #{...}, #@var and #$var (parser_peek_variable_name, is_global_name_punct). parse_qmark: ? starts a character literal unless a value comes before it, a space follows or two identifier characters follow; \\u{...} holds hex digits and spaces. The keywords set the lexer state as defs/keywords lists them (EXPR_END, EXPR_BEG, EXPR_VALUE, EXPR_MID, EXPR_ARG, EXPR_FNAME, EXPR_CLASS); if, unless, while, until and rescue are modifiers unless an expression begins there (EXPR_BEG, after a label or after class: parse_ident), so also after return, break, next and rescue (EXPR_MID). The grammar closes with end what begin, case, class, def, do, for, if, module, unless, until and while open when they are no modifiers, except a method defined with = after its name or its parameters (endless def); the do after the condition of while, until and for belongs to the loop (keyword_do_cond, COND_P, which ( [ { reset); ( [ { are closed by ) ] }. parse_ident: a lower-case name lexes as a local variable (EXPR_END) when one of that name was assigned before (lvar_defined) and as a method call otherwise, so %, /, \<\<, ? and : after such a name and a space can be read two ways. parse_numeric: 0x, 0b, 0o and 0d prefixes, a leading 0 alone means octal (010 is 8), single underscores between digits, a fraction and an exponent only before a digit, and the suffixes r and i only when no letter, digit or \_ follows (number_literal_suffix), so the number of 1end and 1do ends before the keyword. Prism, the default parser of Ruby 3.4, ends the script, reads \_\_END\_\_, \\r\\n, numbers, keywords and heredoc identifiers and terminators the same way (prism/prism.c at the same tag); where it reads otherwise, extra.rubyParsers says. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_7/parse.y)
- `extra.rubyParsers`: NEWS for Ruby 3.4.0: "The default parser is now Prism. To use the conventional parser, use the command-line argument \`--parser=parse.y\`" [Feature #20564]; Ruby 3.3 has parse.y as the default and --parser=prism "for debugging only" (NEWS.md at v3_3_0), and Ruby 4.0 still sets RB_DEFAULT_PARSER_PRISM (iseq.c at v4.0.9). eval_make_iseq in vm_eval.c compiles a string to eval with Prism when it is the default (rb_ruby_prism_p), so the instance_eval that runs the Gemfile uses it too. Where the two read the same text differently (prism/prism.c and parse.y at v3_4_7; prism.c at v4.0.9 the same): lex_question_mark reads ? before a character that is not a letter or digit of Unicode (alnum_char) as a character literal even when an identifier character follows, where parse_qmark reads a ternary for any character beyond ASCII before an identifier character (?€or is a ternary for parse.y, ?€ and the name or for Prism), and with an encoding magic comment the two count the bytes of such a character differently; =begin starts a comment for Prism only before whitespace or NUL, for parse.y also before ^D and ^Z (word_match_p); $0 followed by identifier characters is one global name for parse.y and an error for Prism 3.4 (lex_global_variable). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_7/NEWS.md)
- `extra.lineContinuation`: NEWS for Ruby 4.0.0: "Logical binary operators (\`||\`, \`&&\`, \`and\` and \`or\`) at the beginning of a line continue the previous line, like fluent dot" [Feature #20925]. parse.y (leading_logical; and and or only as whole words, peek_word_at) and prism/prism.c (PM_OPTIONS_VERSION_CRUBY_4_0) at v4.0.9 look for them where they look for a leading . or &.: after the newline that ends a statement, past spaces and comment lines, not past a blank line; .. there is a range, no call. So in Ruby 4.0 source "https://rubygems.org", cooldown: 7 followed by a line && 0 gives the source cooldown: 0; Ruby 3.4 reports a syntax error for such a line. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v4.0.9/NEWS.md)
- `extra.stringToInteger`: String#to_i (rb_str_to_inum, base 10) calls rb_int_parse_cstr with RB_INT_PARSE_DEFAULT: it skips leading whitespace (ISSPACE), takes one + or -, skips a 0d or 0D prefix, then reads decimal digits with single underscores between them and stops at anything else (a second underscore, a letter, a dot, a quote); with no digit the result is 0. So "0x10", "0o14", "true", "\~" and "[0]" read as 0, "1e3" and "1e400" as 1, "0d14" and "1_4" as 14. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_7/bignum.c)
- `extra.configFormat`: Settings#load_config reads .bundle/config with Gem::YAMLSerializer.load (Settings#serializer_class in lib/bundler/settings.rb; Bundler's own lib/bundler/yaml_serializer.rb is the same), a line reader, not YAML. HASH_REGEX takes as the key the text before the last colon that is followed by whitespace or the end of the line and comes before the first #, and as the value the rest after one optional space, without its quotes only when it starts and ends with the same quote; strip_comment then cuts the value at its first # and strips it, unless the value starts with #. A key with an empty value starts a nested map, the number of leading spaces / 2 is the depth, a later line of a key replaces an earlier one, and [] is an empty list. load_config replaces . in keys with \_\_, so only a key spelled exactly BUNDLE_COOLDOWN at the top level is the setting; Settings#converted_value reads its text with to_i (extra.stringToInteger), and a map or a list there makes Bundler stop with an error. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/lib/rubygems/yaml_serializer.rb)
- `extra.cliCommands`: The commands of Bundler::CLI (desc) and Thor's help, with COMMAND_ALIASES (map aliases_for: i for install, package and pack for cache) and Thor's HELP_MAPPINGS. Thor (lib/bundler/vendor/thor/lib/thor.rb) reads the first argument as the command: normalize_command_name takes a command or alias, or an unambiguous prefix of one (find_command_possibilities: bundle inst, bundle upd); a first argument that starts with - and is no alias is no command name (retrieve_command_name), and with no command name normalize_command_name runs default_command, which is the default_cli_command setting or install, with every argument parsed as its options: a bare bundle installs, and so does bundle --cooldown 0. The commands desc declares with hide: true (cli_help, install_or_cli_help, viz, inject) are Thor::HiddenCommand, which find_command_possibilities leaves out, so no prefix names them; a name that matches no command, alias or prefix is read with - as \_ (normalize_command_name: meth.to_s.tr("-", "\_")) and runs the command of exactly that name, a hidden one too: bundle install_or_cli_help and bundle install-or-cli-help run install ("Deprecated alias of install", invoke_other_command("install")). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/cli.rb)
- `extra.versionSelector`: The executables RubyGems writes for a gem (Gem::Installer#app_script_text) take a first argument \_VERSION\_ when Gem::Version.correct? accepts VERSION (ANCHORED_VERSION_PATTERN in lib/rubygems/version.rb), activate that version and drop the argument; for bundler they also set ENV["BUNDLER_VERSION"] to it, so bundle \_4.0.12\_ install runs Bundler 4.0.12 and does not switch to the version of BUNDLED WITH. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/lib/rubygems/installer.rb)
- `extra.rubygemsSource`: "At the top of the Gemfile, add a single line for the RubyGems source": source "https://rubygems.org" ("GLOBAL SOURCE"); bundle init writes the same line (lib/bundler/templates/Gemfile). A source call with a block (source "…" do … end) declares a source for the gems in the block only. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/gemfile.5.ronn)
- `extra.cooldownWithLockfile`: "Preserve per-source cooldown when converging sources from the lockfile" (#9601) under 4.0.14 / 2026-06-10. The test "applies per-source Gemfile cooldown on bundle update when a lockfile exists" (spec/install/cooldown_spec.rb) says: "Converging the Gemfile sources with the lockfile sources used to drop the per-source cooldown, so it only ever worked on a first resolve without a lockfile." SourceList#replace_rubygems_source carries remote_cooldowns over since then (lib/bundler/source_list.rb, missing at bundler-v4.0.13). The cooldown setting and --cooldown work from 4.0.13. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.cooldownSetting`: cooldown (BUNDLE_COOLDOWN): "Number of days a published gem version must age before bundler will resolve to it"; "The CLI flag and this setting apply uniformly to every source, including ones declared with their own cooldown: value." Bundler reads settings from the local config (\<project_root>/.bundle/config or $BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG/config), then the environment, then the global config (\~/.bundle/config); BUNDLE_IGNORE_CONFIG ignores the files. Remote#effective_cooldown takes the setting when it is set and the keyword of the source otherwise (lib/bundler/source/rubygems/remote.rb). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/bundle-config.1.ronn)
- `extra.cooldownSettingValues`: cooldown is one of NUMBER_KEYS, so Settings#converted_value reads its value with String#to_i: "7 days" is 7, and a value that does not start with a digit, the empty one included, is 0, which turns the cooldown off (the resolver skips 0 and less); "false" is read as false, which counts as unset, so the keyword of the source applies. Values are not checked when they are set (lib/bundler/settings/validator.rb has no rule for cooldown). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/settings.rb)
- `extra.lockedVersions`: Resolver#locked_by_lockfile?: "A version already written to the lockfile has been adopted, and cooldown only governs the adoption of new versions", except for the gems named on bundle update GEM or bundle lock --update GEM. bundle install with an existing Gemfile.lock installs the locked versions, a gem added to the Gemfile since then is resolved with the cooldown, and a frozen install reads the lockfile without resolving (the tests "bypasses cooldown when bundle install uses an existing lockfile", "applies per-source Gemfile cooldown to gems added after the lockfile was written" and "ignores cooldown and installs the locked version when frozen" in spec/install/cooldown_spec.rb). The blog post: "an existing Gemfile.lock is always honored as-is". [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/resolver.rb)
- `extra.missingTimestamp`: The cooldown "depends on the gem server providing a per-version created_at timestamp in the v2 compact-index format. Versions without that metadata - older gem servers, historical entries that predate the v2 cutover on rubygems.org, or private registries that still emit the v1 format - are treated as outside the cooldown window and remain resolvable." The test "cannot apply cooldown and installs the latest version" (spec/install/cooldown_spec.rb) shows the same for the dependency API. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/bundle-config.1.ronn)
- `extra.allTooNew`: Resolver#cooldown_hint adds "N versions excluded by the cooldown setting; pass \`--cooldown 0\` to bypass" to the error when the cooldown leaves no version that fits; Bundler stops instead of taking a newer version (test "surfaces a cooldown hint when bundle update filters every candidate"). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/resolver.rb)
- `extra.olderVersions`: Dsl#source of 4.0.12 reads only the type option of source and drops the others without a word, as does that of 2.7.2 (https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/bundler-v2.7.2/bundler/lib/bundler/dsl.rb), so a Gemfile with cooldown: works there and has no delay. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/bundler-v4.0.12/bundler/lib/bundler/dsl.rb)
- `extra.lockfileVersion`: Gemfile.lock ends with BUNDLED WITH and the version of the Bundler that wrote it (LockfileGenerator, LockfileParser::BUNDLED). bundle install installs that version and restarts with it, and the other commands restart with it when it is installed (SelfManager#install_locked_bundler_and_restart_with_it_if_needed and #restart_with_locked_bundler_if_needed), unless BUNDLER_VERSION is set or the version setting is system (its default is lockfile, bundle-config(1)). bundle update --bundler[=VERSION] changes the locked version ("With no argument, update to the latest released version", bundle-update(1)). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/self_manager.rb)
- `extra.resolveCommands`: The gem installs the executables bundle and bundler (s.executables in bundler.gemspec). bundle install, update, lock (bundle-lock(1)), add (which runs bundle install) and cache resolve the Gemfile and take --cooldown (cli.rb); bundle outdated only reads versions. Aliases, prefixes and a bare bundle are read as Bundler reads them (extra.cliCommands), and so is a first argument \_VERSION\_ (extra.versionSelector). [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/bundle-install.1.ronn)
- `extra.gemInstall`: gem install bundler -v 4.0.23 (or --version, Gem::VersionOption#add_version_option in lib/rubygems/version_option.rb) and gem install bundler:4.0.23 (Gem::Command#extract_gem_name_and_version) install that Bundler. The options are read with Gem::OptionParser, so the value may also be attached: -v4.0.23 and --version=4.0.23. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/lib/rubygems/command.rb)
- `extra.configLocal`: bundle config set --local writes \<project_root>/.bundle/config, which also holds machine paths such as path (bundle-config(1)); the .gitignore that bundle gem writes for a new gem ignores /.bundle/. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/templates/newgem/gitignore.tt)
- `extra.configCommand`: bundle config set [--local|--global] NAME VALUE (bundle-config(1)): set "defaults to setting local configuration if executing from within a local application, otherwise it will set global configuration"; --local writes \<project_root>/.bundle/config (or $BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG/config), --global \~/.bundle/config. CLI::Config#set joins the value words with spaces (value\_.unshift(value), then join(" ")), and the hidden base command still runs bundle config NAME VALUE (two arguments, or one with --local or --global) as set, with a deprecation warning. Settings#set_key stores the key as key_for gives it (lib/bundler/settings.rb: dots to \_\_, dashes to \_\_\_, upper case, BUNDLE\_ in front), so cooldown in any case is BUNDLE_COOLDOWN. Both files replace the cooldown: of every Gemfile source (extra.cooldownSetting), so a 0 written there turns the delay off for the later bundle commands on that machine. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/cli/config.rb)
- `extra.updateCommand`: --cooldown 0 disables the cooldown "for this run, overriding any per-source or global configuration. Combine with --conservative to minimize transitive churn when bypassing cooldown for an urgent update." [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/bundle-update.1.ronn)
- `extra.dependencySources`: Of the kinds of sources a policy names, a Gemfile can declare git sources (GIT, GITHUB and the other git sources) and path sources (PATH), with no setting that forbids them; it has no source for an archive URL or a local archive. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/v4.0.23/bundler/lib/bundler/man/gemfile.5.ronn)

### Renovate

- `cooldown.setting`: Formerly stabilityDays; old configs are migrated to "N days". Can be scoped with packageRules, vulnerabilityAlerts and update types. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: Searched in this order, and the first file that exists is the configuration (configFileNames in lib/config/app-strings.ts). The list is the same on every platform: detectConfigFile calls getConfigFileNames() without a platform, so a .gitlab/renovate.json counts in a GitHub repository and a .github/renovate.json on GitLab; only the validation of onboardingConfigFileName filters the names by platform (getPossibleConfigFileNames in lib/config/validation.ts). The "renovate" key in package.json still works but is deprecated. Shared presets (extends) can also set it. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/lib/workers/repository/init/merge.ts)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: Self-hosted CLI only; environment variable RENOVATE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage)
- `cooldown.unit`: For example "3 days" or "14 days". Since 42.19.5 "0 days" is treated like null. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: Earlier versions had the same feature as stabilityDays (first version not tracked). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases/tag/35.46.0)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless configured; the docs table shows no default. config:best-practices adds "3 days" for npm (see presets). Since 44.96.0 minimumReleaseAgeBuffer adds 30 minutes once a delay is set. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/lib/config/options/index.ts)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: No dedicated exclusion list. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/#how-do-i-opt-out-dependencies-from-minimum-release-age-checks)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: Glob and regex patterns since 38.0.0. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchpackagenames)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: The vulnerabilityAlerts defaults set minimumReleaseAge to null; a delay can still be set inside vulnerabilityAlerts. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/#what-happens-to-security-updates)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Renovate disables package manager scripts when it updates lockfiles; the Mend-hosted app never runs them. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#ignorescripts)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: The default; the self-hosted global allowScripts also defaults to false. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#ignorescripts)
- `extra.configLocation`: detectConfigFile looks for each name in configFiles (lib/config/app-strings.ts) in the file list of the repository, whose paths start at the repository root, so a renovate.json in a subdirectory is never read. The configuration options page (docs/usage/configuration-options.md at 44.198.2): "Any config you define applies to the whole repository (e.g. if you have a monorepo)" and "Renovate always uses the config from the repository's default branch". [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/workers/repository/init/merge.ts)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Values such as "3 days" or "1 hour", parsed by toMs (lib/util/pretty-time.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.minimumReleaseAgePresets`: config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which sets minimumReleaseAge "3 days" for the npm datasource (see presets). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/presets-security/#securityminimumreleaseagenpm)
- `extra.excludeRule`: The documented opt-out: a packageRules entry with matchPackageNames and minimumReleaseAge: null. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.securityUpdatesSetting`: The vulnerabilityAlerts default sets minimumReleaseAge to null, so security updates skip the delay unless a value is set there. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/lib/config/options/index.ts)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: matchPackageNames accepts globs (and regex) since 38.0.0. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchpackagenames)
- `extra.ruleDescription`: A human-readable description allowed inside any configuration object; depcurfew uses it to recognize the packageRules entry it manages. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#description)
- `extra.packageJsonConfig`: Deprecated: the configuration options page warns that support may be removed, and Renovate logs that using package.json is deprecated. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/lib/workers/repository/init/merge.ts)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Units shown in the docs: minimumReleaseAge=1 hour on this page and "3 days" in the configuration options. The value is parsed by toMs (lib/util/pretty-time.ts), whose tests also accept 1 day, 1 week and combined values. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.209.0/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.datasources`: Datasource ids for matchDatasources: npm packages come from the npm datasource and Python packages from pypi, whose release timestamp is the earliest upload_time of the version's files. Composer packages come from packagist, the datasource of the composer manager (static readonly id = 'packagist' in lib/modules/datasource/packagist/index.ts and supportedDatasources in lib/modules/manager/composer/index.ts at 44.199.2, read 2026-11-02). Ruby gems come from rubygems (static readonly id = 'rubygems' in lib/modules/datasource/rubygems/index.ts at 44.198.2, one of the supportedDatasources of the bundler manager), which has releaseTimestampSupport: "The release timestamp is determined from the \`created_at\` field in the results" (read 2026-11-03). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/pypi/)
- `extra.packagistReleaseTime`: The release timestamp of a Composer version is composerRelease['published-time'] ?? composerRelease.time: Packagist's publication date, the author-set time only when it is missing. The releaseTimestampNote of lib/modules/datasource/packagist/index.ts at the same tag still says "determined from the time field". [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.199.2/lib/modules/datasource/packagist/schema.ts)
- `extra.negativeMatch`: Patterns starting with ! are negative matches, and none of them may match; matchDatasources is matched this way (matchRegexOrGlobList in lib/util/package-rules/datasources.ts at 44.198.0), so ["!pypi"] covers every datasource but PyPI. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/string-pattern-matching/)
- `extra.packageRuleMatching`: A packageRules entry applies to a dependency when all of its matchers match. Within one matcher, at least one positive pattern must match when there are any, and no negative pattern (starting with !) may match, so a list of only negative patterns matches every name it does not exclude (docs/usage/string-pattern-matching.md and matchRegexOrGlobList in lib/util/string-match.ts). matchPackageNames, matchDepNames, matchDatasources and matchUpdateTypes all match this way; "\*" alone matches everything. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#packagerules)
- `extra.packageRulesOrder`: All packageRules are evaluated and later rules override options set by earlier ones; a matching rule overrides the top-level configuration ("Package rule config overrides any existing config", lib/util/package-rules/index.ts). Presets in extends are merged before the repository configuration, and packageRules is mergeable, so the rules of presets come first and the repository's rules after them, while a top-level option of the repository replaces the same option of a preset (resolveConfigPresets in lib/config/presets/index.ts and mergeChildConfig in lib/config/utils.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#packagerules)
- `extra.delayedUpdateTypes`: The update types that take minimumReleaseAge into account; digest and pinDigest only for some datasources, and pin, lockFileMaintenance, lockfileUpdate, rollback, bump and replacement not at all. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md#which-update-types-take-minimumreleaseage-into-account)
- `extra.internalPresets`: The built-in preset groups; a default preset is written :name or default:name. Other presets (github>, gitlab>, local>, npm packages and so on) are fetched from elsewhere. Among the built-in presets only the security:minimumReleaseAge\* presets set minimumReleaseAge, each in a packageRules entry with matchDatasources for its datasource, and config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm (security.preset.ts and config.preset.ts in the same directory). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/config/presets/internal/index.ts)
- `extra.pypiPresets`: Added in 44.8.0; config:best-practices does not include it (it includes only security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/presets-security/#securityminimumreleaseagepypi)
- `extra.pythonManagers`: pep621 updates pyproject.toml with uv.lock (there is no uv manager) or pdm.lock; poetry updates pyproject.toml with poetry.lock; pipenv updates the Pipfile with Pipfile.lock; pip_requirements updates requirements files. pip-compile is off by default (lib/modules/manager/pep621/readme.md and pipenv/index.ts at 44.198.1). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/pep621/)
- `extra.managers`: The Renovate manager that updates the packages of each tool, by its id in api.ts; github-actions updates the actions the workflows run. The npm manager reads package.json with package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml or yarn.lock (lockFileNames in npm/index.ts). bun and deno have managers of their own that take a package.json over from npm (supersedesManagers in bun/index.ts and deno/index.ts, applied by lib/workers/repository/extract/supersedes.ts), and poetry takes pyproject.toml over from pep621, which updates it for uv and PDM. composer updates composer.json (composer/index.ts), and bundler the Gemfile with Gemfile.lock (managerFilePatterns /(^|/)Gemfile$/ and lockFileNames in bundler/index.ts, so not gems.rb); bundler was read on 2026-11-03. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/modules/manager/api.ts)
- `extra.managerCategories`: getManagerConfig gives each dependency the categories its manager exports (categories in lib/modules/manager/\<id>/index.ts; the list of categories is lib/constants/category.ts), and matchCategories matches them. bundler exports the category ruby (read 2026-11-03). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/config/index.ts)
- `extra.botOnlyEcosystems`: The Renovate manager of each ecosystem depcurfew delays only through the bots (decision D-151), by its id in api.ts, with the datasource it gives the packages and its categories (categories in lib/modules/manager/\<id>/index.ts, all in lib/constants/category.ts): cargo updates Cargo.toml (managerFilePatterns, lockFileNames Cargo.lock) from the crate datasource (lib/modules/manager/cargo/schema.ts) in the rust category; gomod updates go.mod from the go datasource (line-parser.ts) in golang; maven updates pom.xml and gradle the .gradle(.kts) files, gradle.properties and the version catalogs in gradle/, both from the maven datasource, in java; nuget updates .csproj, .fsproj, .vbproj, .props and .targets files, dotnet-tools.json and global.json from the nuget datasource in dotnet. getManagerConfig (lib/config/index.ts) starts every manager from the whole configuration, so the top-level minimumReleaseAge applies to them as to the other managers. All four datasources have releaseTimestampSupport: crate takes pubtime of the crates.io index or created_at of the crates.io API, go the Time of the module proxy (or a later GitHub release or tag of a module on GitHub), maven the Last-Modified header, nuget the published date (index.ts of each datasource). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/modules/manager/api.ts)
- `extra.cratePresets`: security:minimumReleaseAgeCrate sets minimumReleaseAge "3 days" (with internalChecksFilter "strict") in a packageRules entry with matchDatasources ["crate"], and turns it off for lockFileMaintenance, replacement, pin, bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback updates of that datasource. Added in 44.5.0 ("presets: add security:minimumReleaseAgeCrate preset", https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases/tag/44.5.0); config:best-practices does not include it. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/config/presets/internal/security.preset.ts)
- `extra.managerMatching`: matchManagers matches the manager id of a dependency like matchRegexOrGlobList (case-insensitive globs, /regex/ and ! for "not"), a custom manager as custom.\<name>; matchCategories matches when any category of the dependency matches (anyMatchRegexOrGlobList in lib/util/package-rules/categories.ts). The configuration options page says matchCategories uses "any" logic and is applied after extraction (docs/usage/configuration-options.md). These two, matchPackageNames, matchDepNames, matchDatasources and matchUpdateTypes all have allowString in lib/config/options/index.ts, and massageConfig (lib/config/massage.ts) turns such a string into a list of one. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/util/package-rules/managers.ts)
- `extra.githubActions`: An action pinned to a ref that looks like a version (v4, v4.2.0, also as a comment after a commit SHA) is looked up in the github-tags datasource, which gives major, minor and patch updates; another ref (main, a feature tag) goes to github-digest, which gives digest updates only (readme.md in the same directory). getManagerConfig (lib/config/index.ts) starts every manager from the whole configuration, so the top-level minimumReleaseAge applies to github-actions as to the other managers; no built-in preset sets a delay for it (lib/config/presets/internal/security.preset.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/modules/manager/github-actions/extract.ts)
- `extra.actionsMatching`: matchFileNames matches the packageFile of a dependency, the path of the file from the repository root (and its lockFiles, which the github-actions manager does not set: "Deliberately no lockFiles" in lib/modules/manager/github-actions/extract.ts), like matchRegexOrGlobList; a glob goes to minimatch with { dot: true, nocase: true } (getRegexOrGlobPredicate in lib/util/string-match.ts), so \* stays within one directory and \*\* spans directories. matchFileNames takes no string for a list (no allowString in lib/config/options/index.ts); matchDepTypes does (allowString) and matches the depType like matchRegexOrGlobList (lib/util/package-rules/dep-types.ts). The github-actions manager gives the depType action to a repository action in a uses: field (actions/checkout@v4), and workflow, docker, container, service, github-runner and uses-with to the other things it updates (lib/modules/manager/github-actions/dep-types.ts, extract.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/util/package-rules/files.ts)
- `extra.actionsTimestamps`: github-tags reads committedDate of the commit a lightweight tag points to, or tagger.date of an annotated tag, and takes the publishedAt of a GitHub release of the same version when it is newer (lib/modules/datasource/github-tags/index.ts); github-digest takes the commit date (lib/modules/datasource/github-digest/index.ts). Both are dates from git that the person who makes the commit or the tag sets: the minimum release age page (docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md) says github-tags "uses the committedDate, which is separate from when it was pushed", and that a digest update of a tag moved to new commits ages against the original release date, so it may pass at once. Since 42.0.0 an update without a timestamp waits (missingTimestamp). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/util/github/graphql/query-adapters/tags-query-adapter.ts)
- `extra.passesDelayToManager`: Since 44.34.0 Renovate passes POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE (rounded up to whole days) to Poetry 2.4.0 and later. It does not pass the delay to uv or read exclude-newer. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)
- `extra.missingTimestamp`: minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour was added in 41.150.0; timestamp-optional still fails open. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases/tag/42.0.0)
- `extra.independentOfPackageManager`: Source code passes --before to npm only; pnpm, Yarn and Bun gates are not read. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)

### Dependabot

- `cooldown.setting`: Per updates entry: default-days, semver-major-days, semver-minor-days, semver-patch-days, include, exclude. The semver-\* keys apply only to SemVer ecosystems. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: On the default branch. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/about-the-dependabot-yml-file)
- `cooldown.unit`: Integer days; the allowed range is disputed (see dayRange). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: GA date on github.com; NuGet and Helm since 2025-07-29. [↗](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-01-dependabot-supports-configuration-of-a-minimum-package-age/)
- `cooldown.default`: Version updates wait 3 days even without a cooldown block (GHES from 3.23); default-days is also 3 when cooldown is set without it. [↗](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-14-dependabot-version-updates-introduce-default-package-cooldown/)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: Cooldown exists only for version updates. dependabot-core also passes a zero age to npm, pnpm and Yarn for security updates, overriding repository gates. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: insecure-external-code-execution: allow exists only for bundler, mix and pip; nothing allows npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun scripts. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#insecure-external-code-execution)
- `extra.configLocation`: "You must store this file in the .github directory of your repository in the default branch (typically main), at .github/dependabot.yml or .github/dependabot.yaml" (github/docs, content/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/about-the-dependabot-yml-file.md, read 2026-11-01), so a .github/dependabot.yml in a subdirectory is not read. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/about-the-dependabot-yml-file)
- `extra.directories`: Required in each updates entry: directory for one directory of manifests, directories for a list; "Define directories relative to the root of the repository for most package managers"; "The directories key supports globbing and the wildcard character \*. These features are not supported by the directory key." How a glob matches is not described further (github/docs, content/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference.md, read 2026-11-01). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#directories-or-directory)
- `extra.cooldownKeys`: Keys inside the cooldown block of an updates entry; the semver-\* keys override default-days for that kind of update. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: cooldown.exclude accepts \* wildcards. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.excludeMatching`: ReleaseCooldownOptions#excluded? at v0.402.0 skips the cooldown for a dependency when any exclude pattern matches its name with File.fnmatch?(pattern, dependency_name), and included? matches include the same way, both without flags. Without File::FNM_PATHNAME a \* matches / as well ("File.fnmatch('c\*t', 'c/a/b/t') #=> true" in the documentation of File.fnmatch, dir.rb of Ruby 3.4.7, https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_4_7/dir.rb), and without File::FNM_CASEFOLD case counts, so "\*/\*" matches every Composer package (vendor/name) and every scoped npm package. [↗](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/v0.402.0/common/lib/dependabot/package/release_cooldown_options.rb)
- `extra.cooldownInclude`: An include list in the cooldown block limits the cooldown to the dependencies it names (\* wildcards, up to 150 entries): the example applies the cooldown to requests, numpy and names starting with pandas or django, and to cover all dependencies one omits include or uses "\*". The other dependencies get no cooldown at all, not even the default 3 days: dependabot-core skips the cooldown for a dependency that the include list does not match (ReleaseCooldownOptions#included? with File.fnmatch? and CooldownCalculation.skip_cooldown? in common/lib/dependabot, commit 03892a3e8ee26d43eb96f31c5136c98a85d63b14). exclude wins over include. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates#setting-up-a-cooldown-period-for-dependency-updates)
- `extra.ecosystems`: The npm ecosystem covers npm, pnpm and Yarn; bun needs Bun 1.1.39 or later and deno needs Deno 2. pip covers pip, pip-compile, pipenv and Poetry (v2); uv has its own ecosystem (the table lists uv v0.11). composer covers Composer v2, bundler Bundler (the table lists v2; dependabot-core v0.403.0 also builds a helper with Bundler \~> 4.0, bundler/helpers/v4/build). Cooldown, including the semver-\* keys, is supported for all of them (the cooldown table of the same page lists Composer and Bundler with default and SemVer-bump days, read 2026-11-02 and, for Bundler, 2026-11-03). PDM is not listed: dependabot-core skips the dependencies of pyproject.toml when pdm.lock exists (python/lib/dependabot/python/file_parser/pyproject_files_parser.rb at v0.402.0). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#package-ecosystem)
- `extra.yamlAliases`: Dependabot::Config::File.parse loads dependabot.yml with YAML.safe_load(config, symbolize_names: true); Psych.safe_load takes aliases: false unless told otherwise and raises Psych::AliasesNotEnabled on an alias (\*name), so a file with one is not read. The issue that asks for aliases (https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/issues/1582, "YAML aliases", open and labelled Keep on 2026-11-02) quotes the error users get, "YAML aliases are not supported"; the pull request that would allow them (#9653) is open and not merged. The reference of dependabot.yml (dependabot-options-reference.md in github/docs) does not mention anchors or aliases. An anchor (&name) that no alias refers to changes nothing. [↗](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/v0.402.0/common/lib/dependabot/config/file.rb)
- `extra.yamlScalars`: Dependabot::Config::File.parse loads dependabot.yml with YAML.safe_load (dependabot-core v0.402.0, common/lib/dependabot/config/file.rb), which is Psych: Ruby 4.0.5 (.ruby-version) with psych 5.5.0 (Gemfile.lock of dependabot-core at v0.402.0). ScalarScanner#tokenize reads a plain scalar in this order: words, booleans (yes, no, on, off, true, false) and null; times and dates; .inf and .nan; :symbols; base 60 integers [-+]?[0-9\][0-9\_]\*(:[0-5]?[0-9]){1,2}, summed as part \* 60 \*\* (index - 2).abs, so 1:30 is 5400; floats with a dot; then INTEGER_LEGACY, the default without strict_integer: 0b binary, 0 followed by octal digits, decimal without a leading zero, 0x hex, each with \_ and , allowed, read with Integer(string.delete(',\_')), so 010 is 8, 1_0 and 1,0 are 10; anything else, 0o12 and 08 too, is a string. [↗](https://github.com/ruby/psych/blob/v5.5.0/lib/psych/scalar_scanner.rb)
- `extra.githubActions`: package-ecosystem github-actions updates the actions the workflows run: with directory / Dependabot "will search the /.github/workflows directory, as well as the action.yml/action.yaml file from the root directory". The cooldown table lists GitHub Actions with default-days supported and the semver-major-days, semver-minor-days and semver-patch-days keys not supported, and the default cooldown of 3 days covers version updates without a cooldown block (github/docs, content/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference.md, main on 2026-11-02). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.botOnlyEcosystems`: The package-ecosystem values of the ecosystems depcurfew delays only through the bots (decision D-151): cargo (Cargo v1), gomod (Go modules v1), maven, gradle and nuget (NuGet \<=6.12.0), from the package-ecosystem table of the same page. The cooldown table lists Cargo, Gomod (Go Modules), Gradle, Maven and NuGet with default-days and the SemVer-bump days (semver-major-days, semver-minor-days, semver-patch-days) supported, and the default cooldown of 3 days covers their version updates without a cooldown block (github/docs, content/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference.md, main on 2026-11-03). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.maximumDays`: The page says the number of cooldown days must be between 1 and 90; whether 0 is accepted is disputed (see dayRange). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates)
- `extra.composerReleaseTime`: For composer, the cooldown compares the release date with released_at, which parse_release takes from the time field of each version in the Packagist metadata: the date the package author sets, not published-time, the date Packagist received the version. Seen on 2026-11-02: intercom/intercom-php 5.0.2 has time 2026-01-30 and published-time 2026-04-30 (repo.packagist.org/p2/intercom/intercom-php.json). The updater runs Composer 2.10.3 (ARG COMPOSER_V2_VERSION in composer/Dockerfile at v0.402.0), which has no cooldown policy of its own. [↗](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/v0.402.0/composer/lib/dependabot/composer/package/registry_package.rb)
- `extra.composerContentHash`: post_process_lockfile calls replace_content_hash, which writes the hash get_content_hash returns: composer/helpers/v2/src/Hasher.php calls Locker::getContentHash of the composer/composer library the helper installs from its composer.lock (2.10.3 at v0.402.0). That method at 2.10.3 does not hash config.policy (src/Composer/Package/Locker.php at 2.10.3), while Composer 2.11 does, so with config.policy in composer.json every composer.lock Dependabot writes has a content-hash Composer 2.11 reads as out of date: composer install warns and composer validate fails until composer update --lock. [↗](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/v0.402.0/composer/lib/dependabot/composer/file_updater/lockfile_updater.rb)

### Environment

- `botOnlyEcosystems.cargo.project`: "Cargo.toml is about describing your dependencies in a broad sense" (the manifest) and "Cargo.lock contains exact information about your dependencies" (the Cargo book of Cargo 1.99, guide/cargo-toml-vs-cargo-lock.md). [↗](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/rust-1.99.0/doc/book/src/guide/cargo-toml-vs-cargo-lock.md)
- `botOnlyEcosystems.gomod.project`: The Go Modules Reference (go.dev/ref/mod): "A module is defined by a UTF-8 encoded text file named go.mod in its root directory" and "A module may have a text file named go.sum in its root directory, alongside its go.mod file" with the hashes of its dependencies (read on 2026-11-03). [↗](https://github.com/golang/website/blob/master/_content/ref/mod.md)
- `botOnlyEcosystems.maven.project`: Introduction to the POM: "A Project Object Model or POM is the fundamental unit of work in Maven. It is an XML file that contains information about the project", with the project dependencies; "When executing a task or goal, Maven looks for the POM in the current directory", and the examples name it pom.xml, also in modules (my-module/pom.xml). [↗](https://github.com/apache/maven-site/blob/master/content/markdown/guides/introduction/introduction-to-the-pom.md)
- `botOnlyEcosystems.gradle.project`: The Gradle 9.8.2 user guide shows a project with settings.gradle(.kts) in the root directory ("lets Gradle know about the structure of the build") and build.gradle(.kts) in each project, "declaring dependencies and applying plugins"; dependencies_intermediate.adoc in the same directory recommends a version catalog in gradle/libs.versions.toml for the dependency versions. [↗](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.2/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/gradle_directories_intermediate.adoc)
- `botOnlyEcosystems.nuget.project`: PackageReference items "specify NuGet package dependencies directly within project files, as opposed to having a separate packages.config file" (packages.config: reference/packages-config.md); Central Package Management keeps the versions in a Directory.Packages.props "at the root of your repository" (consume-packages/Central-Package-Management.md). Project files have extensions "like .csproj for C# projects and .fsproj for F# projects", and dependencies are referenced in "the project file (.csproj or .vbproj)" (docs/core/project-sdk/overview.md and docs/core/tools/dotnet-restore.md in dotnet/docs). NuGet reads nuget.config, NuGet.config and NuGet.Config, in this order (OrderedSettingsFileNames in src/nuget-client/src/NuGet.Core/NuGet.Configuration/Settings/Settings.cs at the v10.0.403 tag of dotnet/dotnet). [↗](https://github.com/NuGet/docs.microsoft.com-nuget/blob/main/docs/consume-packages/Package-References-in-Project-Files.md)
- `corepack.packageManagerField`: Format name@x.y.z, optionally followed by +\<hash algorithm>.\<hash>; a URL to a .js or .tgz file is also allowed. setup-bun also reads bun@x from this key. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/README.md)
- `corepack.devEnginesSince`: Limited support at first; since 0.36.0 Corepack uses the devEngines.packageManager range when packageManager is missing. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- `corepack.envFileSince`: Corepack reads COREPACK\_\* keys from .corepack.env; since 0.36.0 only the closest file. COREPACK_ENV_FILE=0 turns it off. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- `corepack.bundledWithNode`: Node.js 25.0.0 stopped distributing Corepack; the Corepack README says it ships with Node.js from 14.19.0 up to (but not including) 25.0.0. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V25.md)
- `corepack.package`: Its published bin field (publishConfig.bin) declares yarn (./dist/yarn.js), yarnpkg, pnpm and pnpx next to corepack. corepack enable links them from the folder of the corepack executable (a relative symlink to dist/\<name>.js on Linux and macOS, a cmd-shim on Windows; sources/commands/Enable.ts), so the package.json behind a yarn or pnpm shim is Corepack's, which says nothing about the version the shim runs. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/package.json)
- `corepack.toolPackages`: The npm packages Corepack installs each package manager from: npm; pnpm; yarn below 2.0.0 (Yarn Classic) and, with COREPACK_NPM_REGISTRY, @yarnpkg/cli-dist for Yarn 2 and later ("npmRegistry": { "package": "@yarnpkg/cli-dist", "bin": "bin/yarn.js" }). npm i -g @yarnpkg/cli-dist installs the same package, whose package.json declares bin yarn and carries the Yarn version (observed for 4.18.1). [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/config.json)
- `corepack.enableNpm`: corepack enable [... name] creates shims for the package managers it is given, or for all of them without parameters: "Note that the npm shims will not be installed unless explicitly requested, as npm is currently distributed with Node.js through other means". So corepack enable npm makes npm the version Corepack picks (packageManager), while a bare corepack enable leaves the bundled npm. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/README.md)
- `corepack.manualInstall`: How to Install: "Corepack is distributed with Node.js from version 14.19.0 up to (but not including) 25.0.0. Run \`corepack enable\` to install the required Yarn and pnpm binaries on your path." Manual Installs, "Install Corepack using npm": "npm install -g corepack". The Node.js 25.0.0 changelog lists "build: stop distributing Corepack" (#57617) among its semver-major commits (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V25.md), and the node images of 25 and later extract the release tarball unchanged (docker.nodeImage), so they have no Corepack either. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/v0.36.0/README.md)
- `installScriptPackages.esbuild`: npm/esbuild/package.json at v0.28.2 declares "postinstall": "node install.js" and one optionalDependencies entry per platform (@esbuild/linux-x64 and the others, version 0.28.2). generateBinPath in lib/npm/node-platform.ts, which the JavaScript API and bin/esbuild run, first resolves the binary from that optional package ("First check for the binary package from our optionalDependencies"), so esbuild works without its install script. lib/npm/node-install.ts (the install script) only replaces bin/esbuild with the binary ("This optimization also doesn't apply when npm's --ignore-scripts flag is used since in that case this install script will not be run"; not on Windows, with Yarn or WASM), checks the version of the binary, and downloads the platform package when it is missing ("This can happen if you use the --no-optional flag"). Without both, esbuild fails: "maybe someone installed esbuild with both the --no-optional and the --ignore-scripts flags. The fix for this is to just not do that", with the error "make sure that you don't specify the --no-optional or --omit=optional flags". [↗](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/v0.28.2/lib/npm/node-platform.ts)
- `installScriptPackages.fsevents`: The package.json of fsevents 2.3.3 declares no install script and lists "files": ["fsevents.d.ts", "fsevents.js", "fsevents.node"], so the published package contains the built module that fsevents.js loads (require("./fsevents.node")); the published tarball holds exactly LICENSE, README.md, package.json, fsevents.js, fsevents.d.ts and fsevents.node (listed on 2026-11-02, nothing run). The repository has a binding.gyp at that tag, and npm adds an install script to such a package when it is published: "If there is a binding.gyp file in the root of your package and you haven't defined your own install or preinstall scripts, npm will default the install command to compile using node-gyp via node-gyp rebuild" (https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/using-npm/scripts.md). That is the install: node-gyp rebuild of the registry metadata and the hasInstallScript of lockfiles; the tarball has no binding.gyp to build from. [↗](https://github.com/fsevents/fsevents/blob/v2.3.3/package.json)
- `installScriptPackages.lefthook`: postinstall.js runs the lefthook executable with install in INIT_CWD (the directory the install was started in), and does nothing when CI is set and LEFTHOOK is not ("if (isEnabled(process.env.CI) && !isEnabled(process.env.LEFTHOOK)) return"). get-exe.js resolves the executable from lefthook-\<os>-\<arch>/bin/lefthook, one of the optionalDependencies of packaging/registries/npm/lefthook/package.json (version 2.2.2), whose only script is "postinstall": "node postinstall.js". docs/usage/commands/install.md: lefthook install "Installs configured hooks to Git hooks"; "NPM package lefthook installs the hooks in a postinstall script automatically. For projects not using NPM package run lefthook install after cloning the repo." and "Reinstall is not required when you modify lefthook.yml, the configuration file is read every time a git hook is run." docs/usage/envs/LEFTHOOK.md: "When using NPM package lefthook in CI, and your CI sets CI=true automatically, use LEFTHOOK=1 or LEFTHOOK=true to install hooks in the postinstall script", so by default no hooks are installed in CI. postinstall.js catches every error and does not look at the exit code of lefthook install, so it never fails the install. The legacy package @evilmartians/lefthook-installer fetches the executable when it is installed (docs/installation/node.md), so its script is needed; it is not this entry. [↗](https://github.com/evilmartians/lefthook/blob/v2.2.2/packaging/registries/npm/lefthook/postinstall.js)
- `node.bundledNpm`: The npm field of every release in index.json (fetched on 2026-11-01, sha256 6b27fe5766e87929d16ccdde05c516cbdd12200eab62b28d4b2f31d34e21481a), as the first release of each line that bundles each npm version; latest is the newest release of the line that day. Lines are the major version from 4 on and the minor version before (0.6 to 0.12, as Node.js numbered them then). The bundled npm never goes down within a line. Releases before 0.6.3 (0.1.14 to 0.5.10 and 0.6.0 to 0.6.2) have no npm field: they came without npm. Every release before 18.0.0 bundles npm 8.19.4 or earlier (16.20.2 has npm 8.19.4), so none of them has min-release-age, allowScripts or strict-allow-scripts. 27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0 (npm 12.1.0) is a prerelease and left out: no release bundles npm 12 yet, Node.js 22 stays on npm 10.9.x, 24 reaches npm 11.10 or later only from 24.14.1 (npm 11.10.x was skipped) and 25 ends at npm 11.12.1. [↗](https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json)
- `node.releaseSchedule`: start, lts and end of each line from 4 on, codenames in lower case as nvm and the node image tags write them. After end a line gets no more releases, security fixes included; the README says "Production applications should only use Active LTS or Maintenance LTS releases". From Node.js 27 every line first goes through an alpha phase (27 has "alpha": "2026-10-28" and no codename yet) and every line becomes LTS. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/Release/blob/c3e8696312969c95643cb52f05f124c161db87b2/schedule.json)
- `node.nvmrc`: The file must contain precisely one version followed by a newline; # starts a comment, and comments, blank lines and leading and trailing white space are ignored. node is the latest version and stable an alias for it; lts/\* is the latest LTS and lts/\<codename> the LTS releases of that line; the file may hold "any other string that nvm understands". nvm use looks for the file from the current directory upwards. lts/-n is not in the README but in nvm.sh at the same commit (https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/5e38bc0caed342356ffd26eb21e0e9b995ac228b/nvm.sh, read 2026-11-01): nvm_normalize_lts, which nvm_alias calls for every alias (so also for the version of .nvmrc), matches "lts/-[123456789] | lts/-[123456789\][0123456789]\*", takes N from after the -, adds 1 and picks the N-th last entry of the lts alias directory, whose entries are the LTS codenames (alphabetical, which is release order) after \*; so lts/-1 is the LTS line before the newest one, as in setup-node. When nothing matches it says "That many LTS releases do not exist yet." [↗](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/5e38bc0caed342356ffd26eb21e0e9b995ac228b/README.md)
- `node.nodeVersionFile`: nodenv uses the version in .node-version of the project directory. fnm reads .node-version and .nvmrc and writes the file with node --version, so a leading v occurs (github.com/Schniz/fnm/blob/07f13237ae208f531f8ea88d4cfde3160c22f99a/README.md); setup-node reads it through node-version-file. [↗](https://github.com/nodenv/nodenv/blob/5083e9819756c1a127a626a874703349f4ddb2e4/README.md)
- `node.engines`: engines.node is the range of Node.js versions the package works on. Unless engine-strict is set, it is advisory and only produces warnings when the package is installed as a dependency; it does not choose the Node.js that runs. setup-node reads it from package.json through node-version-file when volta.node and devEngines.runtime are missing, and picks the newest version that matches. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md#engines)
- `node.inheritedVersionFiles`: nvm: "nvm use et. al. will traverse directory structure upwards from the current directory looking for the .nvmrc file". nodenv: find_local_version_file in libexec/nodenv-version-file checks the directory for .node-version and then each parent up to the root (https://github.com/nodenv/nodenv/blob/5083e9819756c1a127a626a874703349f4ddb2e4/libexec/nodenv-version-file). asdf: the tool versions a .tool-versions file declares "will be used in that directory and any subdirectories" (https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/blob/master/docs/manage/configuration.md). Volta is not one of them: for_dir in crates/volta-core/src/project/mod.rs "will search ancestors to find a package.json and use that as the root of the project" and reads a parent package.json only through extends (https://github.com/volta-cli/volta/blob/main/crates/volta-core/src/project/mod.rs), so the volta key of the root package.json does not reach a project with a package.json of its own. [↗](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/5e38bc0caed342356ffd26eb21e0e9b995ac228b/README.md)
- `docker.imageReference`: splitDockerDomain canonicalizes ubuntu and docker.io/ubuntu as docker.io/library/ubuntu, and the legacy domain index.docker.io as docker.io. A reference without a tag means latest (docs/reference/commandline/image_tag.md in github.com/docker/cli at 8c8a77521af82b08bf3499cafb4c0e2e7b024936: "If the namespace is omitted, Docker defaults to library, the namespace reserved for Docker Official Images"). registry-1.docker.io is Docker Hub's registry itself: "DefaultRegistryHost is the hostname for the default (Docker Hub) registry used for pushing and pulling images", DefaultRegistryHost = "registry-1.docker.io" (https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9aa9edfa787e08bb2da31694cd8a402876f32232/daemon/pkg/registry/config.go), so registry-1.docker.io/library/node is the same official image. [↗](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/9aa9edfa787e08bb2da31694cd8a402876f32232/vendor/github.com/distribution/reference/normalize.go)
- `docker.syntax`: Instructions are not case-sensitive. A line that begins with # is a comment unless it is a parser directive; comment lines are removed also inside a continued instruction. Parser directives (syntax, escape, check; keys not case-sensitive) must come first: after a comment, an empty line or an instruction none is read. The escape character (\\ by default, or \`) at the end of a line continues the instruction; escaping is not performed in RUN except at the end of a line. ARG is the only instruction allowed before FROM, and FROM reads ARGs declared before the first FROM ($VAR, ${VAR}, ${VAR:-word}, ${VAR-word}, ${VAR:+word}, ${VAR+word}); --build-arg can change them. FROM [--platform=\<platform>] \<image>[:\<tag>\][@\<digest>] [AS \<name>]; a later FROM \<name> starts from that stage. A here-document (RUN \<\<EOF) makes the following lines part of the instruction, up to the line with only the delimiter. Only RUN, COPY and ADD in shell form take here-documents, and only a whole word starts one: the parser splits the line into words with quotes kept (shlex.RawQuotes) and matches each word against ^(\\d\*)\<\<(-?)\\s\*([^\<]\*)$, so a quoted "a \<\<b" starts none (heredocsFromLine and reHeredoc in frontend/dockerfile/parser/parser.go at the same commit). [↗](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/c1cfdbd30b79b4a4908cdccc3c0f9849c30e34e5/frontend/dockerfile/docs/reference.md)
- `docker.copySources`: COPY and ADD without --from: "When copying source files from the build context, paths are interpreted as relative to the root of the context. Specifying a source path with a leading slash or one that navigates outside the build context, such as COPY ../something /something, automatically removes any parent directory navigation (../). Trailing slashes in the source path are also disregarded, making COPY something/ /something equivalent to COPY something /something." The ADD section says the same about ADD ../something. So /frontend/x, ../frontend/x and frontend/x are the same file, and frontend/.. is the root of the context. [↗](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/c1cfdbd30b79b4a4908cdccc3c0f9849c30e34e5/frontend/dockerfile/docs/reference.md#copying-from-the-build-context)
- `docker.environment`: ENV \<key>=\<value> [\<key>=\<value>...]: "This value will be in the environment for all subsequent instructions in the build stage", and "A stage inherits any environment variables that were set using ENV by its parent stage or any ancestor". "Like command line parsing, quotes and backslashes can be used to include spaces within values". The alternative "ENV \<key> \<value>, omitting the =" sets one variable, and is discouraged. RUN commands see these variables, and ENV wins over an ARG of the same name. [↗](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/c1cfdbd30b79b4a4908cdccc3c0f9849c30e34e5/frontend/dockerfile/docs/reference.md#env)
- `docker.buildArguments`: ARG \<name>[=\<default value>]: the variable "is also passed to all subsequent RUN instructions as a build-time environment variable"; "If an ARG instruction has a default value and if there is no value passed at build-time, the builder uses the default" (--build-arg can give another). "An ARG variable declared within a build stage is automatically inherited by other stages based on that stage. Unrelated build stages do not have access to the variable." "An ARG declared before a FROM is outside of a build stage, so it can't be used in any instruction after a FROM. To use the default value of an ARG declared before the first FROM use an ARG instruction without a value inside of a build stage." "Environment variables defined using the ENV instruction always override an ARG instruction of the same name." (Using ARG variables; Impact on build caching: "all RUN instructions following an ARG instruction use the ARG variable implicitly (as an environment variable)".) [↗](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/blob/c1cfdbd30b79b4a4908cdccc3c0f9849c30e34e5/frontend/dockerfile/docs/reference.md#arg)
- `docker.dockerfileNames`: "The default filename to use for a Dockerfile is Dockerfile, without a file extension." "A common convention is to name these \<something>.Dockerfile", passed with --file. [↗](https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/53581df94e05ad4116a8d31e47ea098289fa5498/content/manuals/build/concepts/dockerfile.md)
- `docker.containerfile`: "A Containerfile uses the same syntax as a Dockerfile internally"; Buildah and Podman read Containerfile or Dockerfile. Docker does not read Containerfile by default. [↗](https://github.com/containers/buildah/blob/14d624b398e05a07deecf29d50a44a149785cc20/docs/buildah-build.1.md)
- `docker.nodeImage`: The image downloads the official tarball of the release and extracts it unchanged; its only npm command is npm --version, and docs/BestPractices.md tells users to add RUN npm install --global npm@\<version> to change npm. So node:\<version> has exactly the npm that release bundles. The Alpine images extract the -musl tarball or build from source. Tags (stackbrew.js): X.Y.Z, X.Y, X and \<codename>, each also with -\<variant>, and -alpine and -slim for the default variants; the variants are those of versions.json, plus alpine and slim. Yarn 1 is in the images up to Node.js 25. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/blob/14b1d124e21d312c46b30db98985ab7e58a89594/Dockerfile-debian.template)
- `docker.pythonImage`: "our policy is now to use the pip version that is installed during the Python build (which is the version bundled in ensurepip), and to not support overriding it": Dockerfile-linux.template configures CPython --with-ensurepip and installs no other pip (only setuptools and wheel for 3.11). So python:\<version> has the pip that CPython release bundles. Images built before 2024-09-07 installed pip with get-pip.py, at the version ensurepip had. Tags (generate-stackbrew-library.sh): X.Y.Z and X.Y, each with -\<variant>; -slim and -alpine mean the default suite. [↗](https://github.com/docker-library/python/blob/f4c67ece208dead594e43628d22e3c6027dd97ab/versions.sh)
- `devEngines`: Each entry is an object or a list of objects with name (required), version and onFail (warn, error by default, or ignore). Corepack and the setup actions read it too. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md#devengines)
- `devEnginesSince`: npm version that introduced devEngines. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v10.9.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- `volta.manifest`: Also extends: a path to another JSON file with a volta key. pnpm support is experimental and needs VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1. [↗](https://github.com/volta-cli/volta/blob/v2.0.2/crates/volta-core/src/project/serial.rs)
- `volta.maintained`: The README says Volta is unmaintained and recommends migrating to mise. [↗](https://github.com/volta-cli/volta/blob/5eedd5fb2f682baceb47a242289111fcd79435a5/README.md)
- `asdf.toolVersionsFile`: One tool per line followed by one or more versions separated by spaces (fallbacks); # starts a comment. [↗](https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/blob/v0.20.2/docs/manage/configuration.md)
- `asdf.plugins`: Short names in the asdf plugin index; there is no plugin named node. python, uv and poetry checked on 2026-10-30 (danhper/asdf-python, asdf-community/asdf-uv, asdf-community/asdf-poetry). [↗](https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-plugins/tree/master/plugins)
- `githubActions.jobId`: Read from the page source in github/docs (data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-id.md, main on 2026-11-02): "You must replace \<job_id> with a string that is unique to the jobs object. The \<job_id> must start with a letter or \_ and contain only alphanumeric characters, -, or \_." The runner checks names the same way with ASCII letters and digits (NameValidation.IsValid in src/Sdk/DTPipelines/Pipelines/Validation/NameValidation.cs of actions/runner, main on 2026-11-02: a-z, A-Z, \_ anywhere, digits and, with hyphens allowed, - after the first character). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_id)
- `githubActions.setupNode`: Current major v7. node-version-file reads package.json, .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions or mise.toml; node-version wins when both are set. [↗](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/v7.1.0/action.yml)
- `githubActions.setupNodeVersions`: Tag v7.1.0. node-version takes semver (22, 24.8.0, >=10.15.0, 12.x), the NVM LTS syntax (lts/jod, lts/\*, lts/-n) and latest, current, node or \* for the latest release. A matching version in the runner's tool cache is used first, so a major version such as 24 may give an older release of the line unless check-latest is set. [↗](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1/README.md)
- `githubActions.setupNodeVersionFile`: node-version-file accepts .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions, mise.toml or package.json, relative to GITHUB_WORKSPACE. In package.json it checks volta.node, then the devEngines.runtime entry named node, then engines.node, then volta.extends. getNodeVersionFromFile in src/util.ts tries JSON, then TOML tools.node, then the first line that matches the pattern, then the whole text trimmed. [↗](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1/docs/advanced-usage.md)
- `githubActions.jobContainer`: Read from the page source in github/docs (data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-running-jobs-in-a-container.md and section-running-jobs-in-a-container-image.md, main on 2026-11-01): "Use jobs.\<job_id>.container to create a container to run any steps in a job that don't already specify a container"; "If you do not set a container, all steps will run directly on the host specified by runs-on"; "When you only specify a container image, you can omit the image keyword" (container: node:18); jobs.\<job_id>.container.image is "the Docker image to use as the container to run the action", and container.env sets variables in the container. So the run steps of such a job use the Node.js and npm of that image, until a setup step installs another. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobscontainer)
- `githubActions.environmentKeys`: Read from the page source in github/docs (content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax.md and data/reusables/repositories/actions-env-var-note.md, main on 2026-11-01): env is "A map of variables that are available to the steps of all jobs in the workflow", jobs.\<job_id>.env "A map of variables that are available to all steps in the job", and jobs.\<job_id>.steps[\*].env "Sets variables for steps to use in the runner environment"; for the same name GitHub "uses the most specific variable": the step's over the job's over the workflow's. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#env)
